items.title: Gastronomy as a catalyst for the circular economy in tourism: a multi-case analysis of UNESCO Creative Cities in Brazil
items.abstract: A economia circular (EC), aplicada aos sistemas alimentares, posiciona a gastronomia como um vetor estratégico. No turismo, essa abordagem valoriza produtos locais, reduz desperdícios e mitiga emissões de carbono. Nesse contexto, o artigo tem como objetivo analisar de que forma os princípios da EC podem ser integrados aos sistemas alimentares no contexto do turismo gastronômico, visando à promoção do turismo regenerativo por meio da valorização da cultura alimentar, dos produtos locais e da redução do desperdício. A pesquisa adotou a metassíntese como procedimento metodológico, caracterizada como um estudo qualitativo voltado à análise e à interpretação integradas de achados provenientes de pesquisas qualitativas sobre um tema comum. Alinhada ao conhecimento contemporâneo sobre EC, sistemas alimentares e turismo sustentável, a pesquisa também contemplou a análise das Cidades Criativas da Gastronomia da UNESCO no Brasil: Belém, Florianópolis, Belo Horizonte e Paraty. Os resultados indicam que a gastronomia é um caminho para a transição rumo a sistemas alimentares circulares, ao fortalecer circuitos curtos de comercialização, estimular a agricultura familiar e agroecológica, valorizar a sociobiodiversidade e fomentar práticas de prevenção e reaproveitamento de resíduos alimentares. Apesar dos desafios relacionados à governança, à infraestrutura e à capacitação profissional, as cidades analisadas demonstram elevado potencial transformador, funcionando como laboratórios vivos de inovação territorial. Conclui-se que a consolidação de sistemas alimentares circulares no turismo depende da articulação entre políticas públicas integradas, da cooperação entre produtores, chefs e gestores de destinos e do reconhecimento da gastronomia como elemento central para o desenvolvimento sustentável e de baixo carbono.

items.title: CONSTRUÇÃO DE UMA CIDADANIA TERRITORIAL PARTICIPATIVA: A IMPLEMENTAÇÃO DO “PROJETO NÓS PROPOMOS” EM TIMOR-LESTE
items.abstract: This article analyses the implementation of the "We propose! Citizenship and Innovation in Geographic Education" in a 12th grade Geography class at the Centro de Aprendizagem e Formação Escolar - CAFE, Suai, municipality of Cova Lima, Timor-Leste, 2025. The initiative aimed to promote geographic education and active citizenship, articulating school knowledge with local territorial challenges. The project involved 27 students and four teachers who developed six research projects on local territorial issues, culminating in the submission of projects in the form of powerpoint, poster and photography and participation in the National Congress of the We Propose Project! carried out by the Institute of Geography and Spatial Planning (IGOT), University of Lisbon, on May 8, 2025. The methodology was based on Project-based learning s and problem-based learning, encoyraging territorial observation, data collection and formulation of Community intervention proposals. The results highlight the potential of school Geography in promoting active territorial citizenship and in articulating knowledge with social transformation.

items.title: Acontecimientos traumáticos severos en la industria mexicana de la construcción: pertinencia normativa y factores territoriales
authors: Scott Michel Martin Da Gama Darby
items.abstract: This article analyzes the presence of severe traumatic events (STE) in the Mexican construction industry in accordance with NOM‑035‑STPS‑2018, integrating the perspective of Sustainable Development Goal 8 (SDG‑8) and the national regulatory framework. It examines the influence of nearby urban and non‑urban territories as factors associated with the violent component of STE reported by workers, following the methodology suggested by the NOM. Findings provide partial evidence suggesting that exposure to external threads to the workplace may increase the likelihood of violent STE. It is concluded that future updates to NOM‑035‑STPS‑2018 should clarify the definition of “hazards surrounding the workplace” to strengthen its relevance in high‑risk industries.

items.title: The Geography of Circular Transition: Regional Ecosystems, Territorial Governance, and Local Resource Efficiency
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.abstract: Circular economy policies increasingly position cities and regions as important sites for reorganizing resource use, yet the conditions under which territorial coordination contributes to sustainable outcomes remain insufficiently specified. This article presents a critical integrative synthesis examining how regional ecosystems, territorial governance, and measurement practices shape circular transitions. Drawing on perspectives from economic geography, industrial ecology, urban governance, and political economy, it develops a framework distinguishing implementation feasibility, governance direction, and environmental and distributive performance. The analysis indicates that geographical proximity facilitates circular exchange only when supported by compatible material streams, knowledge, infrastructure, and credible organizational relationships. Governance structures influence which circular pathways are prioritized, how responsibilities are distributed across scales, and whether existing capabilities, including informal recovery and repair, are incorporated or displaced. Material-flow, footprint, and life-cycle approaches further demonstrate that increases in recycling or circular employment do not necessarily generate absolute reductions in resource use. Three conditional propositions are developed: proximity requires complementary coordination; governance should prioritize outcomes rather than activity expansion; and local value retention represents developmental progress only when benefits are broadly distributed and environmental burdens are not displaced elsewhere. Comparative evidence across diverse contexts indicates the importance of institutional adaptation rather than uniform policy transfer. Effective territorial strategies therefore require integrated approaches to prevention, stock stewardship, accountable intermediation, inclusive market formation, and linked environmental and social evaluation.

items.title: Mechanisms for Building and Measuring Territorial Resilience: An Integrated Approach
items.venue: Journal of Urban Planning and Development
items.abstract: This article explores the foundations, mechanisms, and evaluation methods of territorial resilience in the context of disaster management. It highlights the importance of a systemic and multidimensional approach, integrating social, economic, environmental, and political factors. Key resilience-building processes include risk identification, preparedness, response, and postdisaster recovery. To assess resilience, both quantitative indicators and participatory methods are considered essential, offering complementary insights. This study underscores the need for integrated strategies and robust measurement tools to enhance territorial capacity to anticipate, absorb, adapt to, and recover from disasters, while guiding informed and sustainable decision-making.

items.title: El espacio Atlántico/Caribe guatemalteco: una construcción histórica y territorial liberal 1871-1959
items.venue: Cuadernos Inter c a mbio sobre Centroamérica y el Caribe
items.abstract: The central motivation of this essay lies in explaining the way in which the representation of the Caribbean territory of Guatemala was constructed since 1871. This orientation entails questioning the way in which the official denominated this space, which implies inquiring about the discursive, ideological and politician to name it "Atlantic". This refers to reviewing the trends in urban settlement movements and the construction of communication routes since colonial times. Underlying the thesis that the aforementioned denomination obeys a certainty on the part of liberal intellectuals to denominate the Caribbean space in the aforementioned way, considering that the waters bathe it constitute a common space with Western Europe, a civilizing paradigm. The reproduction of this appreciation takes place with the persistence of an exclusive discourse that led to the assumption of the region as a "window" towards Europe, ignoring the immediate context.

items.title: Spatial Differentiation and Built-Environment Correlates of Street-Block Vitality in Baoding, China
items.abstract: The spatial differentiation of street-block vitality and its built-environment correlates provide an empirical basis for implementing refined street-block governance in the context of the renewal of existing urban areas. Based on the human–environment relationship theory, this study constructs an analytical framework of “built environment condition–street-block vitality response” and establishes a built environment indicator system based on a five-dimensional (5D) framework encompassing density, diversity, design, destination accessibility, and distance to transit. Empirically, street-block vitality is measured by the block-level average heat value derived from Baidu Huiyan data, representing the relative intensity of population activity within each street block. By integrating objective data—such as point-of-interest (POI) data and road networks—with residents’ subjective perceptions, this study employs spatial autocorrelation analysis, hot spot analysis, and multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) models to identify the spatial patterns of street-block vitality in Baoding during the observation week of 8–14 April 2024 and their local associations with built environment factors. Model performance was evaluated through model comparison, sensitivity analysis, and spatial holdout validation. The results indicated that street-block vitality exhibited significant spatial clustering. High–high clusters were primarily distributed in urban development zones and their adjacent areas in the central-eastern, northeastern, and southwestern parts of the city, whereas low–low clusters were mainly concentrated in ecological protection and ecological control zones in the western, northwestern, and northern parts of the city. The density of scenic facilities (Den_sce), facility-density principal component (PC_FAC), road network density (Den_road), and distance to the nearest public transit stop (Dist_transit) generally showed a positive association with street-block vi

items.title: Digital Entrepreneurship and Territorial Bricolage: The Mechanisms Underlying the Construction of a Smart Territory in Dakhla-Oued Eddahab
items.venue: Revue Internationale des Sciences de Gestion
items.abstract: In peripheral territories with still limited digital resources, the emergence of innovative entrepreneurial practices raises questions about the concrete mechanisms through which digital technology contributes to building a smart territory. This is the case of the Dakhla-Oued Eddahab region, engaged in a digital transformation dynamic driven by national strategies and the Morocco Digital 2030 vision, yet where entrepreneurs must navigate significant territorial constraints. This research aims to understand how entrepreneurs mobilize territorial bricolage to turn these constraints into levers for building a smart territory in Dakhla-Oued Eddahab. The study adopts an interpretivist qualitative stance based on a single case study. Twenty semi-structured interviews were conducted with stakeholders of the regional ecosystem and analyzed through a reflexive thematic analysis assisted by Nvivo12, following an abductive approach. The findings show that the contribution of digital entrepreneurship to smart territory construction rests on the interaction between digital infrastructure, territorial governance, entrepreneurial ecosystem dynamics, and entrepreneurs' adaptive capabilities. They further reveal an emerging mechanism, territorial digital entrepreneurial bricolage, through which entrepreneurs creatively mobilize locally available resources to overcome structural constraints. This mechanism enriches the theoretical model and opens avenues for other comparable peripheral territories.

items.title: Construction Path for Dual-Use Public Infrastructure within the Territorial Space Planning System
items.abstract: In the context of advancing urban resilience and modernizing the national governance system, dual-use public infrastructure has emerged as a pivotal spatial carrier for coordinating urban development and security. However, the implementation of the dual-use concept at the planning level faces systemic challenges, including the lack of top-level design, disconnections in transmission mechanisms, and barriers to cross-departmental coordination. This study reviews the conceptual evolution and policy trajectory of dual-use public infrastructure, and explores the jurisprudential logic and integration challenges concerning its alignment with the five-level, three-category territorial space planning system. The study reveals that the development of dual-use infrastructure is by no means a mere stacking of individual projects; rather, it represents a profound transformation of the logic underpinning territorial space governance. Through a comparative case study of three typical cities (i.e., Beijing, Chengdu, and Xi'an), the study identifies four core bottlenecks: jurisprudential conflicts in planning, ineffective indicator transmission, spatial misallocation, and incomplete standards and specifications. Drawing upon the system theory, planning integration theory, collaborative governance theory, and whole-life cycle management theory, this study constructs a closed-loop embedding framework consisting of strategic leadership, spatial constraints, facility coordination, and practical implementation. Accordingly, a systematic embedding pathway is proposed, encompassing four dimensions: strengthening top-level design guidance, optimizing the planning compilation system, reconstructing a collaborative governance framework, and refining laws and standards. This research aims to translate dual-use requirements from policy discourse into statutory planning control requirements, providing theoretical support and strategic references for achieving dual-use coordination and enhancing

items.title: From Skills Gaps to Energy Resilience: Building a Territorialized Solar Workforce Ecosystem in Indonesia
items.abstract: Indonesia’s electricity plan for 2025–2034 projects 69.5 GW of additional generation capacity, including 17.1 GW of solar power, while government estimates associate the plan with 348,057 solar-related job opportunities. These projections make workforce capability a material implementation issue: renewable infrastructure requires technicians, engineers, safety specialists, project managers and locally available operations-and-maintenance personnel. Yet headline job estimates do not reveal whether workers are available in the required occupations, locations or project phases. This article examines how workforce development can be linked to the resilience of solar infrastructure in an archipelagic state. It uses a focused qualitative documentary analysis, official Indonesian planning and employment documents, and international institutional evidence, interpreted through energy security, capacity development and energy justice perspectives. The analysis identifies four interlocking governance gaps: incomplete skills intelligence; weak alignment between training, certification and project demand; uneven territorial distribution of operational capability; and limited feedback from infrastructure performance into workforce planning. The article proposes a territorialized solar workforce resilience framework in which workforce data, competency standards, work-based learning, local maintenance capacity and critical-infrastructure performance are planned together. The framework is a theory-building contribution, not an estimate of causal effects. Before journal submission, its propositions require validation through comparative project-level fieldwork and verified occupational data.

items.title: State Territorialisation Without Urbanisation: Governing Rural China Under ‘Rural Revitalisation’
items.abstract: Amid the global dynamics of planetary urbanisation, urbanisation has been the frontier of a state territorialisation process of enhancing territorial control and spatial governance. However, recent state strategies in China, exemplified by Rural Revitalisation, reflect a renewed political focus on rural society within state‐driven spatial governance. This study argues that this shift produces a distinctive form of ‘territorialisation without urbanisation’, where the state consolidates control by governing in place—embedding its authority within rural space without converting it into urban jurisdictions. It does so through both spatially bounded and relationally reorienting mechanisms. Beyond traditional territorial urbanisation approaches such as territorial regulation and administrative upscaling, the state further reconfigures state‐society and state‐market relations via grassroots party‐building and fiscal mobilisation. The study illustrates these techniques based on the governance transformation of a village in southwestern China.

items.title: How patriotic discourse informs territorial politics: discursive construction of love, path, and leadership
items.abstract: This research challenges the conventional distinction between patriotism and nationalism and conceptualises patriotism as an open-ended discursive resource whose meaning and effects emerge through situated analysis. Using China’s official discourse on the Taiwan question as a case study, we examine how patriotic discourse informs territorial politics, demonstrating the value of situated analysis. Drawing on Ahmed’s notion of nation as an effect of collective movement and applying the DHA, we analyse how China invokes patriotism in its framing of the Taiwan question. The analysis of the 41 presidential remarks reveals how patriotism is invoked and mobilised in state discourse through historical narratives, continuity framing, metaphorical conceptualisation, and argumentation strategies. Moreover, by distilling patterns from explicit elements in China’s official discourse, we conceptualise patriotism as a regulated trajectory comprising ‘orientation’, ‘prescribed path’, and ‘guiding force’ for examining how meanings of patriotism are channelled in territorial politics.

items.title: Coordinated intelligence in weaver ants (Oecophylla): a review of colony organization, nest construction, territoriality, and foraging.
CCRI_Knowledge Hub Use Case Territorial
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.abstract: This guide, developed by CETEC within the CCRI Knowledge Hub project (Horizon Europe, GA 101135174), presents a territorial case study illustrating how the Technology Marketplace and the Key Product Value Chain (KPVC) guides can be combined to identify circular economy opportunities at regional level. Using the Region of Murcia (Spain) as an example, it explores industrial symbiosis opportunities linked to the valorisation of agri-food by-products and municipal bio-waste. The guide proposes a model involving three territorial hubs and six potential valorisation pathways, including bioactive compounds, biopolymers, biofertilisers, biomethane, insect protein and plastic recycling. It also provides a practical methodology covering technological assessment, governance, financing, implementation and monitoring, offering a replicable framework for local and regional authorities seeking to develop circular economy strategies.

items.title: Territorial geopolitics
items.abstract: This chapter discusses the role of boundaries and borders in geopolitics. It begins by defining boundaries, borders, borderlands, and frontiers. These features are identified as a form of territoriality, or the political construction of territory. The process of boundary formation is described as involving the politics of establishment, demarcation, and control. The process of state formation is described as the most important form of territorial geopolitics. Various forms of boundary conflicts are described through the abstract country of Hypothetica. The process of forming peaceful boundaries and the establishment of borderlands is discussed. The case studies of Israel–Palestine and the Korean peninsula are presented as examples. The intersection of geopolitical flows and political boundaries is discussed and exemplified through the case of the European Union and refugees. The territoriality of the sea is introduced, using the example of disputes over island sovereignty in the South China Sea.

items.title: Building Information Modeling in Civil Engineering: Methods, Applications, and Perspectives for Rural Constructions
items.abstract: Building Information Modeling (BIM) can contribute to the design of rural civil engineering structures beyond geometric design by relating building elements to productive activities and environmental constraints. This narrative review brings together BIM, Geographic Information Systems (GISs), farm management, process simulation, and Digital Twin literature to assess their relevance to agricultural buildings. A conceptual Unified Modeling Language (UML) diagram relates building- and performance assessment-related entities and attributes. Software environments are described in relation to their principal design or coordination functions and potential rural applications. A previously published solar-barn dryer study is discussed as an example of linking a parametric BIM representation with reduced-order airflow-network simulation. The synthesis identifies three principal requirements: representing production processes within building information structures; connecting building-scale data to farm and territorial information; and distinguishing offline design simulation from sensor-informed operational Digital Twins. Key research needs concern interoperable agricultural information models, context-dependent implementation costs, and validation against observations from functioning facilities.

items.title: What Can the Body Do? Territorialisation of Embodied Wellbeing Across Childhood and Adolescence
items.abstract: Young people's wellbeing is commonly conceptualised as an individual psychological state, leaving its embodied and relational production underexplored. Drawing on biographical photo-elicitation interviews, embodied collective memory workshops and participant observation with 119 Danish ninth-grade students, this article examines retrospective accounts of changing embodied relations across childhood and adolescence. Building on Coffey's concept of embodied wellbeing through Deleuze and Guattari's process ontology, we conceptualise wellbeing as embodied capacities organised, stabilised and transformed within everyday affective assemblages. Participants reconstruct childhood bodies as comparatively organised around participation, movement and relation, while adolescence involves a gradual territorialisation around evaluative visibility, comparison and self-monitoring. These processes are gendered and racialised, yet remain provisional: friendship, movement, creativity, belonging and care can deterritorialise evaluative relations and reopen embodied capacities. We argue that embodied wellbeing is a structured but continually shifting field of capacities, relationally and unequally produced across everyday life.

items.title: Towards a preliminary model to assess the circularity potential of building materials at the product manufacturing stage:A systematic review
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a preliminary model to assess the circularity potential of building materials at the product manufacturing stage. Design/methodology/approach A PRISMA-guided systematic review analysed 148 peer-reviewed studies across five dimensions: study type, assessment scale, objective, methodological standardisation and scope. Descriptive analysis and a chi-square test identified patterns and relationships within the literature. The resulting research gaps were synthesised with evidence from 42 existing circularity assessment tools and a comparative analysis of BS EN 15804 and BS EN ISO 14051 to develop the preliminary model. Findings The literature is characterised by parallel development of established and novel methods but limited methodological consolidation. Assessment is concentrated at building and territorial scales; comparative sustainability assessment dominates and combined standardised and nonstandardised approaches remain uncommon. System boundaries also vary significantly with assessment scale. In response, the model establishes an A1-A3 product-stage boundary, disaggregates manufacturing through input-process-output mapping, and integrates qualitative circularity strategies with metrics for raw materials, energy and water across direct and indirect manufacturing flows. Research limitations and implications The model is derived from existing literature and has not yet been empirically validated. Several process and transportation-energy metrics require further operationalisation and testing with manufacturing data. Originality/value The study connects systematic literature review evidence directly to model development and combines a standardised A1-A3 product-stage boundary with process-level resource-flow visibility. It provides a transparent basis for developing a circularity-specific assessment of building-material manufacturing.

items.title: Building peace from the territory: community-based peacebuilding, trust reconstruction, and territorial repair in conflict-affected Colombia
items.venue: Graduate Institute Geneva Institutional Repository (Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies)

items.title: The problem of the administrative-territorial delineation of Karachay autonomy in the process of nation-state building in the North Caucasus (1917-1926)
items.abstract: The purpose of the study is to identify patterns in the formation of Soviet statehood in Karachay in 1917-1926. The evolution of state government bodies – from the civil structures of the Provisional Government to autonomous entities within the RSFSR – is examined. Key factors of state-building are identified, including the impact of the policy of “War Communism” and the agrarian question. The scientific novelty of the article lies in introducing into scholarly discourse a number of archival documents of the South-Eastern Bureau of the Central Committee of the RCP(b) (Russian State Archive of Socio-Political History, f. 65, op. 1, d. 44, l. 110; d. 84, l. 29; d. 96, l. 18) that have not previously been drawn upon by researchers and reflect various viewpoints on the formation of national-state entities in the North Caucasus. Based on these materials, the reasons behind conflicts between ethnic groups and government authorities are substantiated. It is concluded that the establishment of the Karachay-Cherkess Autonomous Oblast was the result of a complex interplay between local initiatives of the national intelligentsia and the policy of the Soviet central government. It was established that the path of the Karachay people to statehood developed in stages: initially, the okrug functioned within the Mountain ASSR (January 1921 – January 1922), subsequently within the unified Karachay-Cherkess Autonomous Oblast (1922-1926), and the final step was delineation along national-territorial lines in 1926.

items.title: Human Settlement in Mountains and Its Built Environment: Case Studies from the Caucasus Mountains between Local Pastoral Communities and Cross-regional States
items.abstract: The Caucasian mountain ranges of the Greater and Lesser Caucasus are highlands where people have been sedentary since the Neolithic period. Like in many of the mountains of western Eurasia, settlement oscillated between mobile and sedentary lifeways of the inhabitants, which goes hand in hand with very different forms of the built environment. Particularly in the Bronze and Iron Ages, complex pastoral settlement systems formed, culminating in the state-organized territorial structure of the Urartian kingdom, which partly was located in the South Caucasus. The chapter presents an overview of the organization of the Caucasian mountains as a habitat and domestic space used by mobile and semi-stationary pastoral peoples of the Bronze Age and by the sedentary and partly state-organized communities of the Early Iron Age. Using a case study from the North Caucasus, whose residential and economic architecture is exemplary for construction methods and techniques in high mountain regions, architectural environments and the elements that characterized built-up mountainscapes are discussed.

items.title: Urban socio-territorial movements
items.abstract: This chapter analyzes the MOI (Movement of Renters and Occupiers), an Argentine social movement that fights for access to housing through the self-managed social production of habitat in Buenos Aires. From a critical geographical perspective, the authors characterize it as an urban socio-territorial movement, given that the appropriation of territory is central to its political project. The study explores four analytical dimensions in territorial terms: strategy, identity, political socialization, and institutions. Drawing on fieldwork conducted in 2024–2025, it examines how the MOI builds “territories for life” outside market logic, producing collective housing at costs 30–40% lower than commercial construction. The authors conclude that these movements propose an alternative urban habitability paradigm grounded in self-management, collective ownership, and solidarity, challenging the neoliberal model that dominates Argentine housing policy.

items.title: Transformation of the Kingly State in Consanguineous-Territorial Relations
items.abstract: This chapter examines how competition and change during the Spring and Autumn Period further broke Chinese ancestors away from the bondage of long-standing consanguineous gentile society. The evolution of human society is a continuous process of differentiation from the whole to the individual. The state was born out of division and exists because of the integration of a divided society. However, the early monarchic state, modeled on narrow blood relations and centered on the king and his royal clan, could not bear the political integration function for vast territories with diverse ethnic groups. Thus, society entered a stage of re-differentiation in the form of a state. The division of the Western Zhou and Eastern Zhou resembles brothers splitting up and going their separate ways. The king’s rule could not be maintained without division, and division inevitably led to competition, in which all sides sought change. “Competition” and “change” became the theme of the era. The chapter explores this transformative process through eight dimensions: iron and fire in building a prosperous country with a powerful army; the rise of vassal states and clashes among feudal princes; rivals and the accumulation of power; the emergence of the administrative system and the territorial state; the tension between kinship and talents; the construction of publicness and civilization; the eventual prevalence of the State of Qin as the latecomer wins; and finally, the Tao and the Entity in homogeneous competition.

items.title: SIT-ANTOFAGASTA: TOOL FOR DECENTRALIZED TERRITORIAL PLANNING
items.venue: Revista Geográfica de Chile Terra Australis
items.abstract: Decentralization in Chile has sought to strengthen regional autonomy and improve the efficiency of public management; however, its implementation has been slow and fragmented, with persistent territorial gaps and limitations in subnational capacities. In this context, the article analyzes the Territorial Information System of Antofagasta (SIT-Antofagasta) as a sociotechnical infrastructure that articulates geospatial data, actors, and planning instruments to support territorial governance and regional decentralization. Using methods that combine documentary analysis, interviews with key stakeholders, and geospatial examples, the study examines its operation, governance model, practical applications, and contribution to evidence-based decision-making. The results show that SIT-Antofagasta facilitates the territorialization of the Sustainable Development Goals, strengthens transparency and participation, and contributes to reducing urban–rural gaps through the generation and democratization of information at the local scale, highlighting the case of the Observatorio Salar de Atacama. Furthermore, the role of capacity building and multi-actor collaboration in the system’s sustainability is evidenced. Despite limitations related to costs, technical capacities, and data updating, SIT-Antofagasta is consolidated as a replicable model for sustainable territorial planning and decentralized governance in contexts of regional inequality in Chile.

items.title: Tribal Kingly States in Consanguineous-Territorial Relations
items.abstract: This chapter examines the origin of the state in both temporal and spatial dimensions. Drawing on the Marxist theory of state origin—including the three general ideas derived from Athens, Rome, and Germany—the chapter argues that while most early states emerged from secondary relations as exemplified by ancient Athens, the pristine state followed a different path. Due to a lack of sufficient empirical materials from China’s earliest period, the chapter takes ancient Athens as a productive reference rather than a direct comparison. This approach reveals that the pristine state was formed on the basis of human primordial relations, namely blood relations, rather than territorial divisions. The chapter then traces the making of the state through war and agriculture, giving rise to a dynastic state born in consanguineous relationships. It further examines kingly states within the framework of familial domination, the process of nation-state-building, the tension between territorial expansion and consanguineous connections, the coexistence of dynastic and gentile affairs, and finally, the ancestral integration of kingly states. By reconstructing this distinct origin path, the chapter provides a foundational understanding of how blood-based relations shaped the earliest form of the state in China.

items.title: Clan-based Kingly States in Consanguineous-Territorial Relations
items.abstract: This chapter examines how the Zhou Dynasty achieved the highest realization of the monarchic state by maturing and finalizing the ancestral system based on kinship. Since the establishment of the state under the Xia Dynasty, ancient China had faced dual tasks: territorial expansion on the one hand, and unified yet pluralistic integration on the other—combining “one family dominating the whole nation” with “all under heaven are of one family”. While this political theme manifested differently across dynasties, the Zhou Dynasty marked a turning point. Building on the historical accumulation of the Xia and Shang, the Zhou developed a self-consciousness of state institutional construction, organizing and governing the state in accordance with or in simulation of the kinship-based clan system. The Western Zhou period achieved the first true unification of the state, with “unity” as its defining theme—a unity grounded primarily in “bloodline”. Though ideal and thus difficult to fully realize, this ideal light has traveled through time and space, leaving a rich legacy for future generations. The chapter explores this process through six dimensions: the moralization of the Mandate of Heaven, paternal authoritarianism, the patriarchal clan system, enfeoffment as regionalization of clan relatives, the state of rites, and the integration of family and state.

items.title: Kingly City States in Consanguineous-Territorial Relations
items.abstract: This chapter examines the transition of the early Chinese state from the primitive era to a more discernible form of civilization and statehood during the Shang Dynasty (1600 bc –1046 bc ). While the Xia Dynasty marked the emergence of China out of disorder and violence into a governed society, it remained in a chaotic state where primitiveness and civilization, gentes and state, coexisted with little archaeological or written clarity. The Shang Dynasty, by contrast, offers abundant archaeological evidence—particularly from Yin Xu—making its state-building process much clearer. The chapter argues that during the Shang period, blood relations gradually faded while territorial relations gained prominence, marked by the rise of chengyi (cities and towns). As a result, the outline of the monarchic state within consanguineous-territorial relations became increasingly visible, though many traces of the original consanguineous matrix persisted. The chapter explores this process through seven key dimensions: the emergence of the state as signaled by bronze, script, and urban centers; the centralization of power through the Mandate of Heaven, hegemony, and the capital; generational continuity in succession to the throne; the practical running of the state through kingship, affairs, and institutions; territorial governance in terms of internal/external, near/far, and close/distant relations; the formation of identity via gentile membership, stratification, and hierarchy; and finally, the generation of the patriarchal clan system through sacrifice, gods, and rites.

items.title: The Historical as Resistance to Territorial Stigmatization and Beyond: The Case of the Raploch
items.abstract: This study explores how residents in the working-class community of The Raploch in Stirling, Scotland, use historical objects and symbols to form a counter-narrative to spatial stigma. Our research supports existing literature on resisting spatial stigma by showing that such stigma is commonly resisted through various modalities. Specifically, we highlight how historical objects serve as sources of community identity and pride, challenging negative depictions of the area as deprived and associated with criminality. Applying a neo-materialist perspective, we raise challenging questions about the agency of materials in the built environment in both creating and resisting stigma. We investigate how the agency of these objects, combined with the agency of the residents, creates an assemblage of resistance. Data was gathered using Photovoice, and the analysis and discussion draws on the interviews generated by participants.

items.title: From Waste to Commons: Digital Pathways for Circularity and Community Resilience in Sintra
items.abstract: This paper explores how assessing and implementing the circular economy at the municipal level can serve as a catalyst for regenerative practices rooted in collective action and the responsible use of information technologies. Using the case study of Sintra, Portugal, it examines the potential of local data and digital tools to promote community engagement, resource mapping, and accountability among both public and private actors. The discussion highlights both opportunities and risks at the intersection of ecological transition, territorial equity, and participatory technologies. The circular economy is regarded not only as a strategy for resource efficiency but also as a pathway to local resilience and the sustainability of shared resources goods.

items.title: ORGANIZATIONAL AND ECONOMIC SUPPORT OF STRATEGIC DEVELOPMENT OF TERRITORIAL COMMUNITIES
items.venue: Actual problems of improving of current legislation of Ukraine
items.abstract: The article substantiates theoretical, methodological and applied provisions on the formation of an effective organizational and economic mechanism for the strategic development of territorial communities in the context of the intensification of the processes of digitalization of public administration. It is shown that the key problem in implementing municipal strategies is the lack of consistency among declared priorities, resource capabilities, and practical tools for implementation. The need to overcome the declarative nature of planning by building a holistic, adaptive system of municipal management is argued. The scientific novelty of the study lies in expanding the organizational and economic mechanism by incorporating digital and analytical management circuits. The traditional structure is optimized by introducing digital management centers, mixed-financing models, integrated analytics systems, and digital tools to attract investment and citizen participation. The author has developed a conceptual model of the mechanism that connects the community's input parameters to the management and instrumental blocks to achieve sustainable socio-economic results. A step-by-step algorithm for the mechanism's functioning is proposed, combining diagnostics of the community's state, priority formation, instrumental support, implementation, monitoring, and continuous adjustment of strategic goals based on the feedback principle. The advantages of implementing data-driven governance for sustainable development, optimizing local budget expenditures, increasing government transparency, and enhancing the innovative capacity of territories are systematized.

items.title: Land rent theories and contemporary urban production: A territorial approach
items.abstract: Adopting an ideal-typical and comparative perspective, this article develops a territorial typology of rent theories beginning with Ricardo, Marshall and the Marxian concept of absolute rent. The typology also describes the territorial configurations underlying these theories. The paper then identifies two key mechanisms that characterise post-industrial cities: (1) the attraction of global financial capital into real estate, and (2) the mobility of consumers drawn to cities for their experiential value. These central drivers of urban development actively reshape today's cities. Drawing on the core insights of Vejchodská et al. (2022) and Smet (2016), the article views value creation and rent capture as interdependent processes, sometimes synergistic and sometimes antagonistic. While Smet (2016) highlights the general shift from Fordist production places to post-industrial spaces of consumption and business services, this paper argues that value is no longer primarily generated within a specific sector, such as manufacturing, with urban development following as a downstream effect. Instead, cities are increasingly produced upstream, in anticipation of value that may later emerge from the dynamic interplay among diverse sectors, populations, activities and the built environment. This anticipatory logic is conceptualised as the integrated urban rent. In this context, large-scale real estate investments often precede and shape urban economic activity, signalling a transition from industry-led urbanisation to a financialised form of capitalism in which entire urban environments are commodified as symbolic and experiential platforms. Rent is no longer derived solely from land scarcity or productivity, but increasingly from the ex ante monetisation of spatial experience.

items.title: From Linear Arteries to Circular Loops: Governance, Reverse Logistics, and the Strategic Reconfiguration of Global Value Chains
items.abstract: The circular economy transition extends beyond environmental goals, fundamentally restructuring global value chains. This paper examines circularity through a political economy lens, proposing a “Governance Logistics Industry (GVC) Nexus” framework. We argue reverse logistics is elevated from waste management to a strategic core of value creation, requiring aligned physical and digital infrastructure.Global value chains are undergoing “reconfiguration” rather than deglobalization, with regionalized recovery networks coexisting with global corridors. Crucially, this transition redistributes power, risking “low-value lock-in” for developing economies unless environmental objectives are coupled with industrial upgrading. Ultimately, closing material loops is a question of power and industrial strategy. Firms and policymakers must treat circularity as an integrated value-chain transformation to foster resilient, inclusive global production networks.

items.title: Constructing Political and Territorial Sovereignty in South America, 1808–1860
items.abstract: This chapter’s objective is to raise some key questions about the process of building political and territorial sovereignty in present-day Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Peru between 1808 and 1860 (with some references to Venezuela). By sovereignty, we understand it as “supreme and independent power, meaning, internal power over the population and external power vis-à-vis other states”. 1 This definition encompasses four themes: the shift from a monarchical to a republican regime; the origin and development of a political system based on the notion of representative government; diplomatic recognition; and the military conflicts between the new countries after independence. The first point relates to “political sovereignty”; the second, to “popular sovereignty”; the third, to “international sovereignty”; and the fourth, to military disputes between “sovereign states”.

items.title: Vibrant Maya Ruins: Community Territorialization in Ake, Yucatán, Mexico
items.abstract: The ruination of many Maya cities in the northern Yucatán Peninsula toward the end of the Classic period (AD 300–900) did not necessarily bring about abandonment in those spaces. On the contrary, the transformation of monumental Maya architecture to heaps of rubble fostered new relations among humans, matter, and other-than-human entities in ancestral places. This article examines the formation and dissolution of a community in Ake’s epicenter, an ancestral Maya city located in present-day Yucatán, Mexico, from approximately AD 1100 to 1550. By AD 1000, monumental buildings were transforming into ruins due to human neglect and the action of gravity, erosion, humidity, and vegetation. These ruins were vibrant entities that prompted the growth of plants, attracted animals, materialized deities and ancestors, and generated human affects, conditions that assembled community life after political collapse. This article offers a glimpse into an ancestral Maya perspective on ruins. This Indigenous perspective was relational, nonhuman centered, and conceived of ruins as lively entities in more-than-human communities.

items.title: Vernacular Architecture, Tradition, and Transformation in Rural Colombia: Toward Scenarios for Territorial Development
items.venue: The International Journal of Design in Society
items.abstract: Rural Colombia has experienced a decline in its cultural and architectural identity due to the neglect of vernacular building techniques and the legacy of its ancestors. The objective of this research is to analyze the relationship between the loss of ancestral knowledge, building practices, and territorial identity, based on the understanding of the natural environment and its inhabitants, in order to strengthen design processes that are better adapted to these realities. The study views the configuration of space as a sustainable alternative and conceives of vulnerable rural territories as opportunities for reflection on habitat and housing, capable of generating solutions tailored to the needs and realities of the country’s rural communities. The research was conducted using a mixed-methods approach combining action research, documentary research, and fieldwork in La Mojana, a region in the department of Sucre, specifically in the municipality of San Benito Abad, Colombia, focusing on the regions territorial dynamics, construction practices, and architectural development. Based on the analysis of the results, the importance of the environment and ancestral knowledge in construction is evident, as is their role in shaping identity and/or driving social transformation. However, the realities reveal a complex landscape where rural sectors have been marginalized and require mechanisms to generate opportunities, in which architecture becomes a catalyst for Colombian rural life.

items.title: Advanced Digital Mapping to Foster Territorial Supply and Demand Network of Secondary Raw Materials Towards Industrial Symbiosis Scenarios
items.abstract: Ecology, metabolism, and industrial symbiosis have driven scientific research and field experimentation since the early 1990s, aiming to reduce waste, increase the reuse of resources already withdrawn from natural ecosystems, and valorise secondary raw materials, while supporting decarbonisation in the construction sector. Despite numerous European and international directives promoting circular economy principles throughout the building life cycle, significant legislative, political, operational, and cultural barriers persist. In particular, the limited availability of information on the location, management, and valorisation of secondary raw materials constrains the effective implementation of circular practices at both the production and end-of-life stages. This paper presents the results of the first experimental digital platform for the multifactorial mapping and localisation of secondary raw materials in Sardinia, Italy, where shortages of both primary resources and recycling and reuse facilities call for innovative industrial symbiosis approaches. The digital mapping covers the main waste categories associated with the construction sector, including concrete, wood, glass, plastics, metals, and ceramics. It provides the basis for identifying potential scenarios for reusing waste streams in parallel industrial processes, supported by AI-based tools, while a user-centred interface facilitates interactions between supply and demand. Results show that the platform can facilitate exchanges between waste producers and potential users, supporting territorial networks and more environmentally conscious waste-management practices. Its main limitation is the need for further operational testing with end users, which constitutes the focus of ongoing research.

items.title: A construção e a territorialização da Agroecologia na Educação do Campo no Brasil: revisão sistemática da produção científica (2014–2023)
items.venue: Revista Brasileira de Educação do Campo
items.abstract: RESUMO. Na última década, a agroecologia tornou-se eixo central nos projetos formativos da Educação do Campo no Brasil, sendo incorporada a experiências educacionais contra-hegemônicas em escolas do campo, institutos federais de educação e universidades. Com base em um estudo aprofundado, este artigo revisa a produção acadêmica stricto sensu sobre a centralidade agroecológica na Educação do Campo, no período de 2014 a 2023, com foco nos avanços, desafios e aprendizados dessa relação. Trata-se de uma Revisão Bibliográfica Sistemática (RBS), baseada no exame de 83 estudos, analisados em quatro categorias. A investigação aponta um aumento expressivo de projetos e ações educativas de caráter popular voltados à agroecologia, com destaque para o protagonismo das mulheres na promoção desse enfoque no campo e na universidade. Por outro lado, nos registros de percurso, visualizam-se cenários de institucionalização frágil nos ambientes educativos, de formação docente ainda incipiente e de inserção limitada nos currículos e nas práticas pedagógicas. Conclui-se que, embora a agroecologia avance como campo de conhecimento e matriz formativa, a consolidação dessa referência depende de uma articulação político‑pedagógica mais incisiva com a Educação do Campo, bem como do estabelecimento de políticas públicas permanentes e de programas estruturados de formação de educadores. Palavras-chave: educação do campo, agroecologia, síntese sistemática. The Construction and Territorialization of Agroecology in Rural Education in Brazil: A Systematic Review of Scientific Production (2014–2023) ABSTRACT. Over the last decade, agroecology has become a central axis in the educational projects of Rural Education in Brazil, being incorporated into counter-hegemonic educational experiences in rural schools, Federal Institutes of Education, and universities. Based on an in-depth study, this article reviews stricto sensu academic production on the centrality of agroecology in Rural Education from 201

items.title: Everyday Practices and the Reframing of Territorial Representations: Inhabitants, Agency, and Public Action
items.abstract: This article offers a reflexive account of an action research approach that involved local residents in shaping territorial representations for tourism and heritage development.It examines how the capability approach, social innovation theory, and critical heritage studies can be operationalized through participatory public action.The central hypothesis is that territorial reconversion can produce lasting effects only if it strengthens residents' capacity to influence not only the transformation of their everyday living environments, but also the institutional representations that define, value, and ultimately shape territorial strategies.Drawing on a four-year programme in La Porte du Hainaut (Northern France), the article analyses an action research process combining territorial diagnosis, participatory workshops, actor-network building, and research-creation.The findings show that spaces for critical reflection enable residents' knowledge and everyday practices to challenge dominant representations, broaden definitions of heritage, and strengthen collective agency by generating counter-narratives around gender, migration, industrial memory, and the ordinary uses of heritage sites.Finally, the article highlights the university's role as a mediator between institutions and citizens while discussing the structural limits of such approaches, including unstable funding, conflicting temporalities, and shifting political priorities.

items.title: Documenting Heritage at Territorial Scale: Heritage Building Information Modelling–Geographic Information System Integration (GeoBIM) and an Effort Unit for Scalable Multiscale Documentation Through Remote Sensing—The DIGIBIC Model (Extremadura)
authors: Adela Rueda Márquez de la Plata
items.abstract: Territorial heritage documentation programmes require coordinated acquisition, processing and information management across assets with different documentation demands. This study presents the Equivalent Documentation Unit (UDE, retaining the project acronym from the Spanish Unidad de Documentación Equivalente), defined as one normalized active person-day of eight person-hours, within the DIGIBIC HBIM–GIS workflow in Extremadura, Spain. The framework distinguishes estimated workload, recorded labour consumption and accepted deliverables. Eighteen development cases document workload heterogeneity and inform a preliminary expert-sizing procedure structured by asset descriptors. Recorded effort in this cohort ranges from 3 to 26 UDEs per asset. Six non-overlapping DIGIBIC 2.0 cases support a retrospective descriptive comparison of expert estimates with an equal-allocation comparator for completed, comparable tasks. For total effort, expert estimates yield a mean absolute error of 1.333 UDEs and a root mean square error of 1.732 UDEs, compared with 1.167 and 1.607 UDEs for equal allocation. In these six cases, field-effort errors are lower under expert sizing, whereas office-effort errors show no corresponding improvement. The contribution is an operational framework linking documentation scope, effort records and territorial information products. The observed estimation errors identify office-work sizing as a priority for refinement and motivate further assessment using new cases.

items.title: Geospatial Provision of the Typology of Territorial Communities by an Integrated Assessment of Their Security Level
items.abstract: The article focuses on developing a methodological approach to integrated assessment of the security level of territorial communities based on geospatial modeling and community typology. The purpose of the research is to develop a methodology for assessing risks and security levels of territorial communities in the context of martial law and post-war recovery. The research methodology is based on system, functional, and geoinformation analysis, mathematical modeling, expert assessment methods, and the analytic hierarchy process. The proposed approach includes the identification of security factors, the construction of a multi-level system of indicators, the determination of weighting coefficients, and the development of an integrated assessment model supported by GIS technologies. The study developed a multi-level system for assessing the security level of territorial communities. The proposed system integrates 97 local indicators grouped into six categories: socio-economic, infrastructural and technogenic, law-enforcement and security, regulatory and legal, environmental, and spatial factors. Based on these indicators, group indices and an integrated security index were calculated. The methodology was tested using territorial communities of Kharkiv Oblast. GIS-based visualization and spatial analysis enabled the identification of territorial differences in security conditions and the classification of communities into four types according to their integrated security level. The scientific novelty of the research lies in the development of a methodological approach to integrated security assessment based on geospatial modeling and the typology of territorial communities. For the first time, we propose a multi-level assessment system that combines 97 local indicators into six group indicators and one integrated security index. The developed approach can be used to support security management and post-war recovery planning.

items.title: Evaluating Material Resources: A Methodological Approach to Reading Territorial Possibility for Sustainable Design
items.abstract: Current approaches to material assessment often address environmental, cultural, design and territorial dimensions separately. This research proposes an exploratory multi-criteria framework aimed at bringing these perspectives into a common comparative structure to guide ecodesign and territorial enhancement processes in contexts characterised by widespread yet underutilised material and cultural resources. The framework integrates a set of criteria addressing material, cultural, design and systemic dimensions. A scenario-dependent weighting system allows the comparison to reflect different design priorities, including circular innovation, ecodesign and heritage enhancement. Its first application in the Basilicata Region illustrates how the relative positioning of local material resources changes according to the priorities considered: clay emerges under priorities related to innovation and circularity, while calcarenite assumes greater significance when cultural continuity and territorial identity are emphasised. The proposed framework complements established material-assessment methods by incorporating cultural, territorial and design-related dimensions. The paper highlights the limitations, potential and prospects of the proposed multi-criteria framework, including the possibility of integrating digital tools and AI systems for territorial data management.

items.title: Renewable Energies and Land-Use Change. A Territorial Reading in Northern Portugal
The Legal Construction of Territory in International Law
items.venue: Max Planck Yearbook of United Nations Law
items.abstract: This article challenges the conventional understanding of territory in international law by arguing that territory is not a natural or physical given, but a socially and legally constructed concept. Traditionally treated as a core requirement of statehood under the Montevideo Convention, territory has been insufficiently theorised and often misunderstood as a synonym for physical land. Drawing on scholarly literature in geography and political theory, the article critiques the natural understanding of territory, describing it as a ‘territorial trap’, where legal doctrine conflates physical geography with legal status. Instead, territory emerges through socio-political process which leads to certain legal consequences. The article further examines how historical doctrines of territorial acquisition, such as terra nullius, conquest and cession, continue to shape legal doctrine despite being incompatible with contemporary international law. The UN Charter era rules, particularly the prohibition of the use of force, self-determination and territorial integrity, have rendered these historic modes largely obsolete. Territorial entitlement is now a ‘zero-sum’ game, where changes in territorial status are scarce and legally regulated rather than determined by factual possession and effective control. The fact that territorial title is no longer determined by factual possession and effective control also has consequences for the law of statehood. States do not come into existence automatically upon meeting factual conditions reflected in the Montevideo criteria. Instead, statehood is a status derived from the sources of international law, particularly treaties and custom. Overall, the article argues that territory and statehood should be reconceptualised by separating territorial title from factual control and by treating both as products of legal and socio-political processes rather than as pre-legal natural facts. In doing so, the article challenges the view that effective

items.title: Sabores do Terroir: Vinhos, Frutas Nativas e Desenvolvimento Territorial
items.abstract: Esta obra reúne estudos científicos e reflexões técnico-conceituais voltados à caracterização, valorização e exploração sustentável da biodiversidade e dos recursos agroalimentares do Rio Grande do Sul, articulando ciência e tecnologia de alimentos, vitivinicultura, gastronomia, sustentabilidade, análise sensorial e valorização territorial. A partir de diferentes abordagens metodológicas, os capítulos contemplam a caracterização físico-química de matérias-primas e produtos, a avaliação de compostos bioativos e da atividade antioxidante, o desenvolvimento de bebidas fermentadas, a análise sensorial, a prospecção e caracterização de leveduras autóctones, o aproveitamento de coprodutos agroindustriais e as relações entre terroir, identidade territorial e produção agroalimentar. Entre os estudos apresentados, destacam-se a investigação de frutas nativas, incluindo araçá, butiá, cereja-do-Rio-Grande, guabiroba, jabuticaba e uvaia, quanto às suas características físico-químicas, propriedades funcionais e possibilidades de aplicação gastronômica e tecnológica; o desenvolvimento de bebida fermentada de jambolão e de kombuchas inspiradas no quentão brasileiro; a caracterização de sucos de uva integrais comerciais; e a avaliação do potencial tecnológico de leveduras autóctones da Campanha Gaúcha para a produção de vinhos com identidade de terroir. A obra contempla, ainda, a caracterização físico-química de vinhos da cultivar Syrah produzidos na Campanha Gaúcha e a investigação da influência de estímulos auditivos sobre a percepção sensorial e a experiência de degustação de vinhos. Outro eixo abordado refere-se ao bagaço de uva, considerando sua variabilidade físico-química, composição e possibilidades de aproveitamento tecnológico e gastronômico. Sob a perspectiva da economia circular e da sustentabilidade, sua valorização é discutida como alternativa para o aproveitamento de coprodutos, a agregação de valor à cadeia vitivinícola e o desenvolvimento de novas aplicações na ind

items.title: From Technological Progress to Systemic Implementation: Governance Barriers to Circular Rigid Polyurethane Foam Recycling in Poland
items.abstract: The transition toward a circular economy depends not only on technological innovation, but also on the governance conditions that enable or constrain its implementation in practice. Rigid polyurethane foam (RPUF), widely used in construction and refrigeration, exemplifies this challenge: despite considerable advances in chemical recycling technologies, their wider implementation, particularly for heterogeneous end-of-life waste streams, remains limited. This study investigates the governance conditions, coordination mechanisms, and institutional barriers that shape the implementation of the circular economy for polyurethane waste within a regional waste management system. Based on a qualitative research design grounded in critical realism, ten self-administered qualitative expert questionnaires were analysed, representing participants from public administration, research institutions, and private-sector organisations involved in waste management and related activities in Poland. Participants were recruited primarily through professional and institutional networks located in and around the GZM Metropolis. Thematic analysis identified fourteen themes organised across five analytical dimensions, indicating that institutional fragmentation, coordination challenges, and policy incoherence interact with technological, material, logistical, and market constraints in limiting the wider implementation of RPUF recycling. The findings conceptualise RPUF recycling as an emerging circular solution constrained by market uncertainty, fragmented coordination, established waste-management arrangements, and short-term project structures. governance-oriented framework comprising orchestration, market stabilisation, procurement and contract adaptation, and temporal anchoring. The framework highlights how these mutually reinforcing dimensions may support the transition from isolated recycling initiatives towards more integrated regional RPUF value chains. cites_core: Conceptualizing the circular economy: An analysis of 114 definitions

items.title: Labor, Cooperation, and Agroecology in Agrarian Reform: Power, Social Capital, and Peasant Territorialization
items.abstract: This article analyzes the relationships among labor, cooperation, social capital, agroecology, and agrarian reform, using peasant territorialization as an interpretive axis for understanding the contradictions of the Brazilian agrarian question. Agrarian reform is approached not merely as a policy of land redistribution, but as a multidimensional process whose effectiveness depends on the reorganization of labor, the construction of collective capacities, the mobilization of social networks, and the production of territories in which rural families can reproduce life with autonomy and dignity. The study adopts a qualitative, theoretical-analytical design grounded in a critical and integrative literature review. It articulates classical and contemporary contributions from labor studies, rural sociology, critical agrarian geography, and agroecology, particularly the works of Marx, Chayanov, Bourdieu, Sennett, Haesbaert, Fernandes, Oliveira, Altieri, and Gliessman. The analysis shows that labor mediates the relationship between land, nature, and social reproduction; that cooperation and social capital strengthen collective action while remaining permeated by unequal access to resources and recognition; and that agroecology can connect productive autonomy, food sovereignty, ecological care, and peasant resistance to agribusiness. Agrarian reform acquires transformative density only when the legal transfer of land is followed by the continuous territorial construction of material, political, organizational, and ecological conditions for remaining on the land. The article concludes that democratizing land without democratizing power, knowledge, markets, and the conditions of labor produces incomplete territorialization, whereas cooperative and agroecological strategies can consolidate settlements as territories of life.

items.title: Smart Tourism Promotion and the Role of Digital Territorial Marketing in Enhancing Destination Competitiveness
items.abstract: With the rapid evolution of digital technology, the promotion of tourism has been transformed leading to the emergence of “smart tourism” as a term used by researchers and practitioners alike. This research paper assesses the impact of digital marketing of places on the competitiveness of tourist destinations by situating the research within the context of smart tourism. The investigation used a qualitative approach with the data being collected through a thematic analysis of three different domains of research (i.e. tourism management literature, case studies in destination-marketing, and stakeholders) in order to discover the main mechanisms by which place-based digital marketing contributes to a destination's competitive advantage. The analysis revealed five themes; construction of a digital identity, personalisation based on data recognition, creation of integration of digital platforms, co-creation by stakeholders, and sustainability as a strategic marketing focus.

items.title: The territorial tectonics: A framework for continuous LCA-driven reconfiguration of biopolymer supply networks
items.abstract: Objective: Bio-based packaging polymers such as polylactic acid (PLA) and polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA) are usually sourced through networks fixed by one static life cycle assessment (LCA), although the regional conditions shaping their footprint shift continually. This study proposes Territorial Tectonics, a framework that treats regional supply clusters as plates that reconfigure only when real-time LCA signals breach defined thresholds. Methodology: We coupled a dynamic LCA with a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model and tested it on a calibrated four-region network over 40 quarters (2026–2035), comparing static, annual, threshold-triggered, and readiness-constrained scenarios across 150 Monte Carlo draws. Results: Threshold-triggered reconfiguration cut cumulative global warming potential (GWP) by 19.7% against the static baseline for a 1.4% cost premium, or USD 61 per metric ton of carbon dioxide equivalent. It matched annual re-optimization on emissions while costing less in 91% of draws; only 5 of 17 threshold breaches justified structural change, and weak readiness erased about one third of the gain. Value: The study unites economic geography, supply chain viability theory, and real-time LCA in one decision architecture. Implications: Firms gain an auditable rule for deciding when to move, and regional authorities learn that permitting speed governs the achievable environmental value. Keywords: Biopolymer Supply Networks, Dynamic Life Cycle Assessment, Supply Network Reconfiguration, Territorial Readiness, Circular Bioeconomy.

items.title: From Research Transfer to Territorial Capability: A Place-Based Systemic RTO Model
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.abstract: This paper develops a place-based systemic RTO model for Less Developed and development-trapped regions, addressing the organisational conditions through which research, technology and external resources can be converted into persistent territorial capabilities. The empirical analysis is based on a longitudinal research-action experiment conducted in Salento-Puglia (Italy), a Less Developed Region affected by development-trap dynamics, persistent brain drain and weak capacity to retain advanced human capital. The CRF model was implemented locally through two complementary socio-technical capacity-building devices: the LivingLab, designed to integrate applied research, technological infrastructures and entrepreneurial experimentation, and #IoRestoInSalento, an oriented knowledge value chain connecting academic research, intermediary functions, innovation actors and territorial demand. Their implementation within the regional ecosystem provided an empirical setting for observing how apparently policy-aligned innovation systems respond when new intermediary architectures attempt to modify established relationships, resource flows and institutional roles. The experiment revealed barriers, gatekeeping behaviours and institutional resistance consistent with mechanisms of path dependence and regional lock-in, suggesting that formal adherence to European innovation and Smart Specialisation objectives may coexist with organisational configurations that reproduce incumbent structures and constrain new capability-building trajectories. Rather than interpreting these effects as isolated organisational conflicts, the paper frames them as evidence of an architectural problem in development-trapped innovation systems, where missing intermediary functions, weak innovation-oriented finance, fragmented research-to-industry interfaces and territorial cultures can limit systemic transformation. The subsequent international scale-up of the CRF model, through transregional research netwo

items.title: Whose Future Matters Now? Childhoods, Climate Justice, and Territorial Inequalities in Brazil
items.abstract: This article aims to reflect on aspects of childhood and their children's lives in a diverse and unequal country such as Brazil, from the perspective of social belonging, processes of dispossession and resistance regarding their territorial rights, climate change, and access to fundamental rights such as education, healthcare, decent housing and safety. Therefore, it presents a section that recognizes an expansion in children's studies focusing on indigenous, traditional and peripheral populations, which offers new possibilities for the visibility of these children; followed by another section which, concisely, identifies Brazil’s significant socio-environmental diversity, its repercussions on people’s lives, and on the construction and transmission of knowledge linked to the land, waters, forests and cycles of nature, as well as dynamics of marginalisation and resistance; the third section, which addresses issues related to the socio-political and environmental aspects present in the contexts of children’s lives and displacement, highlighting factors that produce geopolitical and socio-environmental exclusion; this is followed by a brief discussion of processes of coloniality and decoloniality and their contribution to the core of the issue. It concludes by indicating that, by situating children within concrete territorial contexts and recognising their forms of participation in social life, childhood studies broaden their theoretical and political scope and allow for analyses that are more sensitive to the intersections between cultural diversity, socio-environmental inequality and intergenerational justice.

items.title: Towards plastics circularity in Mexico: A systematic assessment of barriers, policy gaps, and operational strategies
Beyond technological innovation for sustainability in the Amazon: governance, territorial conditions and scaling constraints in socio-ecological systems
items.abstract: The Amazon must reconcile ecological integrity with socioeconomic development across diverse territorial contexts. This systematic literature review examines technological innovations studied in Amazonian contexts, their sustainability outcomes, and the conditions shaping adoption, scaling and durability. Searches of Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection and SciELO identified 64 peer-reviewed publications published between 2004 and 2025, including 61 in the main synthesis and three secondary reviews analyzed separately. Because broader Amazonian variants and relaxed innovation-or-technology logic were used only in SciELO, the findings represent a delimited synthesis rather than comprehensive cross-sectoral coverage. The main-synthesis publications spanned eight domains: agriculture, digital monitoring, biodiversity-based processing, circular economy, innovation systems, essential services, forestry and aquaculture. Environmental and economic or productive outcomes were most frequently coded, but technical feasibility was demonstrated more often than realized sustainability. Only 13 publications directly evaluated a sustainability outcome; 21 measured technical performance from which sustainability was inferred; 13 reported or perceived outcomes without independent verification; ten modeled or proposed sustainability; three provided mapping or diagnostic evidence; and one combined measured performance with modeled implications. Implementation depended on public and research institutions, communities, Indigenous actors, firms and producer organizations, while remoteness, ecological variability, infrastructure, finance, markets and regulation constrained scaling. Justice, benefit-sharing and adverse outcomes remained underexamined. The sensitivity analysis retained 12 of the 13 direct-evidence studies, but modeled or proposed evidence declined from ten to four.
