items.title: Claiming the swamp: How territorialization produces hidden populations in South Sumatra's peatlands
items.abstract: Successive interventions in South Sumatra's peat swamps including logging, transmigration, plantations, conservation, and restoration have led to changing land use permits, boundaries, canal systems, different land use classifications, and prohibitions. This article examines how those overlapping territorial regimes reshaped access to wetland resources in Perigi and Riding, Ogan Komering Ilir, and how their effects were differentiated within the local population. It uses 'hidden population' as an analytical concept for politically-produced invisibility rather than as an official or self-ascribed identity. The analysis draws primarily on fieldwork conducted in 2018, supplemented by relevant contextual observations from research undertaken in the same area in 2019 and 2021 and other more recent data sources. Territorialization made earlier histories of use and resource claims progressively less legible within formal governance. Accounts of livelihood loss were particularly pronounced among people dependent on interior swamp resources and poorly connected to village institutions. Legal, institutional, ecological, and economic ambiguities further constrained decisions about fishing, cultivation, canal maintenance, and intergenerational livelihood transfer. Accounts distinguish household adaptations from collective efforts to defend land, including canal construction and negotiation during a plantation dispute. The case contributes to political ecology and feminist political ecology by explaining produced invisibility as an uneven, relational, and negotiated outcome of territorial governance.

items.title: Methodology for assessing geotechnical risks of urban development under wartime impacts and territorial recovery
items.venue: Collection of Research Papers of the National Mining University
items.abstract: Purpose. Development of a scientific and methodological approach to the comprehensive assessment of geotechnical risks in urban development areas affected by military and related technogenic impacts, taking into account the transformation of the soil mass condition and the interaction within the “soil mass–foundation–structure” system. The methods. Systematic and comparative analyses of current approaches to geotechnical risk assessment, soil–foundation–structure interaction, and changes in the state of the soil mass under military and anthropogenic impacts were performed. Structural-logical and conceptual modelling of the sequential transformation of territorial conditions, expert ranking of risk factors, and development of an algorithm for their integrated assessment were applied, incorporating site investigations, stress-strain state analysis, and geotechnical monitoring. Findings. A geotechnical risk assessment algorithm was developed that integrates analysis of the territory’s transformation history, comprehensive site investigations, development of an updated geotechnical model, stress-strain state assessment, identification of potential instability mechanisms, evaluation of impacts on existing structures, and selection of engineering mitigation measures. Future research should focus on numerical modelling of the sequential transformation of the soil mass under military and technogenic impacts. The originality. A correlation was established between ground conditions, structural vulnerability, the intensity of hazardous processes, and the level of geotechnical risk. Based on this relationship, an integrated risk assessment model and an implementation algorithm incorporating feedback between monitoring data and the computational geotechnical model were developed. Practical implementation. The proposed approach can be applied to geotechnical site investigations, reconstruction projects, and new construction in areas affected by military impacts. items.title: Rethinking Territorial Attractiveness in Selected MENA Countries: A Composite Index and Panel Data Perspective
items.abstract: This article analyses territorial attractiveness in six selected MENA countries Algeria, Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, Qatar and Tunisia from 2000–2024. It builds a Composite Territorial Attractiveness Index (CTAI) from seven economic, institutional, infrastructural, tourism and environmental indicators and analyses its relationships with trade openness, inflation rate, internet penetration rate, oil rents (as % of GDP) and population using panel-data econometric models. The analysis employs two-way fixed effects with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors and provides robustness checks on the estimation in terms of alternative index constructions, bandwidth sensitivity and first-difference specifications. Perhaps the strongest positive correlate of the CTAI found across all three index constructions and first-difference models is trade openness. CTAI is negatively (and slightly more significant on levels than first-differences) associated with inflation in the main and alternative specifications, Internet penetration and oil rents are not statistically significant whereas the negative population coefficient is sensitive to index construction and econometric specification. The results reaffirm the view of territorial attractiveness as a spatially complex and multidimensional concept, and call to take external integration policies into account alongside reforms by institutions, infrastructure or productive capacity. Owing to the small, unbalanced panel and ambiguous unit-root results, the findings are taken as conditional correlations rather than causal effects or fitted long-run relations.

items.title: Governing extractive wealth: Mining royalties, territorial capabilities and diversification in Brazilian mining territories
items.abstract: Mining-dependent territories face the challenge of transforming temporary extractive revenues into diversified and resilient development trajectories. Although mining royalties expand municipal fiscal resources, their developmental effects depend on how they are governed, negotiated and mobilised. This article examines how mining royalties become—or fail to become—place-based resources for diversification and innovation. Drawing on evolutionary economic geography and debates on path dependence, path creation and change agency, the article conceptualises mining royalties as contested territorial resources whose effects are mediated by governance arrangements, place-based agency and territorial capability-building. The study compares Itabira and Paracatu, two mining-dependent municipalities in Minas Gerais, Brazil, through a qualitative comparative case-study design based on 45 semi-structured interviews, documentary analysis and territorial data. The findings show that royalties do not automatically generate diversification. Their transformative potential depends on whether territorial actors can coordinate initiatives and convert temporary revenues into cumulative capabilities involving knowledge, skills, organisations, networks and institutional learning. Itabira possesses substantial mining-related assets but faces difficulties in recombining them beyond a deeply embedded extractive trajectory. Paracatu benefits from a more plural productive and institutional environment, although it still faces challenges in consolidating emerging capabilities. The article contributes to debates on extractive development and evolutionary economic geography by demonstrating that transition beyond mining dependence is a process of territorial capability-building. Mineral revenues become transformative when governance and place-based agency connect resources, actors and projects in ways that generate capacities extending beyond political administrations, corporate cycles and the pro

items.title: Artisanal and Historical Gold Mining: A Comparative Study Between Mozambique and Italy Toward Sustainable and Circular Practices
items.abstract: Gold mining takes place within highly diverse geological, technological, and socio-economic contexts, ranging from active artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) to historical gold mining districts where extraction has ceased, leaving long-term environmental legacies. This paper presents a comparative analysis of two case studies, active ASM in Mozambique and historical gold mining in Italy, examining how different stages of the mining life cycle shape environmental and social outcomes. In Mozambique, ASM remains a key rural livelihood but is associated with mercury amalgamation, siltation, and occupational health risks under largely informal conditions, with formalization constrained by artisanal extraction methods and access to finance, although cooperative organizational models and technical support services can help to overcome these constraints. In Italy, decades after mine closure, extractive waste and tailings continue to release potentially toxic elements while showing enrichment in critical raw materials (CRMs), representing anthropogenic resource stocks with secondary raw material recovery potential. Despite their different stages of activity, both case studies reveal opportunities for improving resource efficiency through circular economy approaches, mercury-free processing, geoconservation and geotourism, and integration of cultural heritage into territorial development. The comparison highlights the value of governance, capacity building, and knowledge transfer between active and post-mining contexts, supporting a shift toward more sustainable and circular gold mining practices.

items.title: PROJETO NÓS PROPOMOS! NA UNIOESTE/FRANCISCO BELTRÃO: CIDADANIA TERRITORIAL E GOVERNANÇA
items.abstract: This text presents the Nós Propomos! Project developed at Unioeste in Francisco Beltrão, based on experiences with teachers and students from basic and higher education and postgraduate programs in Geography and Education since its inception in 2017. The project aims to foster territorial citizenship through teaching, research, and extension, with the purpose of studying the historical processes of municipalities in the Southwest region of Paraná, focusing on territorial citizenship and heritage education. This paper synthesizes some of the main actions carried out in public and private schools, in elementary, secondary, and higher education, in the municipalities where the project is implemented: Francisco Beltrão, Itapejara D’Oeste, Verê, Pato Branco, and Enéas Marques (PR). The Nós Propomos! Project occurs primarily with student participation, under teacher mediation, and follows the methodological perspectives developed at the University of Lisbon, Portugal, by Professor Sérgio Claudino. The actions aim to enable students to identify local problems and propose intervention measures, presenting proposals to local public authorities and responsible institutions. These practices are characterized as research, teaching, and extension, contributing to the formation of territorial citizenship and promoting the importance of geographic education at state, national, and international levels. Geographic education is, ultimately, an instrument for building governance.

items.title: Beyond Universal Indicators: A Critical Review and Conceptual Framework for Territorially Situated Sustainability Assessment
items.abstract: Sustainability assessment requires translating a concept that is both plural and normatively contested into criteria, indicators, and procedures capable of supporting evaluative judgments. This critical review examines how conceptual plurality, normative choices, and territorial specificity shape this process of operationalization. Through an interpretive and comparative analysis of conceptual and methodological literature, four interrelated domains were examined: conceptualizations of sustainability, operationalization of evaluative judgments, incorporation of territory, and the participation of actors and different forms of knowledge. The synthesis shows that adapting indicators to local conditions or incorporating participatory mechanisms does not necessarily imply that the conception of sustainability underlying an assessment has itself been territorially constructed. Building on this distinction, we propose Territorially Situated Sustainability Assessment (TSSA), a conceptual framework that shifts the starting point of assessment from adapting predefined indicators to constructing the conception and criteria of sustainability from the constitutive characteristics of the territory. TSSA articulates three cross-cutting conditions throughout this process: normative legitimacy, concerning how values, priorities, and evaluative choices are defined; territorial relevance, concerning their grounding in the socioecological, historical, and cultural characteristics of the territory; and epistemic rigor, concerning the quality and appropriate use of the knowledge and evidence supporting the assessment.

items.title: Assessing the Territorial Embeddedness of Events in Tourism Destinations: A Transparent Criteria-Based Scoring Model
items.venue: Central Asian Journal of Innovations on Tourism Management and Finance
items.abstract: The fact that an international event is held in a particular city does not mean that the event is durably attached to that place. This paper develops a transparent model for assessing the territorial embeddedness of an event, defined as the extent to which its content, control, recurrence and public identity are bound to a host destination, and specifies how the resulting composite score should and should not be interpreted. Building on research in event tourism, event portfolio management and economic geography, four criteria are proposed: dependence on local resources, local governance and brand rights, recurrence at the destination, and place identification. Each criterion is scored 0, 0.5 or 1, with a separate “unknown” state, and the scores are combined by an equal-weight arithmetic mean. The scoring rules were tested on four stylised profiles and on official documentary evidence for two events hosted in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. The stylised profiles produced composite scores of 0.875, 0.500, 0.500 and 0.250. The two profiles scoring 0.500 had entirely different structures, and their relative ranking depended wholly on the weights, reversing in 49.8% of 100,000 random weight draws. Recording a missing criterion as zero pushed the score to the lower bound of its admissible interval (0.625–0.875 in the test case). The criterion profile, the evidence behind each score and the interval bounds should therefore be reported alongside the composite. The model is a planning instrument rather than a measure of economic impact, and its inter-rater reliability must be established before operational use.

items.title: From access to functional inclusion: a realist review of digital finance and territorial inequalities in Brazil
items.abstract: Purpose Digital finance is widely promoted as a scalable pathway to financial inclusion in emerging markets, yet outcomes remain uneven across territories and social groups. This paper synthesizes empirical evidence from Brazil to explain how and under which conditions digital expansion produces functional inclusion or reinforces new forms of exclusion. Design/methodology/approach A realist review, based on context–mechanism–outcome logic, draws on 24 distinct sources comprising empirical studies and contextual material, with searches conducted in Scopus on 30 September 2025. Findings are interpreted through mechanism-based configurations linking territorial conditions, user capability and service delivery arrangements. Findings The synthesis distinguishes formal inclusion, understood as access, from functional inclusion, understood as effective, autonomous and safe use. It identifies four recurrent mechanisms shaping uneven outcomes: inclusion that excludes, vulnerable trust, unequal infrastructure and mediated disintermediation. Together, these mechanisms explain why expanded digital access can coexist with constrained use, dependency and heightened vulnerability in rural and peripheral territories. Practical implications The findings support territorially sensitive digital finance strategies, including hybrid service delivery, accessible consumer support and dispute resolution, monitoring of functional inclusion indicators, and capability-building in low-connectivity contexts. Originality/value Rather than treating adoption or account ownership as inclusion, the paper develops a mechanism-based framework explaining Brazil’s digital inclusion paradox. It contributes to emerging market finance research by showing how institutional arrangements, territorial infrastructures and user capabilities interact to produce functional inclusion or exclusion.

items.title: Integrating International Experience into Strategies for Developing Security-Oriented Management of Territorial Community Development
items.venue: Scientific Notes of Lviv University of Business and Law
items.abstract: Today, territorial communities are developing in an environment characterized by heightened uncertainty, security risks, crisis situations, and the impact of external threats. This necessitates the search for effective approaches to integrating international practices into the system of strategic management of territorial development in Ukraine. The study aims to identify opportunities for utilizing international experience when formulating strategies for security-oriented development management in Ukraine's territorial communities. The research systematizes international approaches to ensuring territorial security, taking into account components such as risk assessment, crisis response, post-crisis recovery, and the building of long-term community resilience. A comparison of international models with current practices in security and development management within Ukrainian territorial communities revealed differences in organizational approaches, coordination mechanisms, and the distribution of responsibilities. At the same time, key problems and institutional constraints hindering the full utilization of international experience in the Ukrainian context were identified. This lays the groundwork for further determining how to adapt such experience to the national local self-government system and for shaping a more resilient model of development management for territorial communities. International practices best suited for adaptation to Ukrainian conditions were identified, considering the security, institutional, socio-economic, and organizational specifics of community development. Strategic directions for integrating international experience into the development management system of Ukraine's territorial communities were substantiated. A model for security-oriented management of territorial community development has been formulated, integrating risk management, crisis response, collaborative partnerships, digital tools, and mechanisms for maintaining territorial

items.title: Evolution characteristics and optimization strategies of territorial spatial conflict in megacities——a case study of Chongqing
items.abstract: ObjectiveSpatial conflict is a key bottleneck hindering the improvement of territorial spatial governance efficiency， which is particularly prominent in megacities with highly concentrated population and production factors. Scientifically identifying the intensity， driving factors， and evolutionary characteristics of territorial spatial conflicts can provide theoretical support and a practical basis for establishing a long-term governance system of territorial spatial conflicts.MethodsTaking Chongqing as the study area， this study used land use data and natural-socio-economic data from 2000 to 2023. Following the analytical framework of “regional functional pattern evolution—conflict intensity identification—zoning-based optimized regulation and control”， it characterized the evolution of territorial spatial patterns， identified territorial spatial conflict intensity， and proposed zoning-based solutions for conflict regulation and optimization.Results（1） The overall territorial spatial pattern of the study area showed the evolutionary characteristics of “urban space expansion， agricultural space contraction， and marginal degradation of ecological space”. The intensity of evolution was closely related to economic development levels and topographic conditions： more intense in the relatively flat and economically developed main urban area， and relatively moderate in the northeastern and southeastern regions of Chongqing， which were economically less developed and had rugged terrain. （2） The overall level of territorial spatial conflict showed an increasing trend over time， forming a “core-periphery” diffusion pattern that highly overlapped with the direction of urban expansion. The level of conflict exhibited strong regional differentiation： conflict levels were high in the main urban area， extending from the central city to the urban fringe. items.title: Technologically Justified Public Investment of a Territorial Community: Financial and Legal Model and Assessment Criteria
items.abstract: Problem setting. The recovery and development of Ukrainian territorial communities require public investment in energy, water supply, transport, construction, communications, digital systems and data management. Limited budget resources increase the cost of an erroneous technological choice because the selected solution determines capital expenditure, future operating expenditure, staffing needs, compatibility with existing infrastructure, procurement conditions and the useful life of the asset. Ukraine’s public investment management framework regulates project preparation, appraisal, implementation, monitoring and completion. However, the technological, operational and life-cycle parameters of technology-intensive projects are distributed among several stages and legal instruments. A coherent financial and legal model is therefore required to connect the available technology, the community’s financing decision and a sustainable public result. Analysis of recent research and publications. The theoretical basis of the study combines research on innovation and technological change by J. Schumpeter, R. Solow and P. Romer; the concept of absorptive capacity developed by W. Cohen and D. Levinthal; studies of path dependence by W. Arthur; and research on technology diffusion by D. Comin and B. Hobijn. Financial-law scholarship provides the doctrinal understanding of public finance as a legally regulated system of relations concerning the formation, allocation and use of public funds. Recent empirical research on local governments demonstrates the relevance of skills, infrastructure, data governance and institutional conditions for technological capability. A. Gjaerum’s study additionally identifies procurement, outsourcing and buyer-provider relations as significant constraints on municipalities’ ability to manage digital transformation. Nevertheless, the literature does not provide an integrated set of financial and legal criteria tailored to technology-intensive public

items.title: ECONOMIC-SPATIAL MODEL OF THE COMPREHENSIVE SPATIAL DEVELOPMENT PLAN OF THE TERRITORIAL COMMUNITY AND THE STATE LAND CADASTRE
items.venue: Scientific Notes of Taurida National V I Vernadsky University Series Economy and Management
items.abstract: This paper aims to investigate the incorporation of functional zones, defined by the comprehensive spatial development plan, into the State Land Cadastre. To achieve this goal, the authors propose using geographic information systems (GIS) and, specifically, geospatial artificial intelligence (GeoAI). The research problem is addressed by developing a model that integrates artificial intelligence with GIS technologies. The findings offer significant value for spatial land management by ensuring construction transparency, predictable investment decisions, and the protection of community interests. The relevance of this study lies in demonstrating the potential of combining GIS and AI. It also substantiates the feasibility of integrating urban planning and land management documentation for post-war recovery.

items.title: Development and Content Validity Assessment of a Bioclimatic–Territorial Framework for Ecolodge Design in the Hot–Humid Ecuadorian Amazon
items.abstract: Ecolodge design in the hot–humid Ecuadorian Amazon must account for climate, ecology, construction, culture, and daily operation. This exploratory, conceptual, and framework-oriented study developed a bioclimatic–territorial framework and assessed its content validity using a sequential mixed-methods design with qualitative priority. Development combined an integrative review of 105 original studies, thematic synthesis, and aggregated contextual evidence from a prior academic project involving five ecolodge managers. Ten experts assessed 19 statements for relevance, clarity, coherence, and anticipated applicability, yielding an overall Aiken’s V of 0.858 (95% CI: 0.843–0.872). Following revision and operationalization, an independent panel of eight experts reassessed the framework, yielding V = 0.854 (95% CI: 0.836–0.869); all five dimensions exceeded the prespecified benchmark of 0.80. The consolidated framework connects multiscale territorial diagnosis, project-specific problems, adaptation principles, architectural and operational decisions, required resources and capacities, and 25 verification criteria. An illustrative application in Macas demonstrates the decision sequence and identifies evidence gaps. The contribution is a traceable design-support process that treats documented Amazonian conditions as operational inputs. Expert assessments support content validity; building performance remains untested.

items.title: THE EVOLUTIONARY TRAJECTORY OF THE GREEN BUILDING CONCEPT: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF SCIENTIFIC APPROACHES
items.abstract: The growing diversity of approaches to green building has significantly expanded its conceptual field, encompassing sustainable, low-carbon, circular, regenerative, and nature-positive construction, as well as whole-life assessment and human well-being perspectives. This study aims to reconstruct the evolutionary trajectory of the green building concept and identify the patterns underlying the expansion of its subject matter, system boundaries, and criteria for assessing the environmental and economic performance of construction activities. The research is based on a structured corpus of 220 scientific publications selected through an iterative search strategy consistent with the principles of systematic literature review. A comparative analysis was conducted using a unified set of criteria, including terminology, the central object of research, dominant assessment criteria, system boundaries, and theoretical foundations. The findings reveal a cumulative and branching pattern of conceptual development. Emerging approaches do not replace earlier ones but extend, specialise, and interact with them, producing an increasingly differentiated conceptual field. The evolution of green building is characterised by an expansion of the object of analysis from the individual building and its operational performance to the entire life cycle, material and carbon flows, value chains, territorial systems, and broader socio-ecological interactions. At the same time, assessment criteria have expanded from energy and resource efficiency to include decarbonisation, circularity, climate resilience, human health and well-being, ecosystem restoration, and positive environmental impacts. The findings provide grounds for interpreting green building as an integrative meta-concept that encompasses interrelated research approaches within a common theoretical field. Its contemporary development is therefore characterised by increasing differentiation, interaction, and integration of conceptual

items.title: Sustentabilidade social e resiliência territorial: Equidade, inclusão e desenvolvimento humano para a transformação das comunidades
items.abstract: Social sustainability, by integrating conditions of equity, well-being, and human development, constitutes a fundamental dimension of sustainable development that promotes the construction of resilient communities. The general objective of this study is to analyze social sustainability from a territorial perspective, considering its main foundations, dimensions, related factors, and challenges in terms of building resilient communities. A qualitative, descriptive, and interpretative study was conducted, supported by a documentary review of scientific literature consulted in Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, SciELO, and Redalyc, prioritizing publications from the last five years. This information was complemented with documents from international organizations and examined through thematic content analysis. The findings show that social sustainability is a multidimensional phenomenon that integrates equity, social cohesion, social capital, education, employment, community participation, and institutional capacities. Challenges related to territorial inequalities, urban-rural gaps, and connectivity limitations were also identified, particularly in Colombia. Digital transformation represents both a risk of deepening inequalities and an opportunity to increase access to services and opportunities. It is inferred that building socially sustainable and resilient communities requires strengthening human and institutional capacities, promoting citizen participation, and consolidating multilevel, multi-actor, and multisectoral governance mechanisms. In this regard, comprehensive territorial strategies are recommended that integrate institutional cooperation, digital inclusion, and community capacity-building initiatives aimed at sustainably improving people's quality of life.

items.title: The Descent into the Underworld and Lake Pergusa: Myth, Sinkhole and the Touristic Construction of Landscape
items.abstract: Purpose – This paper examines Lake Pergusa as an emblematic case of interaction between classical myth, geomorphological processes and the touristic construction of landscape. Drawing on the theoretical framework of literary tourism and imaginative geographies, the article argues that the narrative sedimentation of the abduction of Proserpina – notably codified by Ovid in the Metamorphoses – has contributed to transforming a sinkhole lake in inland Sicily into a ‘mythical gateway’. The aim is twofold: first, to reconstruct the cultural genealogy of the katabasis and the territorialisation of the myth in Sicily; secondly, to demonstrate how this symbolic stratification may represent a resource for cultural tourism and geotourism, particularly within the framework of the Rocca di Cerere UNESCO Global Geopark. Design/methodology/approach – The study adopts an interdisciplinary approach combining literary analysis, historical-cartographic interpretation and geomorphological assessment. It first reconstructs the motif of the katabasis in the Western tradition (from Homer and Virgil to Dante), highlighting the progressive association between physical locations and symbolic thresholds of the underworld. It then investigates the territorialisation of the Proserpina myth in the Enna area through literary, iconographic and cartographic sources that attest to the identification of the lake as the site of the abduction. Finally, it analyses the geological features of the basin, interpreted as a piping sinkhole developed in sedimentary cover deposits over evaporitic bedrock, together with its hydro-biological dynamics (including the episodic reddening of the waters), in order to connect mythical narrative and scientific explanation within a sustainable tourism perspective. Originality/value – The originality of the paper lies in proposing Lake Pergusa as a geomythological landscape in which myth, literature and geology jointly shape territorial identity. items.title: The Technical and Organizational Foundations for Building Local Energy Systems
items.abstract: The article focuses on addressing the issue of increasing the resilience of the energy supply system in the face of terrorist threats. The research carried out made it possible to substantiate the feasibility of the widespread creation of local energy systems for territorial communities as a means of minimizing energy capacity losses due to terrorist and cyber attacks. The aim of the study is to develop technical and organizational principles for building local energy systems (LES) aimed at providing energy to a specific territorial community (TC) through the development of distributed generation and maximum possible use of renewable energy sources (RES). The methodological basis of the study includes decomposition, system, and comparative approaches. In the course of the study, methods of comparative analysis were used (comparing technical and organizational approaches to building energy systems); abstraction (isolating the properties of electric power that most affect the organization of the related market); and synthesis (to develop principles for building a distributed energy system aimed at meeting the needs of a territorial community). The study examined the decisive influence of the physical properties of electric power on the technical foundations for building Ukraine’s unified energy system, and based on this, developed recommendations for the architecture and principles of creating local energy systems focused on supplying energy to a specific community. The analysis of the legal and regulatory principles for organizing the nationwide market was used as the basis for developing proposals on the organization of local electric power markets. These studies made it possible to identify four groups of key factors that affect the process of building local energy systems for territorial communities: technical, organizational, economic, and legal. The scientific novelty of the research lies in the further development of a scientific-methodological approach to buil

items.title: Multi-dimensional analysis of the viability of emerging rural circular bioclusters: proposition of a Canvas
items.abstract: This article develops a multi-dimensional analysis tool, the ‘Canvas for the viability of emerging circular bioclusters’. The Canvas is based on a scoping literature review, covering business models of the circular bioeconomy, (bio)clusters, cluster and supply chain viability, and proximity relationships. It is validated and refined via six empirical case studies mainly from the Occitanie region in France. Compared to the original firm-centric business model canvas which basically aims at economic value creation, this new canvas allows systematically evaluating the conditions and viability of emerging collaborative circular bioeconomy clusters where different geographically close actors jointly aim to valorize biomass in sustainable ways. A complete set of socio-economic and environmental viability factors are identified, encompassing the ecosystem, value proposition including technical and legal feasibility, economic profitability, territorial anchoring and environmental performance. Results further show the interrelations of all viability dimensions and their potential tradeoffs. This study makes an original contribution to existing circular bioeconomy business model and sustainable rural development literature by proposing a structured analysis tool to assess the viability of regional circular bioclusters. The application of the Canvas to data-rich case studies illustrates its effectiveness and identifies the levers and barriers to the emergence, development and sustainability of rural circular bioclusters. Insights from this study also provide valuable information to stakeholders involved in the development and management of these bioclusters.

items.title: Decentralized Cooperation and the Future of African Regional Development: What Public Policies to Bridge the Territorial Gap?
items.abstract: This paper examines whether decentralized cooperation (DC) is associated with lower territorial inequality in Africa and under what institutional conditions. We develop a conditional decentralization framework that distinguishes DC from fiscal decentralization and test it using a balanced panel of 38 African countries from 2000 to 2022. Two‐way fixed‐effects models are complemented by restricted two‐step System GMM and spatial specifications. In the preferred fixed‐effects model, a 1‐percentage‐point increase in DC intensity is associated with a 0.00142 decline in the regional Gini (0–1 scale), about 0.32% of the sample mean. The association becomes stronger as governance improves and is statistically distinguishable from zero above an estimated CPIA threshold of about 3.0. Spatial estimates are also consistent with positive cross‐border spillovers. Robustness checks using alternative governance measures, subsamples, inequality measures, index weights, and placebo specifications support the direction of the findings. The results suggest that DC should be embedded in formal national frameworks, paired with governance safeguards and administrative capacity‐building, and coordinated through cross‐border municipal clusters where spillovers may arise. Because the DC proxy is based mainly on subnational official development assistance, the estimates should be read as directional rather than definitive causal magnitudes.

items.title: Sistemas de geovisualización para analizar desigualdades territoriales y apoyar políticas públicas basadas en evidencia
items.abstract: This study proposes a methodology for designing and applying geovisualization systems that transform statistical and geographic information into accessible evidence for territorial analysis and evidence-based policy. The methodology integrates spatial units, indicator construction, spatial analysis, georeferenced data layers, and interactive visualization to relate statistical information to the territorial environment. Its application to female-headed households in the urban area of the Orizaba Metropolitan Area, Veracruz, Mexico, demonstrates how this approach facilitates the identification, comparison, and spatial localization of patterns associated with gender inequalities and vulnerabilities in the enjoyment of economic and social rights. By relating the percentage of female-headed households at the Basic Geostatistical Area (AGEB) level to its spatial context, the system makes territorial disparities more visible and interpretable. The study argues that geovisualization can contribute to generating evidence for evidence-based policy, informing territorially differentiated planning and public decision-making aimed at building pathways to opportunity and ensuring a more level playing field across territories.

items.title: The development of housing construction in Sevastopol in 1965-1985
items.abstract: The article examines the main principles, mechanisms, and outcomes of the state policy for the spatial and territorial development of Sevastopol in 1965-1985, focusing on housing and civil construction. The aim of the study is to reconstruct the development of housing construction in Sevastopol during this period. The article analyzes a wide range of sources that make it possible to present quantitative and qualitative indicators of the construction of housing and social and cultural facilities. The scientific novelty lies in providing a comprehensive historical analysis of housing construction in Sevastopol in 1965-1985. On this basis, the author develops a three-stage periodization of the sector’s development and identifies the technological and organizational features of the transition from large-block housing construction to industrial large-panel construction. In addition, a substantial body of archival materials is introduced into scholarly circulation, making it possible to identify systemic contradictions in the Soviet urban-planning model. The main result of the study is a periodization of housing construction in Sevastopol, which, based on empirical data, characterizes the specific features and qualitative and quantitative indicators of each stage. The findings demonstrate both the large-scale achievements of the Soviet model of mass construction and its systemic shortcomings and contradictions.

items.title: Harnessing Crowd Intelligence for Collective Digital Reputation and Governing Sustainable Destination Image Through Territorial Marketing
items.abstract: This study underscores the fundamental transformation of destination image formation in rapidly digitizing tourism ecosystems and the role of crowd intelligence in governing territorial marketing. It emphasizes the shift in locus of control from corporate actors to distributed online collectives, stressing the need for Destination Management Organizations to transition from top-down promotional efforts to a governance-oriented paradigm. The study details a system orchestration model, stabilize collective digital reputation through a circular 4-Layer Formation Process involving experience-based signal production, platform-mediated amplification, reputation formation, and territorial governance. It positions three research areas—territorial marketing, digital reputation systems, and crowd intelligence as a manageable strategic resource. The study examines pillars of sustainability including authenticity, stakeholder alignment, and tourist co-creation, while discussing future frontiers like generative AI, decentralized autonomous destinations, and sustainability orchestration.

items.title: Veracruz: gestión hídrica y economía circular en los corredores petroquímicos
items.abstract: Veracruz concentra refinerías, complejos petroquímicos, instalaciones de almacenamiento, terminales portuarias y empresas proveedoras que dependen intensamente del agua y generan efluentes de composición compleja. El objetivo del capítulo es analizar, mediante una investigación teórica y documental, las condiciones necesarias para transitar hacia una gestión circular del agua en el corredor Coatzacoalcos-Minatitlán-Cosoleacaque. La revisión integra aportes sobre eficiencia, tratamiento avanzado, reúso, recuperación de recursos, simbiosis industrial y gobernanza territorial. Los resultados indican que la circularidad debe comenzar con balances verificables, prevención del consumo, segregación de corrientes y recirculación interna antes de desarrollar redes compartidas de agua regenerada. Las tecnologías biológicas, fisicoquímicas, de membrana y oxidación avanzada pueden producir agua para enfriamiento, generación de vapor y servicios industriales, pero requieren energía y generan lodos o concentrados que deben gestionarse. Se propone un modelo multiescalar basado en responsabilidad empresarial, infraestructura compartida, contratos de desempeño y verificación independiente de la sustitución de agua convencional. Se concluye que la economía circular puede fortalecer la competitividad y reducir la contaminación cuando conserva la rectoría pública y prioriza el abastecimiento humano y la protección de los ecosistemas.

items.title: The Urban Planning Structure of Romania's Administrative-Territorial Units: Legislative Framework, Professional Training, and Administrative Discrepancies
items.abstract: This study examines the urban planning structure of Romania's 3,181 basic administrative-territorial units, comparing national legislative requirements with administrative realities. The analysis traces the evolution of the legal framework, from Law no. 350/2001 on territorial planning and urbanism and Law no. 50/1991 on construction authorization, to the 2019 Administrative Code and the recent Code of Territorial Planning, Urbanism and Construction (CATUC), adopted in 2026. The study reviews legal requirements for planning documentation, including General Urban Plans and Zonal Urban Plans, as well as the professional qualification requirements imposed on chief architects and registered urban planners. Official data published by the Ministry of Development, Public Works and Administration, the National Institute of Statistics, the Romanian Court of Accounts, the World Bank, and the Order of Architects of Romania are analyzed. The study finds substantial discrepancies between legal requirements and administrative practice. The chief architect position was filled in only 0.66 percent of communes, compared with 52.4 percent of municipalities. Coverage with updated General Urban Plans remains, even in large cities, below one third of the sample analyzed. Authorization procedures averaged 507 days, nearly four times the national target of 135 days. Local budget self-financing capacity ranged from 82.5 percent in large cities to 27 percent in communes. The study documents profound rural-urban disparities in digitalization and administrative capacity. It recommends strengthening inter-communal planning structures, expanding continuing professional development, and prioritizing digitalization in rural areas. Keywords: Urban Planning, Territorial Planning, Administrative-Territorial Units, General Urban Plan, Chief Architect, Administrative Capacity, Legislative Reform, Rural-Urban Disparities

items.title: Circular Economy in the Reuse of Electronic Components Recovered from Printed Circuit Board Waste: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: Introduction: The growing generation of waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) and the potential value of printed circuit boards (PCBs) reinforce the need for recovery strategies aligned with the circular economy. Methodology: A Systematic Literature Review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020. The search was performed in Google Scholar between 1 and 8 August 2026, considering publications from 2012 to 2025 in Portuguese, Spanish, and English. Fifty records were identified and, after screening, eligibility assessment, and relevance analysis, 25 studies were included and qualitatively synthesized. Results: Thematic analysis showed a predominance of studies on circular economy, urban mining, and the transition to circular models (32%), followed by reverse logistics and WEEE management (20%), PCB material recycling and recovery (16%), and reuse, remanufacturing, and recovery (16%). The remaining studies addressed environmental impacts, management and operational support (12%) and public policy/PNRS (4%). Conclusions: The reviewed literature confirms the potential of WEEE and PCBs as secondary sources of materials and components. The main gap identified was the limited integration of disassembly, characterization, functional testing, classification, and direct component reuse. The development and validation of standardized procedures is therefore recommended.

items.title: Review of Nanotechnology-assisted E Waste Valorisation for Circular Economy Applications: Precious Metal Recovery and E-Plastic Upcycling
items.abstract: The escalating production of electronic waste is a major environmental and resource management problem globally. However, electronic waste is also a source of precious metals and polymeric materials, which can be recovered through circular economy approaches. In this review, recent progress in nanotechnology enabled approaches for electronic waste valorisation, including precious metal recovery and E plastic upcycling, is discussed. The use of magnetic nanoparticles, graphene nanomaterials, metal organic frameworks and nanocatalysts for selective metal extraction is presented, as well as novel methods for transforming E plastics into pyrolytic oils, carbon nanotubes and other high value added materials. It underlines the potential of these technologies to improve resource efficiency, mitigate environmental impacts and contribute to the development of sustainable urban mining. Major challenges such as scalability, economic viability and environmental safety will be discussed, as well as interesting avenues for the future potential integration of green nanotechnology and circular economy principles in sustainable electronic waste management.

items.title: Closing the Loop on Electronic Waste: Circular Economy Strategies for Sustainable E-Waste Management, Resource Recovery, and Hardware Repurposing in the Digital Age
items.abstract: In recent times, technological advancements in ICT have contributed immensely to the increasing production of e-waste, which is regarded as one of the fastest growing waste streams globally. In this chapter, a critical analysis will be provided on how circular economy approaches can be used to ensure sustainable e-waste management through resource recovery, recycling, and hardware repurposing in the digital era. Qualitative inter-disciplinary review of the literature that includes scientific sources, international documents, government policies, and industrial publications on e-waste are associated with health and environmental impacts of e-waste. The chapter will also address some circular economy solutions such as repair, reuse, refurbishment, remanufacturing, and repurposing to prolong the lifespan of e-products, as well as urban mining/resource recovery for recovering valuable secondary raw materials. Furthermore, the chapter will address policy actions that include Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) and Right to Repair (R2R).

items.title: Housing-service conditions and urban mining potential of single residential buildings: insights from material stock–flow analysis in the Philippines
items.abstract: Single residential buildings (SRBs) are a major component of housing, yet their material stocks and flows remain insufficiently quantified in data-scarce countries. This study applies a bottom-up dynamic material stock–flow analysis that integrates material intensities derived from construction documents, statistical data, and remote-sensing datasets for the Philippines from 2008 to 2023. Results show that the estimated annual inflows increased from 19 million metric tons (Mt) in 2009 to 34 Mt in 2023, while the estimated outflows increased from 4.7 to 5.6 Mt. Cumulative inflows and outflows reached 383 and 76 Mt, respectively, resulting in approximately 5921 Mt of in-use stock in 2023. In-use stocks were dominated by mineral- and masonry-based materials. Regional indicators also show that housing-service conditions of SRBs are multidimensional, reflecting distinct aspects of material concentration, population, dwelling-scale accumulation, and active occupancy, while stock-based urban mining assessment identified concrete, masonry materials, and metals as priority streams.

items.title: Reconfiguring urban mining: Orchestrating multi-actor E-waste supply chains for circular value recovery through an integrated DEMATEL–BWM–Agent-Based Modeling framework
Challenges and opportunities in modeling construction materials transportation at the metropolitan scale based on a material flow analysis
items.abstract: Construction is a major driver of resource consumption in cities and generates intermittent and substantial freight traffic with significant environmental and social impacts, yet it remains largely absent from metropolitan transport planning. Two bodies of research each address part of this problem. Urban metabolism and material flow studies quantify the materials a territory consumes, but these remain potential flows that are not expressed as vehicle movements on a network. Transport and logistics studies typically represent plannable flows at the tactical and operational levels, focusing on optimizing transportation for specific construction sites or material supply chains. This paper bridges these two perspectives by proposing a strategic modeling framework based on material flow analysis that converts building permit data into site-level material demand, supplier–site relationships, and truck flows assigned to the road network. In doing so, it brings urban metabolism to a more actionable level, turning material quantities into spatially explicit freight demand that planners can anticipate. The framework is applied to ready-mixed concrete for collective housing in the Strasbourg Metropolitan Area, using French open data on building permits and construction material statistics. A parametric analysis explores how spatial interaction parameters, transport efficiency, and the location of construction activity shape logistics outcomes. The results show that supplier proximity and transport efficiency mainly affect total vehicle-kilometers, while relocating construction activity can leave total vehicle-kilometers almost unchanged yet concentrate heavy-vehicle traffic in specific urban areas. Because it produces spatially disaggregated flows, the framework can support environmental impact assessments, exposure studies, and environmental justice analyses that aggregate vehicle-kilometer statistics cannot inform. Although data availability and quality still limit model va

items.title: THE EL-RAKHAWI THEORY OF SYMBIOTIC URBAN INTELLIGENCE AND REGENERATIVE INDUSTRIAL ECOSYSTEMS From Self-Healing Cities to the Sovereign Cognitive State A Unified Framework Integrating Regenerative Urban Metabolism, Digital Immune Systems, and Living Industrial Twins for the Next Generation of Sustainable Smart Nations
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.abstract: The El-Rakhawi Theory of Symbiotic Urban Intelligence and Regenerative Industrial Ecosystems (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23192881) integrates urban metabolism, sovereign digital governance, and precision manufacturing into a unified self-healing national ecosystem. Three pillars: (1) Regenerative Urban Metabolism with genetically engineered Bio-CCUS microorganisms featuring adaptive carbon absorption efficiency, transforming ports into carbon-negative hubs through waste heat valorization and circular water systems; (2) Sovereign Cognitive State Architecture with a Digital Immune System employing predictive AI, quantum-resistant communications, homomorphic encryption, and Federated Learning to ensure absolute industrial data sovereignty while enabling system-wide optimization; (3) Living Industrial Twins synchronized with urban infrastructure via Federated Learning, achieving zero-waste production and demand-responsive energy management. Introduces the Symbiotic Urban-Industrial Resilience Index (SUIRI) and Regenerative ROI metric (>1.0 within 7-10 years) as novel evaluation frameworks. Integrates organically with the El-Rakhawi Corpus on Quantum-Cognitive Convergence, Bio-Silicon Synergy, Cosmic Digital Sovereignty, and Symbiotic Bio-Intelligence. Released under Ferial Zayed Humanitarian License.

items.title: Raw materials and recycling
items.abstract: This chapter explores the central role of raw materials and recycling in achieving sustainable development within the framework of the UN 2030 Agenda, with particular reference to Sustainable Development Goal 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production). After introducing the fundamental concepts of primary and secondary raw materials, urban mining, resource efficiency, and circular economy, it analyzes global and European trends in raw material extraction, demand, and consumption. Particular attention is given to critical and strategic raw materials and their relevance for the green and digital transitions and the associated supply risks and policy responses developed at the European level. The chapter addresses waste management and recycling, discussing waste generation patterns, management hierarchies, and regulatory targets, and it then examines the structure of the recycling process, including advanced physical, mechanical, and sensor-based separation technologies. By linking material flows, policy frameworks, and technological solutions, the chapter highlights how recycling and circular strategies represent key enablers for long-term environmental sustainability, economic resilience, and climate neutrality.

items.title: The City and the Anthropocene
Performance Optimization of Sustainable Concrete Incorporating Silica Fume, Rice Husk Ash, and Recycled Electronic Wire Fibers
items.abstract: This study investigates the effects of silica fume (SF), a by-product of silicon and ferrosilicon production, rice husk ash (RHA), and waste electronic wire fibers (WEWF), recovered through urban mining of end-of-life electrical cables, on concrete performance incorporating natural coarse aggregate (NCA) and 100% recycled coarse aggregate (RCA), an abundant mineral residue. Ten mix formulations containing 0–1% WEWF by weight of ordinary Portland cement (OPC), in 0.25% increments, were evaluated using fresh, mechanical, durability, and nondestructive tests, including slump, compressive, splitting tensile and flexural strengths, water absorption, acid resistance, and ultrasonic pulse velocity (UPV). At 90 days, incorporating 0.75% WEWF increased compressive strength by 7.2% and 8.8% and reduced water absorption by 27.0% and 31.0% in NCA and RCA concrete, respectively. After 90 days of acid exposure, acid-induced mass loss decreased by 15.2% and 8.9%, respectively. Increasing WEWF to 1.0% further improved splitting tensile strength by 9.0% and 13.4% and flexural strength by 13.8% and 18.8%, although slump and UPV declined more substantially. These findings reveal a dosage-dependent trade-off between mechanical performance, durability, workability, and ultrasonic response. Overall, 0.75% WEWF provided the most balanced performance, whereas 1.0% preferentially enhanced tensile and flexural strengths, demonstrating the potential of electronic wire waste in sustainable recycled aggregate concrete. The findings support circular-economy strategies linking valorization of metallurgical by-products and e-waste, abundantly generated by respective industries, with sustainable construction materials.

items.title: Condition of historical materials, restoration scenarios cost comparison and environmental impact: case study from Võru, Estonia
items.venue: Journal of Cultural Heritage Management and Sustainable Development
items.abstract: Purpose To examine whether urban mining principles on the example of the historic building in the conservation area of Võru, Estonia can reduce embodied carbon/energy and cost feasibility, while respecting cultural heritage values. Design/methodology/approach During this study, visual, non-destructive inspection of structures and materials was conducted; volume estimates compiled; embodied carbon/energy using the Inventory of Carbon and Energy (henceforth ICE) values (A1–A3 system boundaries) calculated; three restoration cost scenarios aligned to Estonian standards (EVS, 2005) were compared to the Energy Performance of Buildings Directive (henceforth EPBD) recast. Destructive and non-destructive testing results of construction materials from the case study building are presented in previously published article. As project-specific Environmental Product Declarations (henceforth EPDs) were unavailable for the historic materials, generic ICE factors were used and affordability was approached through regional income data rather than homeowner surveys. Findings Many load-bearing log walls, roof timber and basement structures remain fit for continued use and are heritage-valuable. Avoiding their replacement corresponds to considerable savings of embodied carbon (∼46.7 tCO2e) and energy (∼437 GJ). The analysis of restoration scenarios shows that base living conditions achievement in historical buildings remains financially challenging to local inhabitants’ incomes, whereas conservation-first actions (rainwater system, plinth and façade repairs) are immediately affordable and heritage-compatible. Current study provides the holistic model for historical building preservation decision-making. The model consists of urban-mining-informed pre-design audits in conservation areas, and incentive schemes that recognise embodied-impact savings and phased renovation value. items.title: Calcium looping for post-combustion CO2 capture using sorbents derived from incineration ashes
Heavy Metal Contamination of Coal Mining Tailing Dumps: A Case Study of the Petrila Mining Site, Jiu Valley, Romania
items.abstract: The increasing demand for metals and the depletion of primary mineral resources have led to a growing interest in alternative sources of raw materials. In this context, mining waste deposits are increasingly considered as potential secondary resources within the concept of urban mining and the circular economy. Historical mining activities have generated large quantities of waste rock that can contain significant concentrations of valuable metals. The Petrila mine tailings dump, located in the Jiu Valley coal basin (Hunedoara County, Romania), includes such a deposit, where millions of tons of mining waste have accumulated over decades of mining. The tailings dump occupies an area of approximately 225,201 m² and constitutes an important anthropogenic deposit with potential resource value. The objective of this study was to characterize the chemical composition of residual materials from the tailings dumps of the Petrila mine and to evaluate their potential as secondary resources for metal recovery potential, in urban mining zone. Sampling was carried out at several locations in the tailings heap, at depths of approximately 30 cm , 50 cm and 70 cm, to investigate the distribution of metals within the deposit of tailing dumps. Elemental concentrations were determined using inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP - OES). In addition, X - ray fluorescence (XRF) analysis was performed to determine the majority oxide composition of the samples and to support the geochemical characterization of the tailings material. XRF analyses show that the tailings material is dominated by silicate phases, with SiO ₂ concentrations ranging from approximately 42 to 65 wt % and Al₂O₃ concentrations ranging from approximately 15 to 24 wt %. Iron oxides are also significant, with Fe₂O₃ values reaching up to about 17% by weight, while TiO₂ concentrations range between about 1.2 and 2.4% by weight. items.title: Enabling technologies and methods for the smart recycling sector in the Industry 5.0 era
Urban metabolic performance and spatiotemporal evolution in central Beijing: a community-scale emergy accounting study
items.abstract: Introduction Urban areas are central to resource consumption and carbon emissions, yet community-scale metabolic mechanisms remain underexplored, particularly when green-space ecosystem services are incorporated into emergy accounting. Methods Taking the 305.8 km 2 central area of Beijing as a case and communities as analytical units, this study develops a community-scale emergy accounting framework for 2011, 2014, 2017, and 2020. Green-space carbon sequestration and oxygen release are included as explicit output emergy. Results Emergy per area (EPA) was high and spatially uneven. Emergy per capita (EPP) was higher in 2020 than in 2011 in most communities, and its spatial disparities narrowed. The emergy yield ratio (EYR) remained below 1. The environmental loading ratio (ELR) rose from mostly 3-10 in 2011 to above 10 in many communities by 2020, and the environmental sustainability index (ESI) remained below 1. Within this accounting framework, expanding green space within community boundaries can only marginally improve the direct accounted output emergy and cannot raise ESI above 1; the limiting factor is the renewable fraction of external supporting flows. With only four observation years, these temporal changes cannot be attributed to specific policies as opposed to interannual fluctuations. Discussion Differentiated community governance should prioritize energy-efficiency retrofits and circular economy pilots in low-EYR areas, functional green infrastructure in high-ELR areas, and, more fundamentally, an increase in the renewable fraction of external supporting flows. The study advances community-scale urban metabolism accounting for SDG 11 while highlighting boundary, data, and methodological limitations.

items.title: Unmodified Kraft lignin and humic acids as biowaste-derived sorbents for selective gold and palladium uptake from acidic e-waste leachates
items.abstract: The management of waste electrical and electronic equipment (e-waste) is a major challenge and an opportunity to recover critical raw materials and precious metals from printed circuit boards (PCBs). Herein, we propose unmodified, low-cost biowastes as sustainable sorbents to recover gold and palladium from HCl-based hydrometallurgical PCB leachates. Kraft lignin (KL), a pulp and paper by-product, and humic acids (VV) from municipal compost were selected as representative industrial and urban aromatic waste streams. Metal uptake was investigated across HCl concentrations (0.0001–1 M) and temperatures (25–70 °C) to identify optimal conditions and elucidate the underlying mechanisms. Both materials captured and reduced noble metal ions without prior chemical modification, while showing negligible Cu 2+ uptake in model Au-Cu and Pd-Cu systems, with selectivity exceeding 99.9%. FT-IR, TEM and XRD analyses provided evidence of interactions of metal ions with oxygen-containing functional groups and metallic nanocluster formation, particularly Au 0 . The results highlighted the role of pH- and temperature-dependent structural reorganization of biowastes (BWs) in governing metal uptake. These biosorbents were also tested in real, strongly acidic e-waste hydrometallurgical leachates from PCB components and automotive catalytic converters, demonstrating their ability to capture noble metals in complex multimetallic matrices. Furthermore, thermal treatment of the metal-loaded biowastes at 650 °C yielded solid residues containing crystalline metallic gold (Au 0 ) and palladium oxide (PdO), providing a preliminary demonstration of metal recovery without any intermediate chemical elution step. This study provides a proof of concept for integrating biowaste valorisation and precious-metal recovery within a circular-economy framework for urban mining.

items.title: Assessment of adhesion and durability of laminated safety glass made from end-of-life float glass
items.abstract: As part of urban mining initiatives aimed at reducing waste, CO 2 emissions and the extraction of raw materials, the demand for sustainable resource recovery and repurposing of construction materials is growing. With many European buildings due to be renovated to meet current energy standards, recovering insulating glass units (IGUs) presents a valuable opportunity to reclaim significant amounts of glass panes while reducing environmental impact of glass facades. However, the outer surfaces of IGUs are especially exposed to environmental influences, such as weathering and mechanical impacts, which may introduce surface defects or changes to the glass surface composition, such as corrosion. These phenomena may affect the processability and remanufacturing processes. This study evaluates the feasibility of producing laminated safety glass (LSG) from reclaimed insulating glass units (IGUs). First the surface roughness is analyzed to evaluate environmental exposure of the glass surfaces. Next, laminated glass, with a new PVB interlayer, is manufactured using two configurations of the glass surfaces, primarily with the reclaimed glass, to determine the effect of natural aging, positioning, and combinations on its adhesion performance tested under temperature and humidity conditions in accordance with EN ISO 12543-4, as well as under mechanical loads in the pummel tests. Comparative tests are also conducted with LSG made entirely from new glass. The results demonstrate the possibility of producing standard-compliant LSG from reclaimed float glass.

items.title: METABOLISMO URBANO Y MATERIALES EN LA CONSTRUCCIÓN DE VIVIENDA: Un estudio en tres ciudades intermedias de Colombia
items.venue: Seminario Internacional de Investigación en Urbanismo (SIIU)
items.abstract: Housing construction is one of the main activities generating environmental impacts, due to the high consumption of materials and CO2 emissions. This study analyzes the urban metabolism in three intermediate Colombian cities, evaluating the flows of materials most used in construction and their environmental effects. It is hypothesized that it is possible to identify patterns in the use of materials to optimize their management and mitigate negative impacts. The study considered the period 2015–2020 and selected urban expansion areas through cartographic analysis and specific criteria. The dwellings were classified according to the homogeneity of their materials and structural complexity. A census was conducted in homogeneous dwellings and an adapted ecological sampling in heterogeneous ones. Through field visits, apparent materials and their sources of origin were identified, complemented with Life Cycle Analysis to evaluate CO2 emissions. The results show that reinforced concrete, fired brick and glass predominate in construction, varying according to the type of housing. These findings allow us to formulate strategies to reduce impacts and promote urban sustainability.

items.title: The value of impurity. The second life of WEEE-derived yttrium in the pharmaceutical industry
items.abstract: Among the strategic raw materials supporting today's digital and energy transition, rare earth elements (REE) pose increasing geopolitical and industrial-economic challenges. Urban mining offers a promising alternative, although the high energy costs associated with recycling remain a significant obstacle. This paper investigates the technical feasibility and economic viability of processes for obtaining secondary materials of lower purity. As an illustrative case study, we analysed the recovery of triflate-yttrium from a mixture of e-waste containing yttrium oxide at varying concentrations; the resulting material can be used in pharmaceutical applications. The study evaluates the economic efficiency and recycling effectiveness, achieving medium-to-high purities under economically viable conditions. These results demonstrate that the tested method can support circular processes in the e-waste chain at lower costs than market prices for high-purity raw material oxides used in the pharmaceutical sector, making the production of secondary raw materials preferable to the production of virgin raw materials derived from extraction processes with high environmental and social impact on the territories.
