items.title: Environmental sensing-based assessment of trees outside forests and land use and land cover change patterns in the Bundelkhand agroforestry landscape
items.abstract: This study assesses land use and land cover (LULC) dynamics and Trees Outside Forests (TOF) in Lalitpur district, Uttar Pradesh, within the semi-arid Bundelkhand landscape. The study addresses the need to distinguish tree resources occurring outside officially defined forest areas from conventional LULC classes and to examine their spatial significance for land management. Landsat imagery was used to produce LULC maps for 2015, 2020 and 2025 using supervised Maximum Likelihood Classification (MLC), while high-resolution canopy-height data were used to derive total tree cover. A one-hectare circular neighbourhood and a 10% canopy-density threshold were then used to identify forest areas according to the operational framework applied from the Forest Survey of India (FSI), and TOF was estimated as tree cover outside that forest mask. The reported LULC results show an increase in agricultural area from 2,351.29 km² (47%) excluding the drought fallow land (1440 sq km) in 2015 to 3,776.26 km² (74%) in 2020, followed by 3,704.66 km² (72%) in 2025, while open forest declined from 1,383.43 km² (27%) to 417.97 km² (8%). The Forest & tree-cover assessment estimated 203,969 ha (40.34%) of tree cover, of which 63,697 ha (12.60%) met the applied forest-density criterion and 140,272 ha (27.74%) were classified as TOF. These findings indicate that a substantial share of mapped tree cover occurs outside the FSI-defined forest category. The combined LULC and TOF framework provides a spatial basis for agroforestry planning and sustainable land management, while the limitations of MLC, the canopy-height threshold, and the available validation information should be considered when interpreting the estimates.

items.title: Unlocking the Selective Extraction and Direct Reduction of Gold From E‐Waste Leachate Through Robust Bismuth‐Based Metal–Organic Frameworks
items.abstract: The rapid increase in electronic waste (e-waste) and the growing demand for rare metals underline the urgent need for effective technologies to recover valuable elements such as gold from waste, a process known as urban mining. However, the development of sustainable and cost-effective adsorbents with high capacity and selectivity remains challenging. Here, two novel bioinspired bismuth metal-organic frameworks using the edible polyphenolic ellagic and gallic acids as building blocks, namely, bismuth-ellagate (Bi-EA) and bismuth-gallate (Bi-GA), are synthesized to evaluate for gold extraction from various matrices, including river water, seawater, and leaching solutions from computer central processing units (CPUs). Both chemically stable bismuth-based metal-organic frameworks (bioMOFs) exhibit an ultrahigh adsorption capacity (2989.9 mg/g for Bi-EA and 2516.3 mg/g for Bi-GA), with high Au3+ removal efficiency (> 99%) within 10 min, high selectivity, and recyclability. The excellent gold recovery performance is attributed to the adsorption-reduction mechanism resulting from the phenolic hydroxyl groups in these frameworks. This work provides a sustainable and cost-effective method for gold recovery with superior efficiency and environmental compatibility compared to existing technologies, thus contributing to the sustainable management of gold resources.

items.title: Biotechnological Advances in Biorecovery of Precious Metals from Electronic Scraps
Toward integrated urban sustainability assessment: a structured review and classification of indicator frameworks and integrated approaches
items.abstract: Urbanization is a primary driver reshaping global socioeconomic and environmental systems, highlighting the need, particularly in the context of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), to develop robust tools for the evaluation of urban sustainability. This structured literature review of urban sustainability indicators initially identified 419 Scopus® records; screening and supplementary searches yielded 43 sources for the final synthesis, classified into three main categories: i) single and composite indicators, which are flexible but often lack comparability; ii) frameworks based on the SDGs, frequently adopted as classificatory rather than operational assessment tools; iii) approaches based on flows and impacts such as Material Flow Analysis (MFA), Urban Metabolism (UM) and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). Unlike previous reviews, which typically addressed only one methodological perspective, the current study compares these three methodological paradigms, evaluating their integration opportunities, limitations, and operational role. The results highlighted a significant gap between indicator-based and impact-based approaches, while the MFA–LCA integration remains insufficiently developed. Based on literature data, a focused sub-analysis of ten studies highlighted frequent attention to transportation, energy, and construction materials. Given the heterogeneous landscape of urban sustainability tools, the review provides a qualitative decision-support matrix to help urban professionals and policymakers select and combine assessment approaches according to their objectives, data availability, expertise, and implementation capacity. The study contributes by proposing a structured typology of indicators and identifying UM–LCA integration as a promising flow- and impact-assessment component within broader hybrid urban sustainability frameworks.
cites_core: Circular economy in cities: Reviewing how environmental research aligns with local practices

items.title: An Intelligent and Highly Autonomous Robotic Cell for Electronic Waste Dismantling and Extraction of REE-Bearing Components: A Hoverboard Case Study
items.abstract: The exponential growth of electronic waste and the demand for Rare Earth Elements require transitioning from manual dismantling to automated urban mining. Current robotic systems often address perception and manipulation as isolated tasks, limiting their applicability in real-world recycling. This article proposes a highly autonomous, multimodal robotic cell integrating active perception, force-controlled manipulation, autonomous tool changing, task verification, and Human-Robot Collaboration for the extraction of REE-bearing components from hoverboards. Building upon previously validated methods, the primary novelty lies in their system-level integration within a unified product-level disassembly cell. The framework combines deep learning, zero-shot segmentation, and Next-Best-View refinement to localize occluded components, while hybrid force-control algorithms provide tactile feedback for adaptive drilling, unscrewing, and handling. Proof-of-concept benchmarking on hoverboards shows most individual task success rates above 90%. However, rotor-stator extraction in rubber-lined and toothed designs (67–71% success) required collaborative fallbacks. A complete end-to-end execution on one hoverboard half was successful, with two collaborative recoveries, both caused by failed screw removal by drilling, besides the planned cable cutting. The robotic cell dismantles a half-unit in ≈ 12–14 min, compared with ≈ 8 min for industrial manual dismantling of the same half-unit, an approximately 50–75% longer cycle time. In exchange, it performs the motor separation (150–260 N magnetic retention forces) without manual handling, reduces exposure to hazardous substances, and provides repeatable sub-millimeter localization. Proof-of-concept experiments on hard disk drives and electric scooters indicate that the strategies can be applied to other WEEE products, although broader validation is required.

items.title: EVALUATING THE ROLE OF URBAN DESIGN TOOLS IN ENHANCING ENERGY EFFICIENCY IN HIGH-DENSITY URBAN DEVELOPMENTS: INSIGHTS FROM LAGOS METROPOLIS
items.venue: International Journal of Environmental Research and Earth Science
items.abstract: Urbanisation in Lagos Metropolis has increased the rate of creating high-density urban centres, thus aggravating energy demands and environmental pressures. It is in this paper that we have evaluated how urban design tools can help to reduce energy use in high-density developments in Lagos. With the Compact City Theory, Sustainable Urban Development Theory, Urban Metabolism Theory and Climate-Responsive Urban Design Theory, we used a descriptive and analytic design and preferred quantitative approaches in a mixed-method approach. The data were collected in the form of structured questionnaires filled by 384 participants, with the supplement of the information by the direct observation and GIS-based spatial analysis of the three purposely chosen high-density districts, Victoria Island, Ikeja GRA, and Surulere. The results demonstrate that mixed-use development, compact-city ideologies, passive design approaches, the street orientation, and green infrastructure have a positive effect on energy efficiency. Victoria Island was a study that proved to be a model region that has been able to adopt design tools more than Surulere and Ikeja GRA, especially using green infrastructure and orientational planning. The results of statistical analyses showed strong, positive correlations between the urban design features and the lower energy consumption, which were supported by the results of spatial overlays, which display favourable morphological patterns. The paper concludes that energy efficiency in Lagos can be significantly enhanced by imposing energy-conscious urban design tools in planning policies and development guidelines. We would, therefore, suggest changes to the regulatory framework, the imposition of the design standards and the enhancement of the capacity-building programmes of urban planners and architects. The results are relevant to evidence-based urban planning and the sustainable development strategy of tropical megacities.

items.title: Rethinking sustainable urban planning in the Global South: six paradigm shifts for the next decade
items.abstract: Cities across the Global South are entering a decisive decade for sustainable development.Rapid urbanization and intensifying climate change are placing growing pressure on urban sustainability, increasing environmental risks while challenging cities' social, economic, and infrastructural systems (Almulhim & Cobbinah, 2026;UN-Habitat, 2024). These pressures are unfolding alongside widening socio-spatial inequalities, infrastructure and resource constraints, and profound technological and economic change, with climate impacts often falling disproportionately on vulnerable and marginalized urban populations (UN-Habitat, 2024).Climate-induced migration adds another layer of complexity, as environmental stress can accelerate rural-to-urban mobility, placing additional pressure on infrastructure, services, and informal and peri-urban development in receiving cities (Almulhim et al., 2024). These pressures do not occur independently. They interact within increasingly complex urban systems, where decisions about land use, housing, mobility, infrastructure, ecosystems, and public services can generate consequences far beyond the sectors in which they originate. The significance of these interactions also extends beyond city boundaries, as urban growth increasingly shapes land cover, hydrological systems, climate, biogeochemical processes, and habitats at broader scales (Espey et al., 2024).Although the term Global South encompasses highly diverse urban contexts and should not imply a single development trajectory, the nature and intensity of urban challenges vary considerably across regions, from rapid urban expansion and informality to housing pressures, climate vulnerability, displacement, and resource scarcity (United Nations, 2026). items.title: Beyond waste management: high-leverage transition pathways for circular construction across the building lifecycle in the UAE
items.abstract: Purpose Despite ambitious national circular economy (CE) and net-zero commitments, CE implementation in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) construction sector remains fragmented and predominantly compliance-driven, with practice largely centered on construction and demolition waste management rather than lifecycle value retention. This study investigates the implementation determinants that shape circular construction across the building lifecycle and identifies high-leverage governance interventions capable of translating policy ambition into lifecycle-integrated project delivery. Design/methodology/approach A sequential mixed-methods design was employed. A systematic literature review developed a preliminary implementation determinant framework, which were subsequently refined and contextualized through semi-structured interviews with 20 UAE construction experts. The validated determinants were prioritized using integrated best–worst method (BWM) and fuzzy TOPSIS to identify the governance interventions offering the greatest leverage for lifecycle-integrated circular construction. Findings The findings indicate that although circularity is increasingly recognized across the UAE building lifecycle, implementation remains concentrated on downstream waste management and recycling, with higher-value circular strategies rarely sustained beyond the design stage. The integrated prioritization identifies regulatory coherence and financial de-risking as the principal governance levers, supported by contractual embedding, early stakeholder engagement and digital traceability. Collectively, these interventions form a sequence of high-leverage transition pathways that strengthen lifecycle continuity and improve material value retention. items.title: Advancing Circular Economy Innovation: A Multi‐Criteria Tool for Evaluating Construction Materials
items.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
items.abstract: The construction industry is a major consumer of raw materials and a significant contributor to environmental impacts, highlighting the importance of circular material selection. This study presents a structured framework for assessing construction materials based on circular economy (CE) criteria to support informed and transparent decision‐making. A three‐phase methodology was adopted, comprising criteria prioritisation, rubric development and validation, and material‐level assessment using evidence from peer‐reviewed literature. Eleven CE criteria were weighted through expert judgement and applied using a validated multi‐criteria rubric to evaluate 10 commonly used construction materials. The findings reveal clear variation in circular performance across materials. Cross‐Laminated Timber achieved the highest overall weighted circularity score (4.15), driven by strong performance in reusability, non‐toxic properties, and embodied carbon, while conventional materials such as PVC pipes recorded the lowest score (2.80), primarily due to poor reusability and disassembly performance despite high availability and market maturity. These results demonstrate that end‐of‐life value retention and lifecycle circularity are more influential than market‐driven factors in determining material circularity. The proposed assessment framework offers a robust and evidence‐based tool for circular material selection in the construction industry.

items.title: Women, Urban Food Practices, and Circular Economies of Care: A Korean Example of Degrowth in Seoul
items.venue: Social Politics International Studies in Gender State & Society
items.abstract: Urban agricultural practices are a form of community care and play a central role in connecting and expanding the functions of food production, distribution, collectivized consumption, and recycling, thereby providing important sociospatial infrastructure. Localized urban food circulation systems are practices of commoning care and, aligned with ideas of degrowth, can revitalize local economies and communities. They therefore emerge as alternatives to counter ecological and environmental problems such as ecosystem preservation, biodiversity, local food systems, and resource circulation in an era of climate crisis. Furthermore, this social infrastructure provides a caring framework that sustains local communities in the face of ongoing urbanization. This article examines the implications of women-led ecological and communal spaces in relation to concepts of commoning, degrowth, and local circular care economies, focusing on a food network in southern Seoul, and considers the challenges and constraints faced by women actors in developing and sustaining these practices.

items.title: From Sensing to Transforming: An AI-Enabled Capability Framework for Circular Construction and Demolition Waste Management
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and AI-enabled digital technologies are increasingly proposed as enablers of circularity in construction and demolition (C&D) waste management, yet existing reviews are organised around technology and lifecycle stage and rarely examine the organisational conditions under which technically capable applications move from pilot to sustained practice. This review addresses that gap through a PRISMA 2020-guided systematic review of 217 recent Scopus records (2022–2026), interpreted through dynamic capabilities theory, diffusion of innovation theory, and the circular economy value-retention hierarchy. Abstract-level coding of capability enablers, AI mechanism clusters, and circularity outcomes is triangulated with latent Dirichlet allocation topic modelling, bibliographic coupling, co-citation and keyword co-occurrence analyses, and statistical tests of association. The central finding concerns where research attention has concentrated: digital infrastructure and AI/machine learning technical capability appear in 64–67% of studies, whereas governance and human/organisational capability appear in only 13–18%, and traceability/material security is the least-examined outcome (11.1%). These patterns describe the published literature rather than organisational practice. They are integrated into a four-layer framework that separates observed associations from theoretical inferences, and into six propositions for organisational-level testing. Substantive policy instruments appear in only 4.1% of studies, so the policy implications are presented as exploratory.

items.title: Circular economy assessment of biomethane value chain in Brazil
items.abstract: From the numerous opportunities to add value to biomass in Brazil, biomethane production in sugarcane mills presents significant potential. This study introduces a diagnostic framework grounded in circular economy (CE) principles to assess new biomethane projects, aligning with the strategic objectives of product diversification, full biomass utilization, circularity, and regional integration. By adopting seven CE principles to qualitatively and quantitatively evaluate systemic impacts, the assessment provides a flexible tool for visualizing and testing alternative biorefinery configurations during the feasibility stage. The framework is applied to two real‐world scenarios: (i) the on‐site replacement of diesel in agricultural and transport operations; and (ii) the regional commercialization of biomethane via pipeline to substitute industrial liquefied petroleum gas (LPG). Results indicate that both pathways achieve over 85% reduction in carbon intensity compared with fossil benchmarks, while simultaneously enhancing nutrient cycling and soil regeneration through improved digestate application. The CE‐based assessment further demonstrates that on‐site utilization fosters internal transactional efficiency and operational control, whereas regional distribution extends defossilization benefits throughout the broader industrial value chain. The framework facilitates strategic decision‐making by capturing dimensions of value retention, regeneration, and stakeholder collaboration within bio‐based systems. This approach serves as a replicable and complementary tool for evaluating diverse bioeconomy contexts, supporting the transition toward more circular and resilient regional systems.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Waste Generation Patterns and Circular Economy Potential in Two Coastal Protected Areas of the Yucatán Peninsula
items.abstract: Inadequate waste disposal in ecologically sensitive reserves threatens biodiversity and water quality, which highlights the urgent need for localized waste management strategies. This study provides a comparative assessment of municipal solid waste generation, its composition, and circular economy potential within two coastal protected areas of the Yucatán Peninsula, such as Isla Arena in Campeche and San Crisanto in Yucatán. Testing the hypothesis that local economic practices dictate waste trajectories, the research integrated a systematic 6-to-7-day household waste characterization study with community surveys, utilizing non-parametric statistical methods. Marked differences were identified between the two communities, with San Crisanto exhibiting a notably higher per capita waste generation rate compared to Isla Arena (0.98 versus 0.25 kg/day). Distinct compositional profiles also emerged for each site, characterized by a predominance of food waste in San Crisanto and a greater prevalence of non-recoverable materials in Isla Arena. The findings underscore the context dependency of solid waste challenges in protected marine–terrestrial interfaces, demonstrating that effective circular economy interventions must reject generic paradigms in favor of strategies calibrated to localized dominance profiles.

items.title: Barriers to Manufactured Sand Adoption in India’s Construction Industry: a STEEPLE-based Assessment for Advancing Circular Economy and Sustainable Resource Management
The Lean-Circular Transition in Morocco: Evidence from the Manufacturing and Construction Sectors
items.venue: International Journal of Strategic Management and Economic Studies (IJSMES)
items.abstract: The depletion of natural resources and growing environmental pressure have prompted interest in linking Lean management and the circular economy as complementary approaches to sustainable industrial transformation. This article offers a narrative review of the literature on how both paradigms interact, with particular attention to the Moroccan context, an angle still scarcely explored in the specialised literature. It examines the synergy mechanisms, enabling conditions, barriers and performance outcomes documented in recent studies on Moroccan manufacturing and construction SMEs. The review shows that Lean tools such as value stream mapping and 5S frequently serve as operational foundations for implementing circular economy principles. Persistent tensions are also identified, among them the risk of a narrow interpretation of Lean, which may constrain the systemic thinking that genuine circularity requires. The Moroccan evidence reveals that small and medium-sized enterprises increasingly draw on Circular Lean Six Sigma 4.0 and Lean Construction practices, although institutional barriers, particularly around public procurement governance, continue to constrain their translation into sustained circular outcomes. The synergy between Lean and the circular economy holds considerable potential, whose realisation requires rethinking Lean from a broader value-retention perspective, adapted to Morocco's institutional conditions.

items.title: Offsite construction for sustainable building delivery: benefits, challenges and future directions
items.abstract: The construction industry faces increasing pressure to mitigate its global carbon footprint, reduce resource consumption, and minimize landfilled material waste. Offsite construction (OSC) has emerged as an industrialized paradigm capable of restructuring traditional project delivery. This paper presents a critical literature review of 19 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2020 and 2026. The objective is to synthesize the environmental benefits, assess the circular economy potential, and identify the supply chain and digital challenges of offsite building delivery. Results demonstrate that modular and industrialized building systems achieve substantial waste reductions, reaching up to 83.2% in weight and up to 78.8% on average across analyzed building projects. Furthermore, comparative life cycle assessments (LCAs) indicate greenhouse gas (GHG) reductions of approximately 8% under typical logistics configurations, with transport thresholds identified around 120km. Incorporating circular principles, such as Design for Disassembly (DfD), can further reduce global warming potential by up to 63% compared to linear offsite options. However, digital integration remains fragmented, with limited deployment of automated digital twins or artificial intelligence (AI). Moreover, widespread adoption is hindered by high upfront capital costs, design-stage constraints, and logistics complexities. We conclude that offsite construction represents an effective sustainable delivery pathway when combined with circular design frameworks, optimized localized supply chains, and integrated digital workflows.

items.title: From Material Recovery to Circular Valorization in Construction and Demolition Waste Management: Evidence and a Circular Valorization Framework from a Brazilian Recycling Facility
items.abstract: Construction and Demolition Waste (CDW) recycling is essential for circular economy strategies, yet material recovery alone does not demonstrate effective circular valorization. This study investigates how a CDW recycling facility can progress from conventional waste recovery toward measurable, traceable, and sustainability-oriented circular resource management. An exploratory-descriptive single-case study was conducted in Porto Rico, Paraná, Brazil, based on systematic direct observation and documentary, operational, and commercialization records. The facility processes approximately 24 000 t of CDW annually, converting concrete and brick waste into recycled gravel, wood into chips for thermal energy applications, and redirecting other recyclable fractions to external recovery chains. Commercialization data for 2022–2023 showed a 5.2% decrease in recycled-gravel sales and a 310.3% increase in other recovered-material volumes, although substantial temporal concentration and variability were observed. The findings reveal circularity gaps related to incomplete material-flow measurement, aggregated records, limited material characterization, market continuity, traceability, and information integration. These results demonstrate that circular performance depends not only on material recovery but also on material quality, value retention, market reinsertion, and measurable resource flows. Based on these empirical gaps, an empirically grounded, case-derived Circular CDW Valorization Framework and a Circular Performance Measurement Architecture are proposed, linking material-flow measurement, material quality, value retention, market development, sustainability indicators, and targeted digital enablement. The study advances the distinction between circular practices and circular performance and provides a structured pathway from waste diversion and material recovery toward measurable and traceable circular resource management.

items.title: Pathways to circular and regenerative urban agriculture through stakeholder-informed approaches
items.abstract: Conventional agriculture typically relies on linear production systems that degrade soil and undermine sustainable resource management and contribute to climate change. Urban and peri-urban agriculture can facilitate the closure of nutrient loops left open in conventional systems, as its proximity to nutrient rich residues and waste provides a local supply for nutrient recovery and reincorporation into agricultural soils. Realizing this shift requires systemically restructuring how food, waste, and land are governed. This study applies the Three Horizons framework to structure stakeholder discussions across present conditions, emerging opportunities, and desired futures. Using grounded theory qualitative analysis, our study inductively derives seven cross-sectoral themes alongside barriers, stakeholder actions, and transformation pathways for advancing healthy soils and sustainable urban and peri-urban agriculture through carbon and nutrient circularity. Our results demonstrate the need for distributed leadership and intersectoral collaboration to enable circular practices such as decentralized and proximity-based waste management, community-led agricultural food networks, and environmental stewardship through procurement and land policy. These actions converge into three interlinking pathways that scale circularity and address system complexity: 1) localized material and knowledge flows; 2) socio-economic reconfiguration through communities and markets; and 3) policy and planning integration for resilience. These findings highlight that advancing circularity requires not only technical innovation but also participatory governance, market realignment, and regulatory adaptation. By integrating stakeholder perspectives into transformation design, the results demonstrate how a transformation to healthy soils for sustainable urban and peri-urban agriculture can be positioned as foundational infrastructure for regenerative urban and regional futures.

items.title: Embedding Circularity in Conceptual Building Design: A Functional Framework for Data-Driven Decisions during the Earliest Architectural Design Stages
items.venue: SpringerBriefs in applied sciences and technology
items.abstract: Circularity in the built environment is ultimately a design governance challenge rather than a purely technical one. While methodological support is increasingly available, its effectiveness depends on the capacity of project stakeholders to align early-stage decisions with long-term value retention, data continuity, and recovery infrastructures. In this context, the transition toward circular building design requires not only improved tools, but also institutional integration across design, procurement, and regulatory systems, enabling circular criteria to become embedded as standard design constraints rather than optional sustainability objectives. The coming convergence of digitalization, such as BIM and digital product passports, together with lifecycle regulation, and performance-based assessment frameworks will likely redefine the role of the conceptual design phase as a decision environment where circularity is operationalized, verified, and governed from the outset. Consequently, the advancement of circular architecture will depend less on the development of new isolated instruments and more on the systematic integration of existing knowledge into coherent, enforceable, and practice-oriented design processes, capable of bridging the gap between circular economy ambition and built reality.

items.title: A Hybrid Raytracing and Deep Learning-Based Approach for Single-Site Localization of Radio Emitters in Urban Environment
items.abstract: Efficient passive radio monitoring in dense urban areas is obstructed by multipath propagation and NLOS conditions, causing conventional single-site localization methods to suffer from compounding geometric errors and sparse data availability. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a novel hybrid framework that fuses physics-based wave propagation geometry with data-driven machine learning. The proposed methodology utilizes an advanced, Circulant Modified MUSIC (CM-MUSIC) algorithm to reliably resolve highly correlated wave components on a 5-element Uniform Circular Arrays (UCA) antenna. The extracted directional inputs are processed via a backward raytracing engine to generate a continuous spatial likelihood map, which is then filtered by a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained as a sector semantic mask. Empirical field validation using a low-cost Software Defined Radio (SDR) platform capturing analog FM transmissions demonstrated high tracking precision and robust noise immunity under severe spatial constraints, while an ideal sector-classification scenario analysis confirmed that the proposed framework closely converges to the theoretical accuracy limits of the geometric model. This framework provides a scalable, highly cost-effective, and hardware-preserving single-site solution for modern civilian radio spectrum regulatory enforcement.

items.title: Circular potential of insulating glass units—a sensitivity study on life cycle impact assessment
items.abstract: Creating closed material loops through value-retention processes is essential for circular economy (CE) strategies in construction, particularly for energy-intensive materials such as glass in insulating glass units (IGUs). In practice, IGUs are often demolished with a façade and treated as mixed construction-and-demolition waste, causing material dissipation and avoidable environmental burdens. Although circular approaches for IGUs are emerging, comparative life cycle impact assessments (LCIA) across realistic system boundaries and disassembly practices remain scarce due to construction diversity, limited data availability, and uncertainties in disassembly processes. This study addresses this gap by providing reproducible LCIAs of promising IGU end-of-life (EoL) scenarios based on ecoinvent data and literature. Prospective scenarios for treating obsolete IGUs and processing components into triple IGUs resemble a "grave-to-gate" phase beyond an IGU's first life. This phase incorporates sequences of disassembly, quality assessment, transport and secondary manufacturing to quantify the Global Warming Potential of the scenarios in kg CO2-equivalent per square meter of triple IGU. Modelling approaches include best practice assumptions and scenario-based material flows. Results show promising potential for reducing the impact of triple IGUs through remanufacturing. Sensitivity analyses were conducted for transport and process parameters. The results show that the acceptance rate during qualification is the most important parameter for sustainable pathways. The transport analysis indicates that qualification and disassembly should be located close to the dismantling process where possible. This study's results contribute to data-driven selection of sustainable pathways and to understanding the relevance of future research topics in circularity of architectural glass.

items.title: Localized Thermal Energy Harvesting and Continuous Circular Flow Stability Control for Surface Heat Mitigation and Decentralized Power Generation: Mathematical Modeling, Simulation, ESP32–TEG Instrumentation, and Product Architecture (G-THRM Series)
authors: Adv. Sanjay Vidya Vijay Gurav Sanjay
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.abstract: Localized Thermal Energy Harvesting and Continuous Circular Flow Stability Control for Surface Heat Mitigation and Decentralized Power Generation: Mathematical Modeling, Simulation, ESP32–TEG Instrumentation, and Product Architecture (G-THRM Series) AUTHOR: Adv. Sanjay Vidya Vijay Gurav Independent Researcher & Advocate, Mumbai–Thane Metropolitan Region, Maharashtra, India ABSTRACT Rising surface temperatures, urban heat island (UHI) intensification, and localized waste heat accumulation represent critical thermal and energy management challenges. This bilingual (English–Marathi) research paper introduces an integrated thermodynamic, control-theoretic, and techno-economic framework for harvesting localized surface and industrial heat into decentralized electrical power while actively stabilizing surface temperature through Gurav’s Continuous Circular Flow & Stability Framework (GCCFS). An energy-balance ordinary differential equation (ODE) model is formulated over a total surface area A_total with deployment density rho in [0, 1] (A_h = rho * A_total), accounting for solar absorptivity, convective and Stefan–Boltzmann radiative heat transfer, Carnot-bounded thermoelectric conversion (eta_th(t) = eta_rel * max(0, 1 - T_sink(t)/T_s(t))), and proportional GCCFS thermal feedback stabilization u_GCCFS(t) = K_GCCFS * max(0, T_s(t) - T_target). Using 24-hour SciPy (solve_ivp) numerical simulations and sensitivity evaluations across rho in {0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75}, the study quantifies peak surface temperature reduction, daily electrical yield (kWh/day), capital expenditure (CapEx), and simple payback period, establishing phased rollout and high-delta-T hotspot prioritization strategies. Furthermore, the paper specifies a reproducible ESP32–TEG hardware testbed incorporating dual DS18B20 probes (delta_T = T_h - T_c), an INA219 power monitor, and LittleFS CSV telemetry (thermal_teg_log.csv), alongside five modular product architectures (G-THRM-PAVE-01 through G-THRM-HYB-05)

items.title: Invisible Sustainability: Gendered Circular Resource Practices and Household Climate Resilience in Rural Bangladesh
items.venue: Indian Journal of Social Science and Literature
items.abstract: Households are not just sites of consumption but dynamic systems that constantly manage, reuse and recirculate resources through everyday practices. This study investigates the household activities of rural women through the lens of ‘household circular resource systems’ (HCRS) to demonstrate how the system generates and contributes to environmental sustainability and household resilience and survives in local resource circulation. This study used qualitative methods and collected data through 35 in-depth interviews, participant observation, and household activity mapping from 30 purposively selected rural households in six villages in Pabna and Sirajganj districts. The data were analysed thematically. The findings suggest that the cyclical use of food waste, water, and compostbased nutrients produces interrelated processes. These processes collectively contribute to environmental sustainability and household resilience through continuous resource regeneration, reduced household waste and expenses, and improved food security and water management. Moreover, the results show that the traditional HCRS is maintained through complex interactions among womens productive family resources, intergenerational ecological knowledge, and unpaid domestic labour. Rural women also perceive the circular system as a culturally embedded family custom. However, the level of circularity varies with the number of family-owned animals and arable land. Changing rural lifestyles, marked by greater reliance on commercial agricultural products and less control over property and livestock, are slowly undermining traditional circular techniques. This study advances sustainability and circular economy scholarship by conceptualising HCRS as a localised socio-ecological framework. It suggests that sustainable rural development policies should include family adaptability by acknowledging regional environmental practices, encouraging small-scale animal production, and giving residents greater access

items.title: Throat localized magnetohydrodynamic actuation for thrust enhancement in supersonic rocket nozzles
items.abstract: Among other important considerations in rocket nozzle design, the geometry limitations remained a big challenge. The geometry constraint imposed by the throat section can greatly influence the effects of flow choking, pressure profiles, and overall thrust efficiency; thus, this research explores the idea of using the localized magnetic field in the throat area to control the flow. Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) flow control offers a non-mechanical approach to modifying high speed compressible flows by interacting with electrically conducting gases. In the present study, a two-dimensional computational fluid dynamics framework coupled with MHD model is developed to investigate the influence of localized magnetic fields on the flow dynamics and performance of a supersonic rocket nozzle. The governing Navier–Stokes equations are coupled with electromagnetic source terms to account for Lorentz force effects, and the numerical model is validated against baseline nozzle flow characteristics. A circular arc-contour nozzle is analyzed under four magnetic field intensities (0, 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 T) applied near the throat region. The study systematically examines the resulting changes in flow structure, pressure distribution, and thrust related performance metrics. The results demonstrate that localized magnetic fields alter the acceleration process and suppress adverse flow features, leading to enhanced exit flow characteristics and improved thrust performance. These findings establish the effectiveness of MHD-assisted flow control as a viable strategy for modulating supersonic nozzle behavior without mechanical actuation.

items.title: Nature’s Microfabricated 3D Coupled Dual-Membrane Resonators—A Dynamic Analysis of Circular Diatom Frustules
items.abstract: MEMS (microelectromechanical system) resonators, meticulously fabricated by advanced lithographic and etching processes, have become indispensable technological cornerstones across modern sensing, time-keeping and actuation applications. Yet, realising 3D coupled architectures for these silicon-based resonators remains a fundamental microfabrication challenge, limiting the toolkit of exploitable dynamic phenomena to the in-plane and flexural modes. Nature, however, through 200 million years of evolutionary refinement, has nano-engineered a ready-made solution: the diatom frustule made from biosilica (SiO2), a robust material with mechanical properties well-suited to micro-mechanical resonator applications. Unlike planar MEMS counterparts, frustules are typically dual-membrane structures, vertically coupled by a girdle band, introducing complex 3D coupling dynamics that are prohibitively complex to achieve with MEMS fabrication. This paper explores the analytical and numerical modelling of a typical circular frustule's dynamic behaviour. Alongside the typical transverse modes expected from MEMS resonators, the 3D coupled structure also exhibits unique girdle band tilt modes, exclusively activated by antisymmetric excitations. Collectively, the presence of partial mode localisation, mechanical energy amplification through the low-inertia girdle band, and rotational-transverse modal coupling, demonstrates the diatom frustule to be a dynamically rich resonator. This establishes the theoretical framework for exploiting the diatom frustule as a novel bio-inspired and bio-derived 3D resonator building block.

items.title: The pedagogy of “smart intervention”: aligning socio-spatial justice and circularity in the adaptive re-programming of Alexandria's Cotton Bourse
items.abstract: Purpose Driven by the climate crisis and systemic urban precarity in the Global South, this article evaluates a novel pedagogical framework for interior architecture education. It explores how the “Smart Intervention” pedagogical framework combining material circularity with socio-spatial justice trains students to transform dormant, post-industrial heritage sites like Alexandria's Cotton Bourse into socially responsive community assets, moving beyond the limitations of static historicist preservation. Design/methodology/approach This research employs a qualitative Research-by-Design (RbD) methodology embedded within a 15-week interior architecture bachelor design studio. Using Alexandria's Cotton Bourse in Mena El-Basal as an empirical living laboratory, the methodology integrates archival analysis, physical structural audits, qualitative community ethnography (N = 45), iterative design prototyping and a qualitative expert appraisal (N = 3 jurors). The “Smart Intervention” framework operationalizes Open Building principles (Support vs. Infill) across a purposive sample of three student project typologies. Findings The study illustrates how applying the “Smart Intervention” pedagogical framework equips future interior architects to move past purely aesthetic adaptive reuse. The resulting speculative spatial proposals illustrate how circular material flows such as dry-joint timber and steel friction clamps, structural reversibility and socio-spatial programming can coexist. By designing demountable interior infill systems that accommodate informal street markets, vocational workshops and community archives, post-industrial heritage is re-programmed as an active driver of localized socio-spatial justice. items.title: Closest Points on a Circular Helix and Kepler’s Equation: Exact Counting, the Focal Surface, and the Principal-Branch Minimizer
items.abstract: The closest-point problem for a circular helix reduces to Kepler’s equation u+esinu=M with geometric eccentricity e=aρ/b2 unrestricted above. Building on this known reduction and earlier half-turn localization, we derive an exact stationary-point count and a theorem selecting the global minimizer. For e≤1, the squared distance is strictly convex and has a unique strict minimum, including the degenerate boundary case. For e>1, the generic count is N=2(M+c)/2π−2(M−c)/2π−3, where c=arccos(−1/e)+e2−1. Separate indicators give the distinct and multiplicity counts on every fold, including simultaneous double roots. The count grows like 2e/π; five distinct stationary points become possible precisely when e>4.6033…. We express the classical normal-plane envelope, called the focal surface here, as explicit bifurcation sheets and determine the cut locus and its termination at the evolute helix. The principal-branch theorem identifies the nearest-turn root as the unique global minimizer with exactly two minimizers when M≡π(mod2π) and e>1. For fixed e>1, its absolute root condition number is bounded by 1/(e−1). Fold separation and cusp displacement scale as square and cube roots of the data offset; the corresponding condition numbers diverge with exponents −1/2 and −2/3. A bisection–Newton solver, an equal-pitch two-helix reduction, and reproducible numerical checks complement the analysis.

items.title: Mechanical Stretch Counteracts Hypomagnetic Field-Induced Changes in YAP Nuclear Localization in C2C12 Myoblasts
items.abstract: The geomagnetic field (GMF) is a persistent environmental factor that influences biological processes. Reduced geomagnetic field exposure can alter cellular processes, but its effects on cellular mechanotransduction and responsiveness to mechanical stimulation remain poorly understood. Here, we developed an in vitro platform combining a programmable uniaxial stretching device with a mu-metal shielding chamber to independently manipulate mechanical stretch and magnetic field exposure. Using C2C12 myoblasts, we evaluated culture conditions and cyclic stretching parameters to identify a regimen that promoted nuclear localization of the mechanosensitive transcriptional coactivator yes-associated protein (YAP). We then compared cell and nuclear morphology and YAP nucleocytoplasmic localization under geomagnetic field (GMF) and hypomagnetic field (HMF; approximately 5 nT) conditions, with or without cyclic stretch. Under static conditions, HMF exposure increased cell and nuclear areas, promoted nuclear elongation, reduced nuclear circularity, and decreased the nuclear YAP level. Cyclic stretch induced nuclear alignment perpendicular to the stretching direction under both magnetic field conditions, without significantly altering cell or nuclear area or nuclear elongation. Importantly, cyclic stretch increased nuclear YAP localization under both GMF and HMF conditions, restoring it in HMF-exposed cells to levels comparable to those in stretched cells under GMF. These findings indicate that C2C12 myoblasts remain responsive to mechanical stimulation under HMF conditions and that cyclic stretch can counteract the HMF-associated reduction in nuclear YAP localization. Our platform provides a foundation for investigating how magnetic and mechanical cues jointly regulate myoblast behavior.

items.title: Marine Exposure Performance of a Circular-Concrete Floating Breakwater Prototype: Biofouling, Chloride Ingress and Structural Monitoring
items.abstract: Field evidence on the performance of circular concrete materials in floating marine structures remains limited. This study presents the design, manufacture and nine-month marine exposure of a reduced-scale floating breakwater prototype measuring 3.40 m × 1.70 m × 1.05 m at the Port of Gijón, Spain. The reinforced shell comprised high-performance concrete in the bottom slab and walls and lightweight aggregate concrete in the top slab, while the core combined cellular concrete with fully encapsulated expanded polystyrene required to satisfy the buoyancy constraints of the reduced-scale prototype. The structure was held in position by a four-line catenary mooring system connected to gravity anchors.Prototype performance was evaluated through biofouling surveys, embedded corrosion-potential measurements, chloride profiling, reinforcement inspection, eddy-current corrosion sensing and acceleration monitoring. Biofouling coverage exceeded 85% on all evaluated surfaces, with mussel-dominated layers up to 35 mm thick. Wet biomass on the two sampled lateral faces ranged from 6.3 to 9.7 kg/m². Highly negative reinforcement potentials at permanently submerged locations were consistent with water-saturated, oxygen-limited concrete and did not, in isolation, demonstrate active corrosion. Chloride content exceeded the applicable 0.6% code limit at reinforcement depth only in the lightweight-concrete top slab near openings introduced for monitoring equipment. Possible localised pitting was observed in this area, but no measurable reduction in reinforcement thickness was detected.Environmental compensation reduced the variability of the eddy-current baseline to a ±135 Ω reference band during the analysed period, although field detection of active corrosion was not demonstrated. Dominant measured frequencies of 0.35–0.45 Hz were broadly consistent, within the estimated ±20% uncertainty, with the calculated rigid-body natural-frequency range, particularly the heave and pitch estimate

items.title: A Break-Even Threshold Framework for Circular Digital Transitions on Family Farms: Precision Agriculture and Blockchain Traceability in Rural Colombia
items.abstract: Digital technologies are promoted as enablers of circular agri-food systems, yet family farms lack tools to judge whether such investments pay off, and economic data at this scale are often unreliable. This study develops a break-even threshold framework that evaluates digital investments using only physical and price variables, derives three propositions on entry costs, decision robustness and unreliable data, and applies it to precision agriculture with blockchain traceability on 100 family farms in Sumapaz, Bogotá, Colombia, 50 of them adopters. Three circular dimensions were assessed: the narrowing of resource flows, value retention and chain governance. Adopting farms used 26 to 42% fewer inputs per tonne of output and recorded fewer batch rejections and intermediaries. The investment broke even with a yield gain of 2.51% against an observed differential of 19.95%, and all farms remained viable if only half of that differential were retained, if half of the additional output went unsold or if technology costs doubled. Viability depended on the ratio of investment to farm area, with an elasticity of −0.65, and no price premium for verified origin was found. The framework turns transition narratives into a computable decision rule and identifies entry cost as the main barrier for smallholders.

items.title: Ultrasonic Guided Wave Localization and Classification of Damage-like Perturbations in a CFRP Plate Using a PZT Network
items.abstract: Ultrasonic guided waves acquired using permanently bonded piezoelectric transducers enable large-area monitoring of composite structures. For practical structural health monitoring; however, both the location and the condition of a structural change are critical. This paper presents a data-driven multi-task framework for a carbon-fiber-reinforced polymer plate using a circular PZT array. To generate a large, precise, and repeatable experimental dataset without permanently damaging the specimen, paired magnets were placed on opposite surfaces of the plate and moved using a two-axis positioning system over a uniform grid. Four magnet-pair configurations were used to form four balanced experimental classes. For each case, ultrasonic guided-wave signals from all actuator–sensor paths were concatenated and processed by a shared convolutional neural network and long short-term memory architecture. The model simultaneously estimates the spatial coordinates through two regression branches and identifies the magnet-pair perturbation configuration through a classification branch. An automated hyperparameter search was used to select the principal architectural and training parameters. Performance was evaluated using five-fold training/validation cross-validation. The selected configuration achieved a classification accuracy of 0.9875±0.005 and a macro F1-score of 0.9876±0.0048. The mean normalized Euclidean localization error was 0.0228±0.0009, and 99.43% of the de-normalized localization errors were at or below 20mm. The shared architecture therefore performs simultaneous perturbation-configuration classification and two-dimensional localization from the same multi-path guided-wave measurements under the investigated controlled perturbation conditions.

items.title: Response-specific machine-learning surrogates for preliminary assessment of a parametric steel I-beam family with four circular web openings
items.venue: Journal of Structural Integrity and Maintenance
items.abstract: Steel I-beams with circular web openings facilitate the passage of building services but exhibit complex deformation and localized stress-concentration behaviour. This study develops machine-learning surrogate models for rapid preliminary assessment of such beams using numerical responses generated in ANSYS. A total of 1126 parametric simulations were performed, of which 981 configurations were retained after geometric, meshing, solution, equilibrium, and response-extraction checks. Three independent single-output regression models were developed for maximum deflection, maximum web-stress demand, and maximum opening-edge stress demand. Ridge Regression, Support Vector Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Gaussian Process Regression were evaluated through nested repeated cross-validation. Among the evaluated models, the dimensional Gaussian Process Regression configuration yielded the lowest mean NRMSE for maximum deflection, with a coefficient of determination of 0.784 and an NRMSE of 0.045. The dimensional XGBoost configuration yielded the lowest mean NRMSE for maximum web-stress demand, with a coefficient of determination of 0.527 and an NRMSE of 0.065. The dimensionless-augmented Support Vector Regression configuration yielded the lowest mean NRMSE for maximum opening-edge-stress demand, with a coefficient of determination of 0.509 and an NRMSE of 0.054. Regression Error Characteristic analysis and locally adaptive conformal prediction were used to examine error tolerance and predictive uncertainty.

A bio-digital circular framework for sustainable duck feed production using agro-industrial side-streams and aquatic biomass
items.abstract: The poultry sector faces increasing environmental and economic pressures associated with agro-industrial by-product accumulation, dependence on conventional feed ingredients, and feed-supply logistics. This study developed the SHIREEM framework, a bio-digital circular approach for the valorization of Snack Food Industry By-products (SFIB) and aquatic biomass (Azolla pinnata and Spirulina platensis) in poultry feed production. The framework integrates IoT-assisted process monitoring, computational feed optimization, machine-learning prediction, and circular resource-utilization principles. An IoT-assisted pelleting system incorporating a Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) and real-time sensors was used to monitor and control processing conditions, while a Python-based Least-Cost Ration (LCR) model optimized feed formulations under predefined nutritional and economic constraints. Under the simulated conditions, the optimized formulation reduced the estimated feed production cost from approximately 22,000 to 12,450 EGP ton⁻¹ (43.4%) and reduced logistics-related CO₂ emissions by 93.8% within the defined assessment boundary. Machine-learning models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation, with Gradient Boosting providing the best prediction of body weight and Extra-Trees providing the best prediction of feed conversion ratio among the evaluated models. Feature-importance analysis indicated that age and metabolizable energy were major predictors of growth-related performance, whereas Azolla inclusion showed a greater contribution to feed conversion ratio than to body weight prediction. In addition, 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo simulation indicated that the economic performance of the optimized system remained feasible across the majority of the simulated uncertainty scenarios, with SFIB cost and transportation expenditure identified as important cost drivers. Overall, the results support the potential of SHIREEM as an integrated computational framework for circu

items.title: Information Disorder in Regional Digital Ecosystems: An Empirical Evaluation of Falsehood Propagation in Social Media in Tamil Nadu
items.abstract: This study is a time-bound forensic assessment of non-political digital misinformation that flowed across the digital ecosystem of Tamil Nadu. The analysis excludes electoral and partisan political narratives and examines ten major viral case studies along four operational pathways: Public Safety and Social Panic, Cyber-Financial Fraud, Educational Integrity, and Public Health and Civic Infrastructure. In this paper, we adopt an empirical mixed-methods framework to quantify audience reach on open broadcast platforms (YouTube, Instagram, X, Facebook) and to compute transmission velocity in dark social environments (WhatsApp, Telegram). Technical telemetry is collected alongside engagement metrics for each case study including distribution by platform, views/impressions, likes, dark social forwards, public shares/retweets and user comments. The empirical findings show that non-political misinformation takes advantage of affective cognitive triggers such as parental panic, financial precarity, and disaster anxiety, not synthetic media (deepfakes). The paper discusses real-world implications of out-of-context video footage, forged administrative PDF circulars, automated smishing APK trojans and deceptively vernacular voice notes that result in mob vigilantism, mobile banking fraud and disruption of public utility. Counter-measures discussed include telecom-level APK filtering, verified administrative push channels, and localized media literacy protocols [1, 2, 3].

Transboundary Macro-Aperture Seismo-Infrasonic Localization of Technogenic Detonations by Contour Phase Closure Method ('TREMBITA-3P'): Verification by the Toropets Event
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.abstract: Transboundary Macro-Aperture Seismo-Infrasonic Localization of Technogenic Detonations by Contour Phase Closure Method ('TREMBITA-3P'): Verification by the Toropets Event Author: Banakh Andriy Stepanovych (Банах Андрій Степанович) ORCID: 0009-0000-2933-1143 Email: bass776@ukr.net Official Portal: https://deepresearchhub.online Abstract The paper develops and experimentally verifies a transboundary macro-aperture method for high-precision spatiotemporal localization and yield estimation of massive technogenic detonations and arsenal explosions. The method is based on Banakh's closed-loop contour phase closure invariant (∑ Δt ≡ 0) and hyperbolic Time Difference of Arrival (TDoA) beamforming utilizing heterogeneous regional and global seismic and infrasonic networks (including EMSC catalog feeds and CTBTO/IMS stations). The method was verified using instrumental recordings from the massive ammunition depot detonation at Toropets (Tver region, 18 September 2024, 00:46 UTC, Mw ≈ 3.6, equivalent explosive yield ≈ 1.5–2.2 kt TNT). Incorporating closed-contour phase residuals suppressed atmospheric wind drift bias, narrowing the epicenter localization circular error probable (CEP50) from ±18.4 km to less than 0.82 km, confirming the technological baseline for the mobile "TREMBITA-3P" / "NIS-EKO" infrastructure. items.title: CULINARY CATALYSTS: DECIPHERING THE ROLE OF SUSTAINABLE RESTAURANTS IN THE JOURNEY TOWARD GREEN DESTINATION STATUS: THE CASE OF URLA, İZMIR, TÜRKIYE
items.abstract: Sustainable destinations are increasingly relies on integrating localized eco-friendly practices across key service sectors. Gastronomy plays a pivotal role in reinforcing destination sustainability and regional brand equity. This study examines the strategic role of gastronomy in positioning Urla as a recognized green destination. Specifically, the contribution of Michelin Green Star awarded restaurants to the overall environmental, social, and economic sustainability performance of green destinations is analyzed theoretically and empirically through the case of Urla. The conceptual integration of sustainable tourism governance and gastronomy is established through an extensive literature review and a theoretical framework. A qualitative case study design is employed to conduct an in-depth evaluation of Urla, a region that serves as a prominent exemplar of sustainable culinary tourism. Consequently, sustainable restaurant practices, localized supply chain operations, and green destination criteria are systematically evaluated through qualitative content analysis. This methodological structure allows for a comprehensive assessment of how regional gastronomic actors align with broader environmental governance and sustainability frameworks. The findings reveal that sustainability practices within the gastronomy sector significantly enhance the environmental, social, and economic performance of the destination. Michelin Green Star awarded restaurants serve as benchmark models that accelerate eco-innovation, circular economy integration, and local heritage preservation. Consequently, strengthening the synergy between sustainable tourism policies and gastronomic practices is critical for fostering long-term destination resilience and sustainable regional development.

items.title: Assessment of Multi-Scale Performance Modelling of Plastic Recycled Bricks
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.abstract: Plastic recycle bricks (PBS) is a product of the mixture of polyethylene (PE) and polypropylene (PP) waste with sand fillers. This brick offers a viable solution to massive environmental, economic and social challenges emanating from accumulation of plastic waste, particularly in developing and rapid urbanizing areas where generation of plastic waste is on the rise. Instead of sending them to landfills this effort advances circular economy by turning plastic waste into high performance building materials. Plastic recycle bricks (PBS) is heterogenous in nature with complex mechanical, thermal and durability that is unpredictable across length which limits its structural adoption and its predictive understanding. This study evaluates a computational multi scale performance modelling framework for Plastic Recycled Bricks by formulating hierarchical and concurrent strategies to couple polymer-matrix viscoelasticity and interfacial cohesion at micro scale, representative-volume-element (RVE) homogenisation at meso-scale, and continuum structural response at macro scale. Constitutive models are parameterised from published experimental dataset. Finite element homogenisation of generated RVEs determine the effective stiffness and thermal- conductivity tensors that was used to analyse macro-scale brick and masonry models. Comparative analysis of multiscale model against single scale continuum approach proves that multiscale model delivers a superior predictive accuracy for compressive strength, elastic modulus and thermal conductivity with the capabilities of capturing damage localization and creep. Interfacial bonding strength, filler volume fraction and residual porosity are the important governing parameters that were revealed by the sensitivity analysis. Due to virtual mix optimization, the framework established a theoretical performance base PRB design which contribute to a transferable computational methodology for recycling plastic waste in sustainable construction a

items.title: Standardized semantic enrichment of OpenBIM for machine-readable pre-demolition audits
items.abstract: The transition to a circular construction sector requires reliable, machine-readable material data from existing buildings. Although reality-capture and emerging scan-to-BIM workflows increasingly support geometric modeling of existing buildings, pre-demolition audits still rely largely on manual interpretation and static reports that downstream tools cannot automatically process. The remaining obstacle is semantic. This paper presents WASTEie2IFC, a web-based framework that addresses this gap by writing audit outputs against the openly published bSDD WASTEie dictionary. The resulting IFC files carry interoperable Property Sets and European Waste Catalogue classifications rather than proprietary labels, standardizing the audit deliverable. We evaluate the framework on a historical railway station in the Czech Republic, enabling a rare ex-post comparison against actual measured demolition tonnages. The comparison shows that the semantic enrichment pipeline itself introduced no measurable computational error: for the mineral fractions represented in the model, the predicted mass deviated by 28% from the measured tonnage, and the aggregate 51% gap between predicted and measured totals is attributable to materials outside the scope of the input geometry (subsurface, external, thin-layered, and non-structural elements) and to on-site re-sorting decisions rather than to the enrichment workflow. Hazardous chimney masonry identified and spatially localized in the model was separately dismantled according to the contractor, and no hazardous fraction appears in the demolition consignment records. Within the bounds of a single validated case and a dependence on the completeness of upstream reality capture, the results indicate that standardized, machine-readable pre-demolition audit deliverables are achievable today using exclusively open standards.

items.title: Utilization of Recycled Concrete Aggregate for Road Subgrade Stabilization: A Syrian Case Study and Feasibility Assessment for Application in Southern Libya
items.venue: Journal of sustainable research in applied sciences
items.abstract: Infrastructure projects in southern Libya, particularly in Ubari, face significant logistical and economic challenges due to the high cost of transporting construction materials from the coast, alongside the accumulation of demolition debris that poses an environmental burden. This study presents an innovative and sustainable solution by utilizing Recycled Concrete Aggregate (RCA) as a soil stabilizer, based on a field-laboratory experiment conducted in Syria on expansive clay soil, which was blended with RCA ratios of 5%, 10%, and 15% according to ASTM standards. The technical results demonstrated significant improvement at a 15% RCA content, where the California Bearing Ratio (CBR) increased from 8% to 22%, the Unconfined Compressive Strength (UCS) increased from 20.94 to 201.6 kPa, and the free swell index decreased from 11% to 2%, making the mixture suitable for the road subgrade applications according to the AASHTO classification. Economically, the study showed that the stabilization cost using RCA is 50% to 75% lower compared to traditional stabilizers such as cement and lime. The research recommends adopting this technique in Libya as a model for the circular economy, and calls for the establishment of national legislations that encourage the localization of concrete debris recycling. This contributes significantly to reducing project costs, achieving environmental sustainability, and supporting local development in the southern regions.

items.title: УМОВИ ТА МЕЖІ ВПЛИВУ ЦИРКУЛЯРНОЇ ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЇ НА РЕЗИЛЬЄНТНІСТЬ РЕГІОНУ В СЕРЕДОВИЩІ СИСТЕМНИХ ВИКЛИКІВ
items.abstract: The article critically examines the assumption that circular transformation automatically strengthens regional resilience and argues that this relationship is conditional rather than universal. The study aims to identify the conditions under which circular transformation enhances regional resilience and those under which its effect becomes neutral or may generate new vulnerabilities. The methodological framework combines systemic and structural-functional approaches, logical generalisation, comparison, matrix analysis and graphical modelling. The analysis shows that the presumed automatic link between circularity and resilience is based on three premises: that reducing external resource dependence necessarily increases stability; that the effect of circular measures is independent of the type of shock; and that deeper circularisation always produces a proportional increase in resilience. Six structural contradictions are identified: resource efficiency versus capacity reservation; localisation of resource cycles versus supply diversification; industrial symbiosis versus network propagation of shocks; life-cycle extension versus technological modernisation; recycling versus energy dependence; and digital management of resource flows versus technological vulnerabilities. Four parameters shaping the direction and strength of the effect are defined: the type of shock, time horizon, spatial scale of the circular loop and institutional capacity. On this basis, a matrix of conditions for the resilient effect of circular transformation is developed. It links circular strategies with the shock profile, time horizon, spatial configuration, required conditions and expected resilience outcome. The study also formulates a principle of conditionality: circularity does not by itself guarantee resilience, while a positive effect depends on the configuration of circular practices, resource diversification, spatial links, reserve capacity, institutional capacity and consistency with

items.title: How organisations account for the SDGs: a systematic review of management, reporting and assurance research
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to evaluate how systematic literature review (SLR) synthesises organisational engagement with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in management, reporting, assurance and accounting practices to address social and environmental challenges. Design/methodology/approach A decade of SDG-related organisational accounting research was examined through an SLR of 755 scholarly articles published between 2015 and 2025 in leading accounting, sustainability and business journals. The review investigates the intellectual structure and evolution of this field by analysing core thematic concerns, publication and citation trends, methodological practices, theoretical foundations and also authorship and collaboration patterns. Bibliometrics and content analysis are combined to map how SDGs have been integrated into organisational accounting discourse, identify dominant research clusters and highlight areas for future inquiry. Findings Publications increase sharply from 1 article in 2015 to 231 in 2025, with sustainability (Switzerland) emerging as the most prominent outlet. The field is predominantly empirical and theory-driven, relying mainly on Legitimacy Theory, Impression Management, Signalling, Information Asymmetry and Green/Bluewashing perspectives to explain SDG-related behaviour. Twelve thematic clusters capture the literature, covering environmental, social and governance performance and SDGs’ contributions, institutional and supply-chain drivers, strategic SDGs’ alignment, reporting and governance, quality of engagement, value creation and integrated thinking, evolving sustainability paradigms, external drivers of disclosure, technology and circular economy transitions, localisation of SDGs, public-sector accounting and critiques of reporting. Originality/value This review provides a detailed overview of SDG-oriented organisational accounting research, which is conceptualised as research involving accounting, reporting, assuranc

items.title: The contribution of blogging in enhancing the uptake of slow fashion in Kenya: a case study of fashion bloggers in Nairobi Parklands
items.abstract: Kenya’s fashion landscape is undergoing a shift toward sustainability, driven by growing environmental awareness, circular economy initiatives, and a critique of fast fashion import reliance. Despite the rising presence of independent fashion blogging as a tool for consumer education, empirical research on its direct role in promoting sustainable consumption in Kenya remains limited. This study investigated the contribution of fashion blogging in enhancing the uptake of slow fashion among urban Kenyan consumers. Guided by the Uses and Gratifications Theory and the Theory of Planned Behavior, the study adopted a mixed method research approach. The study was conducted in Nairobi CBD and Parklands, Westlands Constituency, Kenya. This study used purposive sampling to identify active bloggers and stratified random sampling to select fashion consumers. Data was collected via questionnaires administered to 331 respondents. Quantitative analysis revealed that fashion blog influence has a strong, positive, and statistically significant relationship with slow fashion uptake, independently accounting for 40.2% of its variation. A multiple regression model showed that blogger credibility, content quality, and audience engagement jointly explained 59.0% of the variance, with blogger credibility acting as the strongest predictor. Qualitative insights highlighted visual storytelling, authentic narratives, and localization as key effective communication strategies. The study concludes that fashion blogging is a vital digital mechanism for driving sustainable fashion behavior in Kenya, though affordability and accessibility barriers persist. It recommends tailoring slow fashion messaging to familiar Kenyan practices, including mitumba selection, garment repair, upcycling, and the use of locally produced textiles, to promote accessible and mindful consumption across income levels.

items.title: ADVANCES AND BARRIERS IN THE ADOPTION OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS (SDGS) IN THE CERAMIC INDUSTRY: EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE FROM THE NORTE DE SANTANDER CLUSTER, COLOMBIA (2017–2024)
items.abstract: The adoption of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in traditional heavy industries is critical for the global energy transition. This study evaluates the integration of SDGs within the ceramic manufacturing cluster in Norte de Santander, Colombia, between 2017 and 2024. To assess the sector's operational, technological, and regulatory dynamics, this research employs a mixed-methods approach combining regional empirical data with a systematic literature review of 50 academic sources from Scopus and Web of Science. The findings indicate moderate progress regarding SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure) and SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), evidenced by a 28% increase in the deployment of energy-efficient kilns alongside facility-wide upgrades, and a 15% localized reduction in greenhouse gas emissions. Furthermore, the industry remains heavily dependent on fossil fuels, with natural gas and coal accounting for over 90% of thermal energy generation. Conversely, significant gaps persist regarding SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production); only 9% of enterprises implement circular economy and recycling processes—a rate 40% lower than the national industrial average. Regarding structural obstacles, three major categories were identified: Technical (on-site renewable energy is used by only 5% of facilities), Regulatory (60% of businesses do not know of sustainability incentive programs), and Operational (84% of companies have not implemented water management systems). Importantly, this study indicates that socio-technical barriers, such as resistance to change and knowledge deficits, pose greater barriers than purely financial constraints. To enhance SDG compliance, this paper proposes a strategic framework comprising digital self-assessment platforms for SMEs, Cyber-Physical Energy Management Systems (CPS-EMS) utilizing predictive machine learning algorithms, public-private technological financing mechanisms (projected to mitigate emissions by an ad
