items.title: Research Progress on Global E-Waste Recycling Management and Life Cycle Impact Assessment
items.abstract: Waste electrical and electronic equipment （WEEE） has both resource value and environmental risk characteristics，making its recycling management a key issue in the global circular economy and sustainable development. Although life cycle assessment （LCA） is widely recognized as an effective tool for evaluating the environmental impacts of processes such as WEEE recycling，existing research has largely focused on comparing the environmental impacts of different treatment technologies. There has been little integrated analysis of the systematic interrelationships between management models，technical performance，pathway optimization，and decision-making applications. This review compares and summarizes differences in WEEE recycling management models and systems in various countries and regions. It also systematically examines the environmental impacts of key recycling and treatment technologies，as well as their limiting factors. Furthermore，the challenges faced by LCA in optimizing management pathways and decision-making applications has been discussed. The results suggest that developing countries are significantly behind developed countries in terms of their WEEE recycling management systems，networks，treatment systems，and governance capacity. Current research still faces several key challenges，including discrepancies in accounting boundaries and analytical methods，data quality and regional representativeness，study duration，and the integration of research themes. These issues restrict the gradual expansion of LCA from being used as a single environmental comparison tool to being used as a vital framework that supports multi-dimensional，coordinated decision-making across environmental，economic and social dimensions. consequently, future research should put more emphasis on refining evaluation systems and optimized policy coordination from a life-cycle perspective，particularly focusing on China and other developing countries. Concurrently，efforts should be made to standardiz

items.title: Mechanical and functional performance of lightweight low-carbon eco-bricks manufactured from recycled waste materials
items.abstract: Driven by circular economy goals, upcycling dredged marine deposits and waste tire rubber remains a critical challenge. Conventional eco-bricks rely on natural or recycled aggregates to form a rigid skeleton, introducing heterogeneous interfaces and micro-mechanical defects while increasing energy consumption. This study introduces a novel matrix-dominated, aggregate-free eco-brick fabricated from fine-grained dredged marine deposits, recycled granular tire rubber, and a cement-free, lime-activated ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBS) binder. A comprehensive experimental program evaluated thirteen formulations, varying rubber content from 0% to 20% and particle size from 0.1 to 1.0 mm, to determine how rubber inclusion characteristics affect the composite’s macroscopic performance and microstructural evolution. Results show that rubber particle size fundamentally governs mechanical and functional behavior. While rubber incorporation reduces structural stiffness and increases porosity, optimizing the inclusion size (e.g., 0.1 mm at 10% content) effectively controls interfacial defect formation. This selected formulation ensures a sufficient compressive capacity of 19.5 MPa, alongside a 16% weight reduction and a superior thermal conductivity of 0.73 W/mK. Microstructural analyses reveal that fine rubber grains enhance spatial entrapment and uniform dispersion. This size-dependent spatial restriction limits the widening of the interfacial transition zone (ITZ), thereby mitigating the impact of localized modulus mismatches. Furthermore, utilizing the GGBS binder and eliminating high-temperature firing yields an estimated 74–80% reduction in embodied carbon emissions while ensuring safe heavy metal immobilization. This research establishes a fundamental paradigm for matrix-dominated eco-bricks, demonstrating that tailoring the physical size of waste inclusions and their interfacial compatibility can convert problematic wastes into low-carbon, high-performance bui

items.title: Reference-renormalized Jacobi primitives for finite-distance massive-particle deflection
items.abstract: We develop a reference-renormalized Jacobi-primitive Gauss-Bonnet formalism for finite-distance weak deflection of massive particles in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes. The construction uses the fixed-energy Jacobi metric associated with timelike geodesics and treats the radial curvature primitive as a quantity defined only up to an additive constant. Instead of fixing this constant by requiring the primitive to vanish at a circular timelike orbit, we subtract a reference Jacobi geometry at the same conserved particle energy and impose endpoint normalization on the curvature-density discrepancy. This gives a circular-orbit-free primitive representation of the Gauss-Bonnet curvature contribution while preserving the operational finite-distance definition of the bending angle through local source and receiver directions. We prove that the reference-normalized and circular-orbit-normalized prescriptions agree whenever both are admissible, since their primitives differ only by a constant that cancels from the exact curvature strip integral. The method remains applicable when no admissible circular timelike orbit exists, when the orbit lies outside the Riemannian Jacobi domain, or when the natural no-lens comparison geometry is non-Euclidean. We demonstrate the formalism in three representative settings. For the Schwarzschild-like bumblebee spacetime, the method separates the conical reference contribution from the localized mass correction and recovers the Schwarzschild massive-particle limit when the deformation is removed. For the Kottler spacetime, a de Sitter Jacobi reference organizes the localized mass contribution inside the static patch. For the Janis-Newman-Winicour geometry, the reference-renormalized primitive remains well defined in a photon-sphere-free JNW subinterval 0 < γ ≤ 2 / 5 where unbound circular-orbit normalization is unavailable, and the finite-distance bending angle is completed through second order with explicit dependence on the scalar

items.title: G reen C onstruction M anagement in O ffshore W ind P ower P rojects
items.abstract: The transformation to clean energy in the world promotes the development of offshore wind power in deep and Far Seas. The construction is greatly affected by complex sea conditions, with short effective operation time and a long ecological chain impact path. Most of the existing management methods are based on land-based construction, and no effective circular control measures have been developed for the unique marine pollution factors, which can not meet the needs of emerging industries. This paper summarizes the literature review and typical engineering project examples, summarizes the theoretical research progress and governance experience of green construction of offshore wind power, and compares the policy transmission mode and technology docking mode in different jurisdictions. The academic community has reached a conclusion that the land green construction standard can not be well applied to the marine field. Practice has shown that centralized approval and marine spatial planning are feasible, but the transnational spread of floating wind power is still controversial, mainly due to the contradiction between the requirements for stability and construction flexibility. The current research lacks a localization evaluation method combining micro and macro perspectives and the internalization path of ecological cost.

items.title: A Distinct Mode of Chromosome-End Genome Instability Revealed by Circulome Characterization and Analyses
items.abstract: Genome instability is a central hallmark of cancer and it is characterized largely from sequence: mutation, copy-number change and rearrangement scored against a linear reference. The genome has additional degrees of freedom, such as the physical form (topology) of the DNA itself. A specific mode of localized genome dynamics changes both dimensions (sequence and topology) at once: defined chromosomal regions are also represented as extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA). The biogenesis of eccDNA is a feature of many cancers, supplying the tumor with genetic elements that can participate in phenotypic selection, and supplying the observer with a window into the genomic instability landscape. Genome-wide maps of where these circles arise have not been available at scale or at high resolution. Building such maps requires physical selection of circular species, because most sequenced reads from unselected DNA derive from unrearranged sequence, conflating the signal from dynamic rearrangements with that from bulk chromosomal DNA. Here we combine biophysical and biochemical isolation of circular DNA with next-generation sequencing, applying it to a panel of cancer cell lines and to patient tumors, with non-cancerous cells and adjacent normal tissues as controls. The resulting genome-wide maps of the circular-element repertoire, the Circulome, reveal a consistent and previously unreported enrichment of these elements at particular chromosome ends. The circles map to regions extending well past the telomeres, reaching varying distances up to tens of megabases inward. This activity is accompanied by corroborating rearrangements within the linear genome, consistent with regions of chromosomal instability. Together these features define a spatially localized mode of instability in cancer, which we term Erosion at Distal Genomic Ends (EDGE). We formulate a classification problem to discriminate bladder tumor from matched normal tissue, finding that the EDGE signal outperforms t

items.title: Categorizing Toll Gates using Data of Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, Sentinel-5P, NOAA-20 Satellite, and Objects on Google Map: A Case Study in Indonesia
items.abstract: This study proposes a framework to categorize toll gates based on the development level of their surrounding areas and localized economic activity profiles. The methodology integrates multi-source satellite imagery with geospatial features extracted from the Google Maps API. The localized economic context of 419 toll gates was analysed within a 1-km circular buffer zone. Within this radius, Sentinel-2 spectral bands (B2, B3, B4 and B8) extracted from Google Earth Engine (GEE) were classified into built-up and non-built-up pixels using a Random Forest algorithm to quantify the built-up area percentage. Gates with a built-up density of at least 40% were categorized as Class-1, representing infrastructure in highly developed regions. For the remaining gates, Sentinel-1 VV polarization, Sentinel-5P tropospheric NO2 column density, and NOAA-20 VIIRS nighttime lights data were extracted via GEE, alongside point-of-interest (POI) counts from Google Maps. items.title: Coupled Shaft–Plate Load-Transfer Solution for Helical Piles in Depth-Dependent Elastic Media
items.abstract: Helical piles differ from conventional straight piles because vertical load transfer (LT) is governed by the coupled action of distributed shaft shear and localized bearing resistance mobilized by the helix plate. Existing LT models and continuum solutions for axially loaded piles generally do not explicitly account for this discrete bearing surface and the associated load redistribution mechanism. Building on established continuum pile and embedded plate solutions, this study develops a coupled analytical formulation for the vertical response of a single helix pile embedded in a depth-dependent elastic medium. The pile is modeled as a compressible shaft coupled with an embedded circular bearing surface representing the helix plate. The shaft and soil responses are linked through displacement compatibility at the helix level, allowing the helix load to be determined as part of the solution. Integral-form analytical solutions are derived for the pile displacement, axial force, and soil stress fields using Hankel transforms and Green’s function techniques. The formulation is verified by degeneration to a benchmark embedded circular plate problem and comparison with finite-element results. These results show that the helix induces a distinct axial force discontinuity and localized stress redistribution, marking a transition from shaft-controlled transfer to bearing-controlled load redistribution. Increasing the helix embedment depth, helix diameter, or soil stiffness gradient enhances load sharing by the helix, but the response becomes progressively less sensitive to further increases in these parameters over parts of the investigated ranges. These trends arise from displacement compatibility between shaft resistance and helix bearing. The proposed formulation provides a mechanics-based reference for interpreting load redistribution in helical piles and for assessing simplified and numerical models.

items.title: The whale binaural rings experiment: Long-range acoustic monitoring of North Atlantic right whales in the Gulf of St. Lawrence
items.venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
items.abstract: Effective real-time monitoring of baleen whales over broad areas was assessed using two 20-m circular hydrophone arrays designed for detecting and localizing North Atlantic right whale (NARW) upcalls. The system was deployed over a 24-d period in August 2021 to monitor a ∼80-km-wide trough heavily frequented by NARWs in the Gulf of St. Lawrence. Key functional parameters throughout the processing chain were estimated from in situ conditions and integrated with numerical simulations. The spatiotemporal performances of the system-using deep-learning neural networks upcall detection and bearing-crossing localization-under in situ noise levels was consistent with predictions from comprehensive acoustic modelling of the full transmission pathway, from source emission to signal reception. Among the 3117 NARW upcalls detected, 30% were successfully localized within the common detection area shared by the two hydrophone arrays. Significant diel changes in call occurrence rates were observed. Spatiotemporal call patterns reveal multi-scale habitat use across the 3600-km2 surveyed region. This study highlights the enhanced capabilities and operational constraints of this beamformed, high-gain, directional listening system relative to conventional single-hydrophone passive acoustic monitoring approaches, particularly under conditions of elevated anthropogenic noise.

items.title: West Suffolk Operational Hub Extension, Bury St Edmunds, Suffolk: Geophysical Survey
items.abstract: The geophysical survey comprises an area of 9.03 ha, which was surveyed with a Bartington Grad601-2 dual fluxgate gradiometer at 1m transverse and at 0.25m sample intervals using a zigzag transverse. With the site was laid out using Lecia Captivate with GS18/CS20 GNSS RTK Rover, with a grid size of 30m by 30m. In January 2026, Cotswold Archaeology undertook a geophysical survey at the West Suffolk Operational Hub Extension, Fornham St Martin, Suffolk. A total of 9.03/ha was surveyed within the site. The survey identified a variety of anomalies, which have been classified as agricultural, archaeological, geological/natural, modern, and undetermined. Several possible archaeological features were detected in the central northern part of the survey area. These included a potential trackway, elements of field systems, and a possible circular structure resembling a roundhouse. However, these features were confined to a relatively small part of the overall survey area. The survey also recorded several modern disturbances. Two services run through the site, one of which is a high pressure gas main that generated a substantial buffer of magnetic disturbance. Additional disruptions include an old north/south field boundary and a large geological or natural anomaly in the northwestern part of the survey area. Such interference has likely distorted or obscured minor archaeological features within these localised zones.

items.title: Self-similar rigid rotation in anisotropic squeezed Laguerre-Gaussian beams
items.abstract: We introduce anisotropic squeezed Laguerre–Gaussian beams as an analytically complete family of structured paraxial scalar beams with Gouy-phase-controlled self-similar rigid rotation. Our construction organizes the Laguerre–Gaussian transverse modal Hilbert space into circular modal subspaces carrying parity-resolved single-mode su(1, 1) representations. The resulting optical Bargmann bases support squeezed states whose lowest-weight forms factor into Gaussian beam phases, parity-dependent polynomials, and elliptically anisotropic Gaussian envelopes. Excited seeds are polynomial deformations of the same squeezed envelope, extending the analytic construction to the full family. The Gouy-dressed squeezing parameter sets the semi-axis widths, aspect ratio, handedness, and orientation, while propagation rotates the profile by the accumulated Gouy phase without changing the scaled transverse shape. We generate these fields with synthetic phase holograms and experimentally confirm their self-similar rigid rotation. Our scalar-beam family provides a tunable anisotropic structured-light platform whose transverse orientation encodes propagation distance and may support axial localization, range finding, optical manipulation, and modal diagnostics.

items.title: Geophysical Survey at Mile Oak, Staffordshire
items.abstract: This geophysical survey was completed using a Sensys FMG650/3 system. Readings were recorded at a resolution of 0.01 nT and data collected with a traverse interval of 1 m and a sample interval of between 0.16 - 0.25 m. The geophysical survey produced good data throughout and has identified several anomalies of possible archaeological origin as well as a number of further anomalies associated with medieval to postmedieval agricultural practices. Three recorded former boundaries have been identified within Field 1, two of which are situated in the north and east of the field and correspond to patterns of land division visible on 19th century (1830s- 1880s) Ordnance Survey (OS) maps. The third is located in the southeast of the field and is noted on OS maps dating to the 18th-19th centuries (1798-1878). Two linear anomalies that may represent additional, unrecorded boundary features are present in both the northeast and centre of Field 1, although it is also conceivable that they are of a more recent agricultural origin. A large linear anomaly situated in close proximity to the latter, centrally located anomaly has been labelled as an uncertain trend. It is possible that this anomaly represents an additional unrecorded boundary, holloway or former headland, although a definitive interpretation is precluded by its weak response. Several similarly weak, linear trends noted in Field 2 are likely to represent land drains, although it is also plausible that they indicate evidence of earlier agricultural regimes or ridge and furrow. Two broadly circular areas of dipolar response present within the centre of Field 1 are characteristic of areas subject to burning and may be of medieval origin but may predate this period. A further pair of positive, amorphous anomalies situated in the east of Field 1 may represent mineral extraction activity or refuse pits, although they may alternatively be the product of localised geological variation. items.title: Geophysical Survey at Webheath, Redditch
items.abstract: This geophysical survey was completed using a Sensys FMG650/3 system. Readings were recorded at a resolution of 0.01 nT and data collected with a traverse interval of 0.5 m and a sample interval of between 0.25 m. A weakly positive, circular anomaly is noted extending from the northeastern boundary of Field 3. This anomaly may indicate a cut and infilled ditch feature. In addition, a further, even weaker positive circular trend is adjoined to its northwest. However, a modern agricultural origin, or even a geological origin cannot be entirely ruled out. Two weakly positive linear anomalies are noted to the south of the possible ring ditch, also at the eastern boundary of Field 3 and may be indicative of former enclosure of uncertain provenance. A weakly positive, curvilinear anomaly is noted in the northwest of Field 1 and has tentatively been interpreted as an uncertain trend. This may denote a cut and infilled ditch feature though a modern land drain is equally plausible. Weakly positive, parallel linear trends indicating historical cultivation traverse the width of Fields 1 and 2 and may be indicative of ridge and furrow, a medieval to post-medieval cultivation practice. Amorphous area of weakly enhanced magnetic response located in the northwest corner of Field 3 and denoted localised geological variation within the underlying mudstone bedrock. The remaining anomalies within the dataset and modern in origin and indicate evidence of modern irrigation features and 'spike' anomalies which are likely to be caused by material and debris in the topsoil.

items.title: Moving Away from Fossil Fuels with Other Heat Technologies
items.abstract: Electricity from heat technologies represent a frontier in the global energy transition, serving as a bridge between untapped thermal resources and the growing demand for sustainable power. These systems function by capturing thermal energy — derived from geological reservoirs, industrial exhaust or incidental waste heat — and converting it into electrical energy through either mechanical or solid-state means. By repurposing heat that would otherwise dissipate, these technologies significantly bolster sustainable energy resources, and potentially enhance overall energy efficiency of heavy industries by reducing their carbon footprint. Currently, two primary pathways dominate the field: (1) geothermal systems, which harness the immense, constant heat stored beneath the Earth’s crust to drive large-scale turbines [658], providing a reliable ‘baseload’ power source that is independent of weather conditions. Industrial waste heat is also a significant heat resource, though the vast majority of it remains untapped; and (2) thermoelectric technology, which utilises specialised materials to generate electricity directly from temperature gradients via the Seebeck effect [131]. Because they have no moving parts, these devices are ideal for localised applications such as capturing heat from vehicle exhaust or powering remote sensors. As global energy needs continue to surge, the refinement of these technologies is no longer just a technical curiosity but a strategic necessity for building a resilient, circular energy economy.

items.title: Geomorphic Evidence for Post-Impact Modification of a Small Crater in Mare Boreum, Mars
items.abstract: Small impact craters within the Martian north polar layered deposits (NPLDs) provide localized geomorphic records of surface modification within an ice-rich polar environment. We investigate a small crater in Mare Boreum using CTX and multi-temporal HiRISE imagery, HiRISE-derived topography, and regional constraints from MOLA, TES, GRS, SHARAD, and geological mapping. The crater retains a sub-circular planform but exhibits markedly subdued topographic expression, including attenuated rim relief and a shallow interior. HiRISE-derived topography indicates substantially reduced relief relative to fresh-crater morphometric expectations for a feature of comparable scale. The coexistence of a preserved planform and strongly attenuated relief indicates substantial cumulative post-impact modification. Multi-temporal HiRISE observations resolve the crater rim, interior, and illumination-sensitive surface features under broadly comparable seasonal conditions. Regional geological, thermophysical, geochemical, and radar observations constrain the broader ice-rich polar setting but do not resolve crater-scale composition, infill, or subsurface structure. The observed morphology is consistent with cumulative modification that may include depositional infilling, sublimation-related redistribution, rim degradation, and relaxation within the NPLDs, although the relative contributions of these processes cannot be uniquely determined from the available orbital observations.

items.title: Sustainable cement production via a liquid-phase pathway
AgroCableBot: Experimental Validation of a Reconfigurable Cable-Driven Parallel Robot for Precision Agriculture and Crop Monitoring
items.abstract: Precision agriculture requires robotic platforms capable of covering large cultivation areas while providing accurate positioning for localized crop monitoring and management operations. Cable-driven parallel robots (CDPRs) offer large workspaces and lightweight moving structures; however, their usable workspace is constrained by cable tension requirements. This study presents the experimental validation of AgroCableBot, a reconfigurable CDPR for precision agriculture previously proposed by the authors, in which the proximal cable attachment points are vertically reconfigured to increase the wrench-feasible workspace (WFW). Previous simulation results showed that this reconfiguration increases the WFW from approximately 58% to 100% of the geometrically admissible workspace for a minimum cable tension of 5 N. In this work, a physical prototype with adjustable anchor height was built, and a vision-based sensing system was integrated for end-effector localization, automatic calibration, and closed-loop trajectory tracking. Experimental validation included square and circular trajectories and an agricultural inspection trajectory over a seedling tray, executed at three anchor heights (400, 600 and 900 mm). The system achieved a three-dimensional RMSE between 1.9 and 2.6 mm, a 95th-percentile error below 4.5 mm, and a maximum tracking error of 6.0 mm, measured with the vision system. These results demonstrate the potential of AgroCableBot as a reconfigurable robotic platform for accurate crop monitoring and localized agricultural operations in protected cultivation environments.

items.title: Accurate measurement of concrete void defects based on deep learning and binocular vision technology
items.abstract: Automated detection and area quantification of concrete surface void defects are important tasks in field inspection. This study proposes a method integrating deep learning and binocular vision to measure planar projected defect areas. A dataset comprising 432 original stereo image pairs representing 287 distinct physical defects was collected using a ZED 2i stereo camera. The improved YOLOv11n model localizes defects, and its predicted bounding boxes serve as prompts for a fine‐tuned Segment Anything Model to extract defect contours. CREStereo estimates disparity for three‐dimensional contour reconstruction, followed by reference‐plane fitting, local coordinate transformation, and contour projection for area calculation. On the independent test set, detection mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 reach 93.1% and 58.3%, respectively, while segmentation mean intersection over union and boundary intersection over union reach 93.59% and 86.74%. Area estimates are presented for nine field defects, of which five with circular‐marker‐based reference areas are included in the agreement evaluation. The mean and maximum absolute relative errors relative to the marker‐based reference measurements are 6.87% and 8.86%, respectively. The results demonstrate the potential of the method for automated projected‐area measurement of concrete surface defects, while broader field data and independent reference measurements are needed to further establish its reliability.

items.title: Excitation of terahertz quasi-BIC resonances via complementary metallic dimer metasurfaces
Towards an Automated Waste-Sorting System: Computer Vision and Neural-Network Inverse Kinematics for a 5-DOF Arm
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.abstract: Automated waste sorting with a robotic manipulator requires two capabilities that belong to different fields: recognizing and localizing the object in the image, and converting a target Cartesian position into joint angles. This paper reports the construction and separate evaluation of both modules for a 5-DOF manipulator, and verifies the inverse-kinematics module on a continuous trajectory. For the recognition module a dedicated dataset, EPU_waste, of 2,955 images and 4,068 annotated instances in three classes was built, and two instance-segmentation models, YOLOv8s-seg and YOLO11s-seg, were trained and compared on it. YOLOv8s-seg reaches a recall of 0.97 against 0.88 and runs at 56.5 frames per second on a Quadro RTX 3000 GPU, and was therefore selected. For the inverse-kinematics module a 7–15–15–4 feedforward network with 424 weights was trained by the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm over ten independent runs, giving a joint angle error of 2.2164 ± 0.1811° and a position error of 9.96 mm. On a continuous circular trajectory, the network gives a position RMS error of 3.461 mm with a standard deviation of only 1.30 mm, so the error is largely a near-constant systematic offset.

items.title: Chiral Cavity Vacua as Local Generators and Probes of Non-Abelian Kitaev Topology
items.abstract: We show how a gyrotropic cavity vacuum generates, probes, and spatially programs non-Abelian topology in the Kitaev honeycomb model. Gauge-consistent virtual-photon elimination produces a universal helicity-odd interaction $\mathrm{i}[P_x,P_y]$ alongside same-order even dressing. For the leading bond polarization, this commutator is exactly the Kitaev three-spin mass. Mode normalization imposes a thermodynamic constraint: one extended normalized mode gives a local mass that vanishes with sample area, whereas a localized mode writes a finite topological island and a finite mode density enables a bulk mass. The exact Majorana solution yields helicity-reversed Chern gaps and edge propagation, while integrated circular dichroism exactly measures the mass generator, $\langle\mathrm{i}[P_x,P_y]\rangle=-\sqrt3p^2\langle O_3\rangle$. Real-space calculations reveal a non-Abelian island and a helicity wall with two co-propagating Majorana modes. Uniform helicity reversal is a Dirac-mass quench with $n_{\rm ex}\proptoτ_Q^{-1}$, whereas moving a wall localizes the gap closing. The equilibrium vacuum kernel contains sum-frequency rather than resonant denominators. These results establish distinct criteria for local and bulk cavity-induced topology.

items.title: Numerical study of nozzle configuration effects on dynamic afterburning characteristics of rocket exhaust plume
items.abstract: A detailed method for analyzing the multifrequency energy distribution and flow structures of unsteady separated flows of rocket exhaust plume is developed to clarify the morphological and frequency-domain evolution of separation modes for different nozzle configurations. We performed large eddy simulations of the dynamic afterburning reaction flow within rocket exhaust plumes from the nozzle exit downstream. A spectral proper orthogonal decomposition reduced-order model tailored to supersonic exhaust plumes was constructed to extract joint space-frequency modes of flowfield fluctuations and quantify the evolution of coherent structures under multi-frequency energy weighting. We compared the separation-mode morphology and dominant frequency characteristics in the afterburning flow fields of identical exit area rectangular and circular nozzles and analyzed the mechanisms by which nozzle geometry modulates vortex-induced entrainment during afterburning. The results show that the rectangular nozzle yields greater plume expansion and stronger shear layer effects than those of circular nozzles. The plume core exhibits approximately 45° axis switching, and localized overexpansion occurs near the nozzle corners. For the circular nozzle, increasing azimuthal order yields progressively finer coherent structures with retained rotational symmetry; for the rectangular nozzle, the geometric asymmetry redistributes modal energy toward higher azimuthal wavenumbers, and physically meaningful structures arise from the coupling of multiple azimuthal modes. The pressure field exhibits an energy peak near St = 0.01. In the medium-frequency band ( St = 0.005–0.02, i.e., 500–2000 Hz), the modal energy of the rectangular nozzle is less than that of the circular nozzle, indicating a weaker influence of the Kelvin–Helmholtz instability. This study provides a systematic characterization of the dynamic afterburning behavior under different nozzle exit geometries, offering physical insight int

items.title: Irregular weight-one Eisenstein series and Euler systems
items.abstract: Let $f=E_1(χ_1,χ_2)$ be an irregular Eisenstein series of weight one, that is, with $χ_1(p)=χ_2(p)$, and consider the generically cuspidal ordinary family passing through it. When $χ_1$, $χ_2$ and $χ_1χ_2^{-1}$ are primitive of the same conductor, we show that the specialization at $f$ of the modular-symbol $p$-adic $L$-function of this family, with periods taken in the cohomology of the compactified modular curves, factors as a product of two Kubota--Leopoldt $p$-adic $L$-functions attached to $χ_1$ and $χ_2$. Since there are no complex critical values in weight one, the factorization is obtained directly from the cohomological construction: we compute the tame-twisted modular measure by means of the localized Sharifi map and explicit reciprocity, and show that tame twisting identifies the compact period modules at weight one. This gives a weight-one analogue of the factorization of Bellaïche--Dasgupta for critical-slope Eisenstein series. As applications, and under explicit specialization hypotheses, we compare Kato classes with circular units, Heegner classes with elliptic units, and diagonal cycles with Kato classes through two successive Eisenstein degenerations. We also discuss the passage from compact to open periods, and include an exposition of the congruence and degeneration methods underlying these comparisons.

items.title: Nonlinear Vacuum Medium Model 4.0: A Falsifiable Nonlinear Substrate Model for Emergent Quantum and Gravitational Dynamics
items.abstract: The Nonlinear Vacuum Medium (NVM) Model 4.0 presents a falsifiable theoretical framework investigating whether quantum phenomena, particle-like excitations, electromagnetic behavior, and gravitational dynamics can emerge from the nonlinear organization of an underlying physical substrate. Rather than assuming that quantum fields and effective spacetime geometry are fundamental, NVM examines their possible emergence through collective dynamics governed by a continuous, nonmechanistic medium. The framework introduces a real, nonnegative magnitude field and a unit-vector orientation field defined on a fixed 3+1-dimensional Minkowski background. Their coupled nonlinear evolution provides a mathematical setting for investigating localized configurations, propagation, stability, and effective physical observables. Particles are proposed as persistent localized organizations, while measurement is explored as an objective stabilization process rather than an observer-dependent creation of reality. Version 4.0 develops the canonical field structure, variational dynamics, topological considerations, stability criteria, and mathematical conditions required for consistent evolution. It also establishes a staged correspondence program addressing quantum observables, probabilistic measurement outcomes, electromagnetic field behavior, and effective gravitational geometry. The principal contribution is a unified mathematical research architecture that distinguishes established results, conditional constructions, and unresolved derivations. Particular emphasis is placed on well-posedness, nonlinear persistence, empirical correspondence, and the avoidance of circular explanations of emergent spacetime. NVM does not claim to have reproduced quantum mechanics or general relativity in full. Instead, it identifies explicit mathematical obligations and potential observational tests through which the proposed substrate ontology can be independently evaluated, refined, or falsified against

items.title: Core-angle controlled dispersion engineering in a sector-truncated photonic crystal fiber for optical communication applications
items.abstract: By altering their microstructured architecture, photonic crystal fibers provide us with great design versatility. In this work, we present a particular kind of photonic crystal fiber with a unique core form and use simulations to examine its characteristics. This new design is different from circular-core photonic crystal fibers because it has a core region that is cut off at certain angles giving us more control over how light behaves. We looked at five core-angle configurations: 360°, 350°, 340°, 330°, and 320°. We studied how these configurations affect the fiber’s properties over a wavelength range of 1–2 μm. When we reduced the core angle, we found that it changed the refractive index, the amount of power in the core, the effective mode area, the nonlinear coefficient, the confinement loss, and the chromatic dispersion. Our simulation results show that cutting off the core at angles changes how light is distributed and how the fiber works, but it still keeps the light confined. We observed that the effective mode area decreased and the nonlinear response increased for truncated-core configurations. This means that the light is more localized within the guiding region.

items.title: New geophysical insights into gold mineralization at Gabal Abu Marawat, Central Eastern Desert, Egypt
items.abstract: The Abu Marawat district in the Central Eastern Desert of Egypt hosts significant gold mineralization, yet the deep structural and magmatic controls governing its distribution have remained poorly constrained. This study applies an integrated magnetic interpretation workflow to resolve the structural architecture of the mineral system. By combining reduced-to-pole (RTP) and upward-continued fields with advanced edge-detection filters (TAHG, LTHG) and automated lineament extraction, we document a deep-seated, regionally persistent N–S to NNE–SSW shear corridor. This D3-related structural framework overprints earlier NE–SW and NW–SE fabrics and exerts first-order control on gold localization along rheological contacts. Crucially, Circular Feature Transform (CFT) analysis identifies depth-persistent, ring-like magnetic anomalies coincident with felsic intrusions at Abu Marawat gold mine and G. Wae’ra. These CFT-defined circular magnetic anomalies, tentatively interpreted as possible intrusive centers, raise the hypothesis that Abu Marawat may host a hybrid orogenic–magmatic component, which requires independent verification. Depth estimations using Euler deconvolution and Source Parameter Imaging (SPI) define a vertically integrated architecture: shallow shear-hosted rock units (< 0.8 km) are connected via deep-rooted fault networks (resolved > 1.5 km depth). Finally, a fuzzy-logic prospectivity model was developed by integrating structural complexity, CFT anomalies, depth solutions, and lithologies. The model is spatially consistent with known deposits falling within high fuzzy-membership (high-favorability) zones, which were used, in part, to inform the model's lithological favorability criteria; this spatial coincidence should therefore be interpreted with caution rather than as independent validation and delineates several underexplored, high-favorability segments along the Semna–Miranda Gossans gold mines and Abu Marawat corridor. items.title: Adelic–Gamma–Theta Structure Preservation and Constant Ledgers in Spectral Approaches to the Riemann Hypothesis
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.abstract: We organize spectral approaches to the Riemann Hypothesis around the Adelic–Gamma–Theta factorization of the completed zeta function. The deductive spine consists of four links: a master equation independent of the zeros, a self-adjoint realization, a structural identification of the completed spectral determinant with the completed zeta function, and a structural critical-line parameterization. We prove the independence and self-adjointness links in the Rindler–Majorana, Horn, Carathéodory–Fejér, and Prime Fock frameworks. We prove the Hadamard alignment theorem, the central constant ledger, the smooth zero- counting constants for primitive Dirichlet characters, the matrix form of the Weil positivity criterion, the continuous Carathéodory–Fejér zero localization for convolution operators, a Galerkin obstruction excluding unitary equivalence between finite truncations and infinite limit operators, certified two-sided bounds for the Weil profile on [−0.8, 0.8], the Landau– Widom decay law for the Weil profile, and the interior-gap propagation theorem for finite- window Weil positivity. The global Weil positivity is reduced to the construction of outer arithmetic bounds for arbitrarily large windows. The TEBAC G1–G4 inputs, the Horn zero-set rigidity, the Yamaguchi spectral matching condition, and the Rindler–Majorana Mellin–Barnes correspondence are stated with their precise non-circularity conditions.

items.title: Perfluorocarbon emissions from aluminum electrolysis: Generation mechanisms, abatement strategies, and carbon neutrality pathways
A material-parameter-driven velocity-corrected phase-coherence fusion algorithm for total focusing imaging of CFRP defects
items.abstract: Conventional ultrasonic total focusing method (TFM) imaging of carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) laminates is limited by anisotropic propagation-time mismatch and structural noise, which impair the detection and localization of small, deeply buried defects. Existing velocity-corrected phase-coherence methods often rely on experimentally obtained or pre-fitted group-velocity profiles. To reduce this dependence, a material-parameter-driven velocity-corrected phase-coherence fusion method is proposed. An angle-dependent effective group-velocity model is first established from CFRP material parameters through elastic-stiffness-matrix construction, Christoffel-equation-based wave-velocity calculation, and reverse ray tracing. The resulting model is used to calculate anisotropic propagation delays for velocity-corrected total focusing method (VC-TFM) reconstruction. The Hilbert transform is then applied to extract the instantaneous phase of full matrix capture signals, and a circular coherence factor (CCF) is used to weight the VC-TFM image, yielding a phase-coherence-enhanced total focusing method (PCE-TFM) image for structural-noise suppression. Experiments were performed on a CFRP laminate containing 18 flat-bottom holes with diameters of 2, 3, and 4 mm and buried depths of 7–17.5 mm. VC-TFM reduced the average depth error from 2.51% to 0.52%, corresponding to a 79.4% relative reduction, and reduced the maximum absolute localization error from 0.50 mm to 0.15 mm. After CCF weighting, the average signal-to-noise ratios of the 2, 3, and 4 mm defects reached 14.17, 20.02, and 28.62 dB in PCE-TFM, respectively, compared with 3.04, 4.67, and 8.92 dB in conventional TFM. These results indicate that velocity correction mainly improves propagation-delay matching and defect localization, while phase-coherence weighting mainly suppresses structural noise and enhances defect contrast. The proposed method improves the quantitative accuracy and detectability of small, deeply b

items.title: Lamb Wave Monitoring Method for Delamination Damage in Carbon-Fiber-Reinforced Polymer Composite Materials Based on a Graph Convolution–Transformer Fusion Network
items.abstract: Accurate detection, quantitative assessment, and localization of delamination damage in composite materials remain major challenges in structural health monitoring (SHM). This paper proposes Adaptive Graph Transformer (AGFormer), a framework integrating a graph convolutional neural network with Transformer encoders, for size quantification, severity grading, and localization of circular delamination damage in carbon-fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) laminates. First, ten-dimensional edge features, including root-mean-square deviation, correlation coefficient, energy ratio, time-of-flight shift, and spectral variation, are extracted from differences between multipath Lamb-wave baseline and damaged-state signals. These features are aggregated into 42-dimensional enhanced node features to fuse multipath damage information at the sensor nodes. Second, a multimodal adjacency-matrix construction strategy combining sensor spatial distance with signal time–frequency distance is proposed to provide an adaptive topology for the graph convolutional network. On this basis, the AGFormer model employs three residual graph-convolution modules to extract local topological features, a multilayer perceptron for dimensional mapping, and two multi-head self-attention Transformer encoder layers to capture long-range dependencies among sensors. Attention-gated pooling and parallel output heads then simultaneously perform damage-radius regression and four-class severity classification. In addition, damage-centroid localization is achieved by combining multipath damage indices with the RAPID (Reconstruction Algorithm for Probabilistic Inspection of Damage) elliptical imaging algorithm. Experimental validation was conducted on a 450 mm × 450 mm six-ply CFRP laminate instrumented with a 12-piezoelectric-sensor network, under progressively increasing simulated delamination damage. The model was trained and evaluated using five-fold cross-validation grouped by damage size, while Gaussian-noise i

items.title: The Spatialization of Ecological Literacy: Reconceptualizing Pre-Pottery Neolithic Megaliths as Seasonal Knowledge-Transfer Hubs
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.abstract: The traditional paradigm in Near Eastern archaeology routinely classifies architectural complexity and monumental scale in the Pre-Pottery Neolithic (PPN) as evidence of emergent, centralized religious hierarchies ("temples"). This paper challenges this view by proposing an alternative operational framework: megalithic complexes across the Taş Tepeler network functioned primarily as advanced, seasonal socio-ecological training hubs and dynamic knowledge-transfer installations. Driven by the severe, abrupt climate fluctuations of the Younger Dryas (c. 12,900–11,600 cal. BP), pre-agricultural societies required highly resilient, adaptive information-sharing networks to navigate localized ecological bottlenecks. Rather than static spaces for dogmatic worship, these circular stone enclosures, subterranean bedrock chambers, and iconographic pillars are modeled as spatial mnemonic hardware, behavioral simulators, and regional skill-sharing summits. This model traces a fundamental cognitive split between the fluid, verb-based "grammar of animacy" characterizing ecological engineering and the rigid, noun-based abstractions of later monoculture agrarian states. Furthermore, the deliberate backfilling of these structures is reframed as an intentional, off-season winterization technology designed to insulate physical assets from environmental weathering. This framework shifts the interpretive lens from anachronistic state-level religious structures to an organized, high-investment system of human capability, seasonal landscape optimization, and inter-communal ecological literacy.

items.title: A Modular Strategy for Collagen-Mimetic Peptides Using Diastereoselective Ugi Reactions
items.abstract: Here, we report a highly efficient and modular strategy to synthesize characteristic tripeptide units via diastereoselective Ugi multicomponent reactions and use them to construct collagen-mimetic peptides (CMPs). Biocatalytic desymmetrization of prochiral cyclic amines provides optically pure chiral imines, which are combined with readily available isocyanides and amino acid building blocks to generate stereodefined tripeptide modules for solid-phase peptide synthesis. Monoamine oxidase N (MAO-N) mediated desymmetrization afforded imines in excellent enantiomeric excess (>99% ee), while the corresponding tripeptide modules were obtained with high diastereomeric ratios (>92:8 d.r.). After assembly into medium-sized CMPs, Circular Dichroism (CD) spectroscopy confirmed triple-helix formation. The synthetic analogues exhibited melting temperatures (Tm) of up to 39.2 °C, corresponding to a decrease of only 3.2 °C relative to the parent Hyp CMP sequence. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that the bicyclic substituents optimize local packing via enhanced inter-chain van der Waals interactions and localized desolvation, rendering the fully folded analogues thermodynamically indistinguishable. This strategy enables the modular introduction of unnatural proline analogues into CMPs and provides a platform to rapidly evaluate how proline-analogue structure and stereochemistry influence triple-helix formation and stability.

items.title: Geometrically optimized superhydrophobic platforms for enhanced duckweed cultivation and nutrient recovery
items.abstract: Duckweed is an important resource for bioenergy and animal feed, yet conventional cultivation methods often suffer from uneven nutrient distribution and excess water consumption. This study introduced novel superhydrophobic (SHP) platforms in three geometries: rectangular (SHP-R), oval (SHP-O) and circular (SHP-C), with the surface area standardised as 53.5 cm 2 . The primary objective was to investigate how geometrically optimized thin-film environment influence biomass productivity and nutrient uptake. After 7 days of cultivation, plantlets grown on the SHP platforms significantly outperformed the control. Lemna minor achieved a relative growth rate (RGR) of 0.1078 ± 0.0139 day − 1 , while Spirodela polyrhiza attained 0.0878 ± 0.0051 day − 1 , surpassing the control by 2.37-fold and 1.64-fold, respectively. The higher surface-to-volume (S/V) ratio and shallow liquid layer are hypothesized to facilitate localized nutrient transport efficiency, coinciding with high nutrient removal efficiencies where L. mino r removed 89.97% ammonia and 95.78% phosphate, while S. polyrhiza achieved 100% ammonia and 87.17% phosphate removal. Furthermore, the harvested biomass maintained high nutritional quality, with protein contents of 31.02 ± 3.85% for L. minor and 29.14 ± 2.41% for S. polyrhiza . These results demonstrated that geometrically optimized SHP systems can revolutionize duckweed cultivation by maximizing uptake efficiency and minimizing water usage. By providing a transformative avenue for high-density biomass production and sustainable resource recovery, this technology advances the field toward more resilient and efficient circular bioeconomy models.

items.title: Directional emission in a CQW-gain hybrid plasmonic nanolaser enabled by nanorod array symmetry breaking
The Healer’s Touch in 19th-Century Gujarat: A Clinical and Codicological Analysis of the ‘Dambha-Kriyā-Pratikāra’ Manuscript
items.abstract: The evolution of Ayurvedic surgical practices is often viewed through the lens of classical Sanskrit Samhitas; however, the true dynamism of these traditions is frequently preserved in regional, practitioner-oriented manuals. The Dambha-kriyā-pratikāra, a 19th-century Sanskrit manuscript dated 1898 CE and authored by Vinayak Rao Sadashiv, serves as a critical primary source for understanding the localization of Agni Karma (therapeutic cauterization) in rural Gujarat. Archived at the Oriental Institute of M.S. University, Baroda, this 31-verse manual represents a significant departure from purely academic texts, functioning instead as a highly specialized field guide for community-specific health challenges. This research explores the clinical and codicological nuances of the manuscript, aiming to demonstrate how classical surgical theory was adapted to serve the occupational and ergonomic needs of the rural labouring classes. By analyzing the physical state of the paper manuscript alongside its technical content, the study identifies a sophisticated system of anatomical mapping based on three primary geometric shapes: Vartula (circular), Lambaka (longitudinal), and Valaya (ring-shaped). These configurations were strategically employed to manage thermal distribution across more than 25 systemic diseases. A particularly profound finding is the manuscript’s documentation of Kuranta Vata, a musculoskeletal pathology explicitly linked to the Mochi (cobbler) community of the Baroda region. The text details a unique 15-point cautery protocol involving the toes and knee joints, utilizing the Vyatyasa (contralateral) principle to address chronic pain resulting from the repetitive, professional postures of the artisan class. Furthermore, the manual describes a “Visceral Map” for gastrointestinal disorders, such as Atisara and Grahani, using a complex Kūrmapāda (Tortoise-foot) pattern of marks below the navel. From a codicological perspective, the scribe’s editing habits—inclu

items.title: A Comparative Economic and Meteorological Analysis Between Solid-Liquid and Pure Liquid Rocket Propellant Frameworks
items.abstract: A critical gap in modern aerospace monitoring lies in systematically decoupling the direct meteorological footprints and structural economic trade-offs of solid-liquid versus pure liquid rocket propulsion architectures. Because contemporary heavy-lift launch vehicles frequently deploy multi-stage propellant configurations simultaneously, their granular physical signatures and cost metrics are often mathematically masked. To address this constraint, this study engineers an independent, two-port remote sensing framework utilizing open-source Copernicus Sentinel-5P TROPOMI satellite datasets processed via Google Earth Engine (GEE). A pure liquid hydrocarbon architecture (Falcon 9 at Kennedy Space Center, LC-39A) was directly contrasted against a mixed solid-liquid propellant matrix (Blue Bird Block 2 at Satish Dhawan Space Centre, FLP/SLP) across tightly controlled temporal windows. To insulate localized exhaust anomalies from background environmental noise, pixel values within a 5-kilometer circular buffer zone were compressed , with regional meteorological stability explicitly verified via cloud-fraction masking to insulate measurements from weather-induced scattering anomalies. The empirical data demonstrates a distinct structural divergence across both vectors: from a meteorological perspective, the pure liquid baseline architecture yielded a transient 37.65% increase in localized tropospheric nitrogen dioxide (NO2) vertical column densities (5.87 × 10-5 mol/m2 to 8.08 × 10-5 mol/m2) that rapidly dissipated. Conversely, the solid-liquid booster architecture induced an immediate, severe shift in the Absorbing Aerosol Index (AAI) from -0.52012 to -0.85124, validating a 60% escalation in persistent, highly scattering stratospheric particulates. When integrated with a structural macro-fiscal model, the findings demonstrate that transitioning away from expendable solid booster configurations toward monolithic, reusable liquid systems reduces long-term atmospheric partic

items.title: Pseudospectral Bounds and Transient Amplification in Low-Rank Economic Systems
items.abstract: Pseudospectral analysis provides a natural framework for assessing robustness, systemic vulnerability, and transient shock amplification in non-normal dynamical systems, but its direct application becomes computationally demanding in large-scale problems. Recently, a scalable framework for matrices of the form A=UV*, with U,V∈Cd×r and r≪d, was developed, and the computation of the smallest singular value of zI−A, together with several related pseudospectral problems, was reduced to structured eigenvalue problems whose dimensions depend only on the low rank r. Building on this framework, the present paper develops further theoretical and computational results motivated by systemic-risk analysis in large-scale economic and financial interaction models. We extend the analysis to diagonally shifted low-rank systems and derive a characterization of pseudospectral boundary intersections with circular trajectories centered at the diagonal shift. For approximately low-rank matrices, known localization results are used to derive computable lower and upper bounds for the distance to instability. As a new theoretical contribution, we establish an analytical lower bound for the smallest eigenvalue of the reduced matrix MU,V(z), together with computable refinements involving only reduced-order quantities; the bound is shown to be sharp in a representative example. The reduced framework is further employed in the computation of the Kreiss constant and the analysis of transient amplification. Numerical experiments on large-scale economic interaction models illustrate how these results enable computationally tractable assessment of robustness and transient risk through reduced problems whose dimensions are independent of the full system size.

items.title: Strategic Optimization of Industrial Lubricants for Energy Efficiency and Asset Reliability in Saudi Arabia’s Oil and Gas Sector: A Vision 2030 Framework
items.abstract: Industrial lubrication is usually regarded as a maintenance item rather than as a means of achieving energy efficiency, asset reliability, and lifecycle value. This difference is important in Saudi Arabia's oil and gas industry, since pumps, compressors, turbines, gearboxes, hydraulic systems and auxiliary equipment have to operate under heavy loads, thermal stress, a risk of contamination and strict availability requirements. This study brings together peer-reviewed evidence published between 2020 and 2025 in order to look at how lubricant selection, application engineering, contamination control, condition monitoring, predictive analytics and sustainable formulation can be incorporated into a strategic lubrication framework that is in line with Saudi Vision 2030. To do this, a structured integrative approach is applied drawing on the fields of tribology, reliability engineering, condition monitoring, digital transformation and the literature on Saudi energy transition. The evidence shows that lubricant optimisation improves efficiency by reducing friction and churning losses, enhances reliability by ensuring good film integrity and controlling wear, and has an impact on maintenance costs by enabling earlier detection of degradation and allowing for better timing of interventions. Yet value is sacrificed when lubricant decisions are left scattered among the procurement, operations, laboratories and maintenance departments. It is therefore suggested that a framework geared towards Saudi Vision 2030 should be based on five interconnected capabilities: asset criticality, application-specific lubricant engineering, condition-based surveillance, data-driven decision support, and circular resource management. The review concludes that the greatest opportunity does not lie in simply using higher-performance oils, but in treating lubrication as an asset-management system that delivers measurable results in the areas of energy, reliability, environment and localisation.

items.title: Study on Corrosion Imaging of Aircraft Riveted Structures Based on Pulsed Eddy Current
items.abstract: Precise quantification of minute defects in pulsed eddy current (PEC) testing is fundamentally limited by the broadening of defect boundary response signals caused by eddy current field diffusion — a key factor that undermines detection accuracy. To improve quantification precision for such small defects, this paper introduces an adaptive power-law sharpening signal processing approach. This method incorporates an algorithm that dynamically tunes the power-law exponent γ according to normalized peak height, thereby compressing the edges of the response envelope and reducing the impact of boundary effects. Subsequently, piecewise cubic Hermite interpolating polynomial (PCHIP) interpolation is applied to generate a high-density data field. This data field is then combined with K-means clustering for automatic segmentation of the defect region, enabling precise extraction of both the area and two-dimensional coordinates. Experiments were conducted using a pulsed eddy current array sensor to detect multi-layer riveted blocks containing corrosion defects. Experimental results verify that the proposed method effectively suppresses the adverse effects of eddy current diffusion on boundary resolution. For circular corrosion defects with diameters from 5 mm to 12 mm at identical burial depth, the method achieves a relative area error below 16.3% and a localization error within 1.5 mm, significantly outperforming conventional threshold-based approaches. This work provides a systematic signal processing framework that addresses the fundamental limitation of boundary broadening in pulsed eddy current testing, paving the way for high-precision quantification of minute defects.

items.title: Flood vulnerability modelling in informal aquatic settlements using ensemble machine learning and multi-source earth observation: a case study of Makoko, Lagos
items.abstract: Flood vulnerability modelling in informal aquatic communities is methodologically underdeveloped, as traditional frameworks emphasize formal urban infrastructure and lack the spatial resolution and operational outputs necessary for community-level risk management. This study establishes a high-resolution ensemble machine learning framework that incorporates Sentinel-1 SAR imagery, Sentinel-2 optical data, Digital Elevation Models, and socio-environmental conditioning variables within a Google Earth Engine cloud computing environment to assess flood vulnerability in Makoko, a densely populated informal aquatic settlement in Lagos, Nigeria, with approximately 250,000 residents. A localized Flood Vulnerability Index was developed using multi-source earth observation and anthropogenic indicators. Following correction of target circularity and spatial autocorrelation identified during peer review, spatially cross-validated evaluation (Random Forest with Borderline-SMOTE2 class balancing) achieved AUC = 0.879 (95% CI: 0.872–0.885), outperforming XGBoost and Logistic Regression on all metrics. Explainable AI utilizing SHAP analysis identified nocturnal light intensity, proximity to roadways, and water indices as primary vulnerability drivers, overturning the traditional hierarchy of terrain-dominated conditioning factors and highlighting the significance of anthropogenic surface alterations in aquatic settlement flood dynamics. The model outputs were implemented into a synthetic sandbox dashboard, classifying 4,816 of 14,448 grid cells (10 m spatial units) as Critical risk to at-risk homes, effectively converting modelling outputs into actionable community-level flood early warnings. The framework offers a replicable and transferable modelling methodology for assessing flood vulnerability in data-deficient informal aquatic settings throughout the Global South.

items.title: ECOLINGUISTICS IN DIGITAL MARKETING DISCOURSE: A CORPUS-BASED CRITICAL ANALYSIS OF SUSTAINABILITY NARRATIVES, CHALLENGES, AND OPPORTUNITIES IN PAKISTANI ORGANIZATIONS
items.venue: Insights (Bhalwal) International Journal of Humanities Management and Social Sciences
items.abstract: Digital marketing has become a key area in today's world where companies communicate their ideas of sustainability, environmental responsibility and socio-economic development. This study challenges the sustainability narratives from a limited set of official digital communication materials created by Nestlé Pakistan, Unilever Pakistan, Jazz, HBL and Engro. This data set includes twelve carefully selected samples from public organizational websites, including official websites, campaign materials and corporate sustainability reports. The analysis is based on the framework of ecolinguistics of Stibbe (2021), which deconstructs ideological constructs, framing strategies, metaphors, evaluative language, identity formation, conviction, erasure mechanisms, salience, and narrative patterns. These "qualitative" interpretations are supported by basic corpus frequency data and thematic-key word analysis. The lexicon is clearly dominated by certain content words, such as "waste" (18 occurrences), "environmental" (15), "energy" (13) and "plastic" (13). The main themes in this lexical profile are: resource management, waste mitigation, renewable energy adoption, and climate action. The qualitative analysis shows that the core themes around which organizations have defined sustainability are stewardship, innovation, circularity and long-term responsibility, shifting the paradigm from traditional perceptions of sustainability as the role of the government to a more modern view in which organizations and stakeholder alliances are seen as key drivers of change. The analysis also exposes key omissions, however, in the context of what can be achieved in a promotional text: broader supply-chain trade-offs, growth in consumption, localised ecological costs and the need for independent verification are not consistently visible. Therefore, these findings only offer a explorative function and do not have the power to conclude on environmental performance or to identify cases of greenwashi

items.title: Unraveling the mechanistic role of trace Nb microalloying in inclusion evolution and pitting corrosion resistance of 304 austenitic stainless steel
items.venue: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
items.abstract: : Trace Nb microalloying is a promising strategy for mitigating inclusion-mediated pitting in austenitic stainless steels, but the mechanisms linking Nb-induced inclusion evolution to localized corrosion remain unclear. The effect of 0.05 wt.% Nb on 304 austenitic stainless steel was systematically investigated using thermodynamic calculations, microstructural characterization, electrochemical and immersion tests, XPS and by surface chemical composition analysis. Nb refined the austenitic microstructure, reducing the area-weighted equivalent circular diameter from 19.2 to 11.4 μm and increasing the low-angle grain-boundary fraction from 35.2% to 61.7%. More importantly, Nb modified the inclusion population, reducing inclusion density and size, promoting finer Nb-rich oxides, and suppressing sulfide-rich phases. The corrosion current density decreased by more than one order of magnitude, accompanied by increased charge-transfer resistance and substantially suppressed stable pit growth. XPS revealed Nb-O species and a more oxide-rich passive film, while AFM/SKPFM showed reduced local electrochemical heterogeneity after Nb addition. These findings indicate that trace Nb enhances pitting-corrosion resistance through a coupled mechanism involving inclusion stabilization, reduced micro-galvanic activity, and improved passive-film stability, thereby delaying passive-film breakdown and inhibiting the transition from pit initiation to stable propagation.

items.title: GIS-Based Morphometric Analysis and Hydrological Assessment of the Hor Al-Shuwaicha Drainage Basins, Eastern Iraq
items.abstract: This study presents a comprehensive quantitative morphometric analysis of the five drainage basins of Hor Al-Shuwaicha in eastern Iraq, which cover a total area of 22,245.54 km². Previous morphometric studies have primarily focused on three basins (Torsaq, Shosharin, and Galal Badra), the morphometric characteristics of the entire drainage system insufficiently characterized. A 30 m Digital Elevation Model was processed using Geographic Information System techniques to delineate watershed boundaries and extract the drainage network, followed by the calculation of twenty-one linear, areal, and relief morphometric parameters using standard equations. The seventh-order stream represents the highest stream order. The Sayed Ghazal Basin exhibits the highest basin relief and a drainage intensity of 0.41, suggesting that rugged topography may enhance drainage. In contrast, the lowest drainage intensity (0.38) in the Galal Badra Basin suggests lower drainage response and potential temporary surface-water accumulation, which may contribute to localized flooding in some areas. Drainage density analysis reveals that the Shosharin Basin exhibits the highest drainage density (1.15 km/km²), indicating a potentially greater tendency for rapid surface runoff. Whereas the Mandaly Basin, with the lowest drainage density (1.09 km/km²), indicates relatively higher groundwater recharge potential. Furthermore, drainage texture ranges from very coarse to fine, while the form factor, circularity ratio, and elongation ratio consistently indicate predominantly elongated basin geometry, suggesting a potentially lower tendency for rapid concentration of runoff. These findings provide quantitative morphometric evidence that can support preliminary flood-hazard assessment and groundwater-recharge evaluation.

items.title: СТРАТЕГИЧЕСКИЕ ПРИОРИТЕТЫ ЗЕЛЕНОЙ ЭКОНОМИКИ КАК ОСНОВА УСТОЙЧИВОГО МАКРОЭКОНОМИЧЕСКОГО РОСТА В РЕСПУБЛИКЕ КАЗАХСТАН И РОССИИ
items.abstract: В статье исследуются стратегические приоритеты зеленой экономики как факторы устойчивого макроэкономического роста Республики Казахстан и Российской Федерации. Цель исследования состоит в обосновании такой модели зеленой трансформации, при которой экологические ограничения преобразуются в стимулы повышения ресурсной производительности, технологического обновления, инвестиционной активности и устойчивости экономики к внешним и климатическим шокам. Информационную основу составили действующие нормативные правовые акты и документы стратегического планирования Казахстана и России, официальная статистика, материалы профильных государственных органов, а также современные исследования ученых Казахстана, России, государств СНГ и зарубежных стран. Показано, что рост установленной мощности низкоуглеродной генерации сам по себе не обеспечивает зеленого макроэкономического эффекта: результат зависит от энерго- и ресурсоэффективности, состояния сетевой инфраструктуры, технологической локализации, структуры инвестиций, циркулярности производства и качества климатической адаптации. Для Казахстана особое значение имеют снижение энергоемкости, модернизация углеродоемких отраслей, развитие сетей и гибких мощностей, повышение водной производительности и формирование внутренней технологической базы зеленых проектов. Для России приоритет связан с использованием существующего низкоуглеродного потенциала атомной и гидроэнергетики для структурно-технологической модернизации, повышения ресурсоэффективности, развития экономики замкнутого цикла и конкурентоспособности промышленности. Обоснован авторский принцип двойной результативности зеленой политики, согласно которому каждый значимый проект или мера должны одновременно иметь измеримый экологический и макроэкономический результат. Сделан вывод о необходимости перехода от отраслевой экологической политики к интегрированной институциональнопроизводительной стратегии зеленого роста. items.title: Ventricular Septal Pulsed Field Ablation: Noninvasive, Longitudinal Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Assessment of Lesion Structure and Function in a Preclinical Model
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ventricular pulsed field ablation (PFA) is an emerging myocardial ablation strategy, but lesion evolution and noninvasive assessment in ventricular myocardium remain incompletely characterized. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate interventricular septal (IVS) PFA in a preclinical swine model and assess the feasibility of serial cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) for lesion characterization. METHODS: Eight swine were allocated to acute and chronic cohorts. PFA was delivered to the IVS using a variable-loop circular catheter (VLCC). Multimodality assessments included electroanatomic mapping, serial CMR, echocardiography and pathology. Pathological lesion-depth measurements were obtained at terminal timepoints, whereas serial CMR enabled within-animal longitudinal assessment. CMR-pathology correspondence was evaluated using anatomically matched slices. RESULTS: Serial CMR showed reductions in late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)-derived lesion mass and volume by Day 21, with stabilization thereafter. Among 37 matched CMR-pathology slices from five animals, CMR-LGE-derived lesion-depth measurements showed positive association with pathology-derived measurements (Pearson's r = 0.77), moderate reliability (ICC = 0.74), and a mean difference of 0.03 mm, with 95% limits of agreement from -1.15 to 1.21 mm. Both methods showed decreased chronic lesion depths, consistent with lesion maturation and fibrotic remodeling. Transient reductions in left ventricular ejection fraction and regional septal mechanics were observed after PFA, followed by partial recovery. CONCLUSION: Ventricular septal PFA produced well-demarcated lesions that evolved into chronic fibrotic scars. Serial CMR enabled noninvasive assessment of lesion localization, depth, and temporal evolution, with lesion-depth measurements showing correspondence with anatomically matched pathological measurements, supporting the feasibility of CMR for longitudinal assessment after ventricular PFA.

items.title: [Global Livingry Governance Architecture I Part 19]: Redefining National Defense in the Era of Hybrid Warfare: From Traditional Hardware Procurement to Infrastructure Autonomy Density, Bio-Logistics, and Autonomous Algorithmic Matrices.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.abstract: The traditional NATO defense spending model of 2% of GDP faces a critical structural crisis. Channeling financial resources into standalone hardware and centralized ammunition depots creates a fragile defense architecture vulnerable to modern hybrid warfare. This paper argues that national security cannot be measured solely by lethal weapon quantity, but must instead be defined by: Infrastructure Autonomy Density: Localized autonomy in renewable energy microgrids and clean water supplies. Self-Sustaining Green Military: Transforming defense infrastructure into practical peacetime civic utilities to foster voluntary community participation. Biomedical Optimization: Eradicating Central Nervous System (CNS) fatigue in personnel using empirical biomedical data from PubMed. Algorithmic Chessboard Architecture: Utilizing real-time technological ecosystems (passive multisensor mesh and pre-launch AI analytics) to eliminate the "fog of war". Nature Restoration and Reproductive Value: Shifting budgets from weapon consumption to ecosystem restoration, easing household living costs, and resolving the trust crisis underlying declining birth rates. Core Mathematical Models & Frameworks 1. Budget Allocation Optimization Model (M_alloc): Maximizes strategic resilience under fiscal constraints (B_total) while minimizing resource attrition risk caused by centralized structures. 2. Structural Risk & Vulnerability Function (Psi_risk): Quantifies systemic vulnerability based on target concentration density and personnel CNS fatigue. 3. Distributed Survival Index (S_survival): Evaluates sub-regional self-sufficiency in renewable energy, clean water, and circular agriculture during a central grid collapse. 4. Asymmetric Cost-Benefit Comparison Matrix: Contrasts the financial deficits of traditional centralized hardware (e.g., using multimillion-dollar interceptors against cheap drones) with decentralized algorithmic cyber-takeover protocols and green microgrid infrastructures.

items.title: Beyond the database: Information management requirements for material passports supporting design for disassembly and adaptability
Contextualizing a process information approach in material passports: a case on modelling circular façade product requirements
items.abstract: Information gaps are a key challenge in transitioning to a circular economy, particularly beyond the first use of building products. Material passports could bridge these information gaps by acting as shared information repositories across actors and product stages. However, current material passport research primarily defines product-centric information requirements addressing the here and now, while process-related information to enable future reuse remains less examined. This research developed a stepwise method to identify contextual process information requirements. The method combined a canvas linking process, organizational and information dimensions from the end of use to next use with process modelling. The canvas was tested in a workshop that produced a window maintenance contract case, which was translated into a BPMN process model to derive its information requirements. Their analysis confirmed that across literature and regulations, process information is largely overlooked, a gap that widens towards next use. Overlooked requirements concern capabilities, sequencing dependencies, actors’ roles and agreements. The results suggest material passports should shift from accumulating perishable product descriptions towards sustaining circular models. The maintenance contract case illustrates how service agreements could initiate this shift and keep material passports updated, while the method offers practitioners a way to design circular model adoption.

items.title: Machine-Readable Material Passports for Photopolymer Products: Composition Boundaries, Process History and End of Life
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.abstract: Digital product and material passports are moving from conceptual circular-economy tools toward operational lifecycle information systems. For photopolymer products, a useful passport must represent more than product identity: it must preserve formulation boundaries, print and post-cure history, service-relevant state changes, repair or recoating events, and end-of-life constraints. This review proposes a machine-readable passport architecture that separates public, controlled and confidential information while retaining provenance. It emphasises state transitions and uncertainty, because a printed photopolymer component can no longer be described adequately by the identity of the original liquid resin alone.
