items.title: Anti-Dumping Policies of BRICS Nations: Intra-BRICS Vulnerabilities and Reforms
items.abstract: The urgency for transformation in governance is imperative to address the multi-faceted challenges impeding sustainable development. Particularly for the BRICS nations, the integration of comprehensive governance mechanisms can catalyze economic health and social progress. This book explores the concept of "integrative governance" in the context of BRICS countries, highlighting its potential to reconcile rapid economic growth with sustainable development. Integrative governance, rooted in inclusivity and adaptability, encompasses diverse domains such as participatory governance, human capital development, and macroeconomic stability. It provides insights into how BRICS nations can leverage governance to mitigate poverty, inequality, bolster rural development, and enhance social welfare. The book will focus on thematic successes and challenges observed in BRICS nations, with a particular focus on participatory governance, human capital and health, macroeconomic and debt management, urban local economic development, and technological advancement in governance. The book adopts a call for papers approach, promoting a transformative agenda in line with the principles of the United Nations Global Compact and promoting sustainable development.

items.title: How Circular Economy Practices Drive Sustainable Performance: A Dual‐Moderator Model of Green Culture and Environmental Dynamism in the Hotel Industry
items.abstract: This study examines how circular economy practices (CEP) influence sustainable performance (SP) in the hospitality industry. It explores the mediating role of green supply chain management (GSCM) and investigates how green organizational culture (GOC) and environmental dynamism (ED) moderate the CEP–SP relationship. Data were collected from 425 employees of four‐ and five‐star eco‐friendly hotels in Türkiye using judgmental sampling. Data were analyzed using PLS‐SEM to test the measurement and structural models, including mediation and moderation. CEP did not directly improve sustainable performance. However, GSCM fully mediated the CEP–SP relationship, indicating that circular practices must be operationalized through supply chain processes to create sustainability outcomes. Furthermore, GOC strengthened the positive effect of CEP on SP, highlighting the importance of supportive internal culture. ED also amplified the CEP–SP link, suggesting that dynamic external conditions enhance the effectiveness of circular initiatives.

items.title: Circular economy-based design alternative selection model for construction projects
items.abstract: The growing adoption of circular economy (CE) principles in construction requires systematic approaches to evaluate design alternatives. This study develops a CE-based model enabling decision makers to systematically assess and compare alternative building designs by their circularity performance. The proposed framework integrates circularity-related criteria identified through an extensive literature review and Focus Group Discussions (FGDs). Pythagorean Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (PF-AHP) is employed to determine criteria weights, while Fuzzy TOPSIS is used to rank alternative design options. The applicability of the model is demonstrated through a hypothetical design case. The findings indicate that circular design selection should extend beyond material-related considerations and also incorporate environmental, consumption-related, social, and financial dimensions. Material recyclability emerged as the most influential criterion with a global weight of 0.095, followed by wastewater reduction (0.078) and raw material consumption (0.072). The material impact dimension obtained the highest aggregate weight (0.309), followed by environmental (0.260) and consumption-related (0.232) dimensions, while social (0.106) and financial (0.094) dimensions ranked comparatively lower. The integrated PF-AHP–Fuzzy TOPSIS framework provides a systematic and transparent approach for evaluating circular design alternatives. Unlike previous studies focusing on contractor evaluation or general sustainability assessment, this research supports more informed and consistent early-stage design decision-making.

items.title: Barriers to Engagement in Circular Business Models Among Small and Medium‐Sized Enterprises: Evidence From the Irish Construction, Manufacturing and Retail/Wholesale Sectors
items.abstract: Although circular business models (CBMs) are central to the circular economy (CE) transition, their adoption among small and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs) remains limited, and evidence on barrier variation across CBMs and sectors is scarce. This study examines barriers to engagement in five CBM activities, spanning secondary raw material use, takeback, repair/maintenance, remanufacturing/refurbishment and leasing/rental, using a survey of 452 Irish SMEs in construction, manufacturing and retail/wholesale, in which respondents rated barriers for each activity. Barrier importance proves strongly contingent on CBM activity and sector, with variation also evident across firm characteristics. Only two barriers, secondary raw material costs and upfront costs of leasing/rental, are high‐priority in all sectors; several recur across sector pairs, while most bind in single activity–sector combinations. Resource‐based, institutional and contingency perspectives help explain this patterning. The findings move CBM barrier research beyond descriptive classification, provide systematic evidence on SMEs and inform more effective CE policymaking.

items.title: Circular Economy Disclosure in Europe's Automotive Sector: An Analysis of Reporting Patterns
items.abstract: According to the European Circular Economy Action Plan, the automotive industry plays a key role in Europe's transition to a circular economy (CE). Industry‐specific legislation and upcoming reporting guidelines raise the question of the current CE implementation level, which is still an underexplored research field. Based on 77 corporate reports from European automotive companies, a content analysis is conducted using a mix of a deductive and inductive code system to examine CE disclosure in terms of its reporting patterns. Overall, a wide range of CE practices are already being pursued. However, the automotive industry focuses on more easily implementable practices such as reduce and recycle activities. Frequently disclosed CE practices are generally described in more detail than those reported less often. Furthermore, the reports lack specific targets and quantitative statements. Lastly, supply chain position, compliance with voluntary reporting guidelines, and external assurance are associated with CE disclosure.

items.title: Adoption of the Sustainable Model: European Union Circular Economy and the Implementation of Environmental Regulations in Peru
authors: Ricardo Leonidas de Jesus Velez Chicoma
items.abstract: Background This study examines how selected regulatory instruments and implementation principles from the European Union circular-economy framework can be adapted to strengthen the operational effectiveness of environmental regulation in Peru. Methods The study combines documentary and comparative regulatory analysis, semi-structured interviews with two key institutional informants from PRODUCE and MINAM, and a complementary bibliometric review of 2404 open-access Scopus-indexed documents processed with bibliometrix/Biblioshiny. Results The bibliometric corpus showed an annual growth rate of 45.71%, with 91.8% of publications concentrated in 2020–2025 and 32.7% international co-authorship. The co-word network positioned circular economy as the main bridging node and connected sustainability, the European Union, policy implementation, and regulatory frameworks, while consolidated clusters around waste management and life-cycle analysis remained visible. The EU–Peru comparison showed that Peru has expanded its formal circularity architecture but still faces gaps in enforceability, measurement, product traceability, and institutional coordination. Triangulation supported seven context-sensitive measures, including sector-specific EPR strengthening, auditable circularity reporting, Digital Product Passport pilots, ecodesign, an operational waste hierarchy, circularity criteria in environmental assessment, and performance-linked incentives. Conclusions The findings support selective and sequenced regulatory adaptation rather than direct transplantation of the EU model.

items.title: Sustainable Business Model Innovation Research: Bibliometric Structures and the Emerging Frontier of Regenerative Business Models (2016–2025)
items.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
items.abstract: This study presents a bibliometric mapping of sustainable business model innovation (SBMI) research, analysing 961 Scopus‐indexed documents (2016–2025) retrieved via a title‐field Boolean query and a four‐stage screening protocol. Circular, regenerative, and resilient business models are treated as distinct, related perspectives rather than sequential stages. The corpus shows a three‐phase growth trajectory: emergence, acceleration, and consolidation, with an overall compound annual growth rate of 24.5%. Knowledge production concentrates in European institutions, led by Sweden, the UK, and Italy, anchored by Lund University. Co‐citation (four clusters) and keyword co‐occurrence (five clusters) analyses reveal a field anchored in Osterwalder and Pigneur's business model canvas. The regenerative perspective remains bibliometrically marginal, appearing as an author keyword in only 2 of 961 documents. The study clarifies the boundaries separating these perspectives and proposes a structured research agenda, positioning regeneration as an emerging, not accomplished, frontier for sustainable business model innovation scholarship.

items.title: Scaling Waste-to-Wealth Ventures in Emerging Markets: A Circular Economy Framework for Sustainable Growth
items.abstract: The circular economy offers emerging markets a route to growth that does not depend on continued resource extraction, and waste-to-wealth ventures have proliferated in response. Few achieve scale. This paper asks what distinguishes ventures that replicate across markets from those that remain confined to a single site, and develops a conceptual framework in answer. A structured review of four literatures was conducted, covering circular economy theory, waste management in developing economies, the informal recycling sector, and the relationship between circular practice and development objectives. The framework identifies three enablers of scale, namely an adaptive business model, a hybrid capital structure and policy co-creation, and argues that they act through ecosystem orchestration, the alignment of informal collectors, offtakers, municipalities and financiers around a single material flow. Scaling is specified as four stages in which the binding constraint shifts from technical proof to feedstock security, then to offtake, then to policy stability, so support instruments must be matched to stage. Four testable propositions and a set of observable indicators are stated. The framework is offered for empirical testing rather than as a validated model.

items.title: Learning from degrowth: strengthening circular economy approaches through case studies of plastic packaging and textiles
items.abstract: To date, the circular economy (CE) and degrowth literatures have had a substantially separate existence. Whilst a CE is increasingly regarded as a central element of sustainable development, its meaning is far from uniform, with diverse interpretations in both literature and practice. This heterogenous discourse mirrors the tension between green growth, degrowth and post-growth approaches in the wider sustainability debate. Moreover, whilst the idea of a CE has taken a firm hold with policymakers, there are questions regarding its adequacy for the challenges faced, especially in terms of achieving absolute reductions in environmental impacts and positive social outcomes. By contrast, the concept of degrowth calls for significant societal changes to achieve a functioning but smaller and more equitable economy. It is less politically and economically palatable than CE. Degrowth strategies, however, overlap significantly with those favored by some of the CE literature. The potential for these overlaps to support a CE capable of delivering a more sustainable future has received little attention. This paper offers both theoretical and empirical insights by exploring how degrowth and circular economy principles intersect in case studies focused on textiles and plastic packaging. Using integrative literature reviews and empirical data, the case studies assess the extent to which different stakeholders approach the CE, drawing on semi-structured interviews with textile manufacturers in Germany and stakeholders of plastic packaging on the east coast of England. Our analysis finds that the far-reaching socio-ecological transformation towards short-loop options likely necessary for a CE to confront urgent sustainability crises is seldom addressed in the literature and lies beyond the current scope of stakeholders to action or comprehend. items.title: Beyond waste valorization: Environmental justice in Brazil's Sertanejo Biodigester Program - Evidence from two municipalities and multi-level stakeholders
items.venue: Energy Sustainable Development/Energy for sustainable development
items.abstract: Circular bioenergy systems can improve waste management, energy access, and rural livelihoods, but their justice implications remain insufficiently examined. This study assesses the Sertanejo Biodigester Program as a circular rural-energy intervention, focusing on distributive, procedural, and recognitional justice and on the Transformative Innovation Policy (TIP) principles of directionality, inclusivity, and reflexivity. We use a qualitative case-study design that combines documentary analysis, 20 semi-structured stakeholder interviews, and five days of field observation in Mirandiba and Verdejante, Pernambuco. The evidence indicates perceived reductions in purchases of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and firewood, sanitation benefits, and productive use of digestate; these are reported or observed co-benefits rather than quantitatively estimated impacts. Participation is concentrated in installation and training, with limited evidence of upstream influence over technology design, beneficiary selection, or long-term governance. Evidence concerning women's participation suggests gendered exclusion from some decision-making spaces, while evidence on Indigenous and Quilombola inclusion is too limited for population-wide conclusions. The study contributes an operational qualitative framework that links Environmental Justice (EJ) dimensions to TIP governance criteria and shows that transformative potential depends on transparent allocation, participatory governance, recognition of local knowledge, and sustained post-installation support. Because field observations are confined to two municipalities, program-wide claims are made only where supported by broader documentary and institutional evidence.

items.abstract: Метою статті є теоретико-методологічне узагальнення генезису, систематизація провідних наукових шкіл і концептуалізація понятійно-категоріального апарату циркулярної економіки з акцентом на її підприємницький та інституційний виміри. Методологічний базис дослідження становить комплекс методів пізнання, а саме хронологічного та бібліометричного аналізу (для диференціації етапів розвитку циркулярної парадигми); порівняльного аналізу (для зіставлення фундаментальних наукових шкіл); семантичного контент-аналізу масиву дефініцій (для виявлення структурних диспропорцій у трактуванні циркулярності); методу сходження від абстрактного до конкретного (для формулювання авторського визначення). Здійснено періодизацію еволюції циркулярної економіки (1966–2026 рр.) із виокремленням чотирьох якісних фаз: філософсько-теоретичної, термінологічно-концептуальної, операціоналізаційної та системно-нормативної. Атрибутовано пріоритет фундаментального внеску Р. Фроша та Н. Галлопулоса (1989) у закладення засад промислової екології. Систематизовано концептуальні постулати семи провідних наукових шкіл, доведено наявність наукового консенсусу щодо неможливості реалізації циркулярної моделі в межах окремого ізольованого підприємства. Окреслено принципову дискусію між технологічним оптимізмом щодо абсолютного декаплінгу та критичною школою щодо ризиків «циркулярного відскоку». Запропоновано авторську полікомпонентну дефініцію циркулярної економіки, що розглядається як системна модель організації суспільного виробництва, розподілу, обміну та споживання, що базується на принципах превентивного усунення відходів за допомогою екодизайну, утримання продуктів, компонентів і матеріалів на найвищому рівні їхньої функціональної корисності та регенерації природного капіталу, формуючи специфічне інституційне підприємницьке середовище, у межах якого відкриті інновації, стратегічні партнерські мережі, платформна коопетиція та наскрізна цифровізація виступають системоутворювальними чинниками генерації еконо

items.title: Tactics of infrastructures in transitions: exploring the space between decarbonization strategies and operational practices in Dutch infrastructure organizations
items.abstract: Infrastructure systems are critical to advancing decarbonization goals, yet translating strategic ambitions into practice remains challenging. While prior research has explored high-level visions and operational experiments, the tactical level—where mid-level actors coordinate between strategy and operations—has received limited attention. This study investigates how tactical-level functions shape sustainability strategy implementation across three Dutch infrastructure providers: a national mobility agency, a regional drinking water utility, and a regional electricity distribution operator. Based on 34 semi-structured interviews and document review, it identifies four tactical functions: translating strategic goals into operational roles, processes, and requirements; taking advantage of emerging interdependencies and collaboration opportunities; trade-off navigating between conflicting priorities; and transferring lessons from operations back to strategy. These functions are shaped by sector-specific constraints and institutional contexts but reveal shared interdependencies, particularly in capacity planning. The findings underscore tactical actors’ crucial role in aligning sustainability ambitions with operational realities across interdependent infrastructure systems.

items.title: Designing Liminal Spaces for Upstream Performativity: Lessons From The Futures Lab
items.abstract: This paper examines how business schools can function as liminal socio‐material infrastructures for upstream performative experimentation. Recent work has advanced management scholarship to foreground the role of imagination in theorizing for desirable futures. However, less is understood about how alternatives might be made sufficiently tangible and credible to acquire performative force in the first place. This is compounded by performativity research that has largely examined how theories acquire effects once they circulate in markets and organizations. To address this, and drawing on a 5‐year qualitative case study of The Futures Lab (TFL), I show how shared visual workspaces, repeated critique, direct engagement with stakeholders, and the making and remaking of maps, models and prototypes enabled participants to (re)‐search alternative futures by making possibilities visible, contestable and open to revision. These practices produced credible fictions: tangible yet provisional representations to which external actors could attach, align with, and sometimes enrol around emerging possibilities. I develop prefigurative theorizing as a materially experimental mode of prospective theorizing, showing how desirable futures gain performative force not through imagination alone, but by being externalized, provisionally enacted, tested and revised in the present. The study thereby specifies conditions through which business schools can cultivate upstream performativity.

items.title: Kent ve Çevre Bilimlerinde Yeni Yaklaşımlar
items.abstract: Kentler; iklim değişikliğinin, kaynak baskısının, göç hareketlerinin, toplumsal eşitsizliklerin ve hızlı teknolojik dönüşümün en görünür hâle geldiği mekânlardır. Bu karmaşık tabloyu tek bir disiplinin araçlarıyla açıklamak giderek güçleşmekte; kent ve çevre bilimleri, mekânı, toplumu, teknolojiyi, siyaseti ve doğal sistemleri birlikte düşünmeyi gerektirmektedir. Elinizdeki kitap, bu ihtiyaçtan hareketle hazırlanmış dört bölümden oluşmaktadır. Kitap, Abidin Kemeç'in "Dijital Çağın Sürdürülebilir Kent Modelleri: Döngüsel Kent, Akıllı Eko Kent ve Veri Odaklı Kent" başlıklı bölümüyle kavramsal bir çerçeve sunarak açılmaktadır. Hasan Ege Söğüt'ün "Digital Infrastructure Ecosystems in Smart City Strategies: A Comparative Analysis of Konya Metropolitan Municipality and Bucharest Sector 5" başlıklı bölümü, dijital altyapı yatırımlarının kurumsal öğrenme kapasitesi ve çok aktörlü yönetişimle desteklenmedikçe dönüştürücü olmadığını göstermektedir. Özgür Bayraktar'ın "Kent Siyasetinde Süreklilik ve Değişim: Genel ve Yerel Seçimler Işığında Karaman'ın Siyasal Görünümü (1991–2024)" başlıklı bölümü, kentin siyasal zeminini seçim verileri üzerinden ele almaktadır. Son olarak Fatma Calayır, Sema Kaptanoğlu ve Ali Rıza Kul'un "The Interaction Between Global Fire Dynamics and Climate Change: Causes, Consequences, and Future Strategies" başlıklı bölümü, tartışmayı küresel ölçekte iklim krizi ve orman yangınları ilişkisine taşımaktadır. Bölümler birlikte okunduğunda ortak temalar belirginleşmektedir: Teknoloji tek başına yeterli değildir; kurumsal kapasite, katılım ve veri etiği gereklidir. Küresel normlarla yerel bağlam arasında süregelen bir gerilim vardır. Sürdürülebilirlik ise ancak sosyal adalet ve ölçekler arası iş birliğiyle mümkündür.

items.title: Creating interdependent relationships for circular strategies adoption in Brazilian manufacturing
items.abstract: To implement circular strategies, such as reduce, reuse, and remanufacture, manufacturers need access to non-virgin materials spread across the supply chain with different actors. To this end, the creation of interdependent relationships is needed. Literature lacks clarity on the rationale for establishing supply chain relationships to enable circular strategies. This study applies Resource Dependence Theory (RDT) to define and explain the establishment and management of interdependent relationships required for the adoption of circular strategies. By integrating RDT with the 10-R framework of circular strategies, this study delivers a theoretically grounded analysis of empirical insights from a case study of circular strategy adoption in Brazilian manufacturing. The findings explain how manufacturers shape interdependent relationships with diverse external actors around actions, outcomes and conditions necessary for circular strategies. Interdependence fosters both willingness and capacity for actors to engage, despite inherent complexities and challenges. Practitioners can use these findings to identify relevant actors and actions for specific circular strategies, and to inform the outcomes and conditions necessary to promote and enable exchange relationships. Future research should extend this study’s theoretical framework to explore circular strategy adoption in other settings, particularly developed markets where contextual boundaries will be distinct from Brazilian manufacturers.

items.title: Dijital Çağın Sürdürülebilir Kent Modelleri: Döngüsel Kent, Akıllı Eko Kent ve Veri Odaklı Kent
items.abstract: Kentsel nüfus sayısının ve yoğunluğunun artması aynı zamanda kentlerde üretim ve tüketim ilişkileri kaynaklı olarak, kentlerde ekonomik, çevresel ve sosyal bir dizi sorunların ortaya çıkmasına neden olmaktadır. Kentler zamanla kirliliğin, enerji tüketiminin, atıkların, kaynak tüketiminin, suçların, ekonomik krizlerin, sosyal eşitsizliklerin merkezi haline gelmiştir. Bu sorunlar kentlerin sürdürülebilir kent olma potansiyeline zarar vermektedir. Bir taraftan kentsel sorunlara çözüm üretmek diğer taraftan vatandaşların yaşam kalitesini artırmak için son yıllarda yeni kent modellerin ve stratejilerinin belirlenmesi ve uygulanması ihtiyacı ortaya çıkmıştır. Çalışmada örnek durum incelemesi yöntemi kullanılarak dijital çağda ortaya çıkan sürdürülebilir odaklı kent modellerinden olan döngüsel kent, akıllı eko kent ve veri odaklı kent modelleri ele alınmıştır. Döngüsel kent modellinde varlıkların yeniden kullanılması, daha az tüketim ve geri dönüşüm öne çıkarken akıllı eko kentte çevresel etkiyi azaltmak, yaşanabilir kentler ve sürdürülebilir topluluklar yaratmak için yeni nesil teknolojilerden yararlanılmaktadır. Veri odaklı kent modeli ise, sensörler, oyunlar, internet siteleri, uygulamalar, sosyal medya hesapları ve banka hesapları gibi kaynaklardan elde edilen verilerle çevresel, sosyal ve ekonomik faydalar sağlayan etkili hizmetler sunmak hedeflenmektedir.

items.title: Türkiye Yeşil Taksonomisi Yönetmeliğinde Döngüsel Ekonomi ve Sürdürülebilir Finansın Yeri ve Önemi
items.abstract: Türkiye Yeşil Taksonomisi Yönetmeliği (TYTY), çevresel sürdürülebilirliği ekonomik faaliyet düzeyinde tanımlayan ve sürdürülebilir yatırımlara finansman akışını desteklemeyi amaçlayan yeni bir düzenleyici altyapı kurmaktadır. Bu bölüm, Yönetmeliği özellikle döngüsel ekonomi ve sürdürülebilir finans arasındaki ilişki bakımından incelemektedir. Analiz, 24 Eylül 2026 tarihli TYTY Yönetmeliği ve Ek-1’in sistematiği esas alınarak; Avrupa Birliği Taksonomi Tüzüğü (ABTT) ve ilgili ikincil mevzuat ile güncel akademik literatür çerçevesinde geliştirilmiştir. Yönetmelikte döngüsel ekonomiye geçiş, altı çevresel hedeften biri olarak kabul edilmekte; Ek-1’de plastik ambalaj, elektrikli ve elektronik ekipman, atık toplama ve işleme, fosfor geri kazanımı, inşaat ve yenileme, onarım, yenileme, yeniden imalat, ikinci el faaliyetleri ve ürün-hizmet modelleri gibi kaynak değerini koruyan faaliyetler taksonomi kapsamına alınmaktadır. Sürdürülebilir finans boyutunda ise hasılat, yatırım harcamaları ve işletme giderlerine dayalı anahtar performans göstergeleri ile finansal kuruluşlara özgü raporlama mantığı, taksonomi verisini sermaye tahsisiyle ilişkilendirmektedir. Bölümde, Türkiye modelinin AB Taksonomi Tüzüğü’nün altı hedef, önemli ölçüde katkı, önemli zarar vermeme, asgari sosyal koruma ve teknik tarama kriterleri yaklaşımıyla güçlü yapısal benzerlik taşıdığı; buna karşılık faaliyet-özel teknik eşiklerin, doğrulama usullerinin, geçiş planı içeriğinin ve finansal kuruluşlara özgü ayrıntılı metodolojilerin henüz tamamlanmamış olması nedeniyle uygulama düzeyinde önemli belirsizliklerin sürdüğü sonucuna ulaşılmaktadır. Döngüsel ekonominin finansmanı bakımından temel mesele, taksonominin yalnızca geri dönüşümü değil; ürün ömrünün uzatılması, onarım, yeniden kullanım, yeniden imalat, ikincil hammadde kullanımı ve ürün-hizmet sistemleri gibi daha yüksek değer koruma stratejilerini ölçülebilir ve doğrulanabilir biçimde finansal karar süreçlerine aktarabilmesidir.

items.abstract: Hacia una Biocibernética Regenerativa propone un enfoque integral para la restauración de territorios vivos, especialmente en el contexto del Geoparque Imbabura. El libro plantea superar la sostenibilidad basada únicamente en “reducir el daño” y avanzar hacia un desarrollo regenerativo que aumente la capacidad de vida, resiliencia y autoorganización de los sistemas socioecológicos. La obra integra biosfera, sociosfera y tecnosfera, relacionando ecología, sociedad, tecnología, gobernanza, bioeconomía y restauración forestal. También aborda la biocibernética, la resiliencia, los ciclos adaptativos, el monitoreo mediante tecnologías y la aplicación de estos principios a especies forestales y proyectos biobasados.

items.title: A novel integrated objective-subjective weighting method using principal component analysis to correct overrepresentation of correlated criteria in sustainability decision-making
items.abstract: Indicators can be used as criteria in multicriteria decision-making. However, when indicators measure the same phenomenon, they exhibit correlations that can bias decision-making. Methods that consider correlations have limitations and are either objective or subjective. This paper proposes a new integrated objective-subjective weighting method that accounts for criterion correlations via principal component analysis. This method favours objective weights when criteria are correlated and subjective weights when they are uncorrelated. The method was validated through three comparative case studies and six sensitivity analyses, with a qualitative analysis of decision-relevant rank changes. Results show decision-relevant rank changes across all case studies, highlighting a correlated structure in decision-making in 11 of 13 MCDM models. 10 MCDM models report changes in the countries that constitute the top or bottom 5. 9 MCDM models report that most countries changed ranks, while 8 MCDM models report that countries have moved by more than 5 ranks. The sensitivity analysis highlights the method's contribution: it may enable more balanced decision-making. Pairwise comparisons allow for a more complete configuration that better captures the correlations among the criteria and their weights. The sensitivity analysis also identified limitations, including incomplete consideration of variance and computational complexity. Further research should apply principal component analysis to remove redundant criteria and validate the proposed method's decision quality.

items.title: Ecosystem governance for circularity
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The circular economy is a paradigmatic perspective that has captured the attention of management and strategy scholars. Yet, while a growing body of literature considers ecosystems in circular economy contexts, a coherent approach to governance remains missing. We adopt a strategic lens to understand how circularity can be facilitated through deliberate ecosystem governance, first identifying the three channels through which ecosystems contribute to circularity in industrial systems, and then differentiating ecosystems from other industry structures such as industrial supply chains and industry architectures. Building on the articles from the special issue, we propose an integrative framework of ecosystem governance for circularity, identifying four coupling mechanisms through which ecosystems shape material and energy flows, as well as coordination challenges and governance modes. We conclude with a discussion of future research directions.

items.title: Assessing the relative importance of factors influencing the development of industrial parks toward a circular economy in Vietnam: An analytic hierarchy process (AHP) approach
items.abstract: This paper assesses the relative importance of factors affecting the development of industrial parks (IPs) toward a circular economy in Vietnam. Most IPs still follow a largely linear model. The factors involved are mostly qualitative and hard to measure, with little direct statistical data, so the study uses the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). The hierarchy, built from a literature review, has three levels: the overall objective, seven factor groups, and 24 criteria. Each criterion has a definition and observable indicators. Six experts from four fields (IP management, state management, circular economy and environment, and research), each with at least five years of experience, made pairwise comparisons on Saaty’s 1–9 scale, providing 306 judgments. The judgments were aggregated by the geometric mean, and weights were derived with the row geometric mean method. All 48 expert-level and 8 aggregated matrices met the consistency requirement, with a consistency ratio (CR) of 1.4% for the factor-group matrix and 0.0% to 2.1% for the criterion matrices. The three groups with the highest weights were environmental factors (0.2537), industrial symbiosis (0.2346), and policy and institutions (0.1512), together accounting for about 64% of the total weight. They were followed by technology and infrastructure (0.1349) and economic and financial factors (0.1148). The two lowest were social and human resources (0.0743) and natural conditions and location (0.0365). By global weight, the highest-ranked of the 24 criteria were enhancing recycling, reuse, and renewable energy adoption (0.0943) and protecting and efficiently using natural resources (0.0938), followed by sharing by-products, waste, and energy (0.0784) and industrial symbiosis network development (0.0721). Topographical and geological conditions ranked lowest (0.0040). items.title: Transitioning to Circular Automotive Systems: A Systematic Review of Supply Chain Practices and Implementation
items.venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
items.abstract: The Automobile industry shifts from linear to circular economy for sustainability on a global level with respect to the industrial revolution 5.0, but it faces challenges when establishing circular economy.Circular supply chain implementation is dependent on multiple barriers and enablers, including economic managerial, technological, regulatory and social domains, making it ineffective for single factor solution.The purpose behind this review is to conduct a systematic literature review to develop an understanding how these interconnected barriers and enablers can together shape the circular supply chain implementation and their performance, specifically inside the automotive sector which is still remain a little known.By applying the PRISMA framework on 150 peer reviewed articles, research papers.The research shows that literature focuses on primarily on electric vehicle barriers within developing economies.Circular supply chain implementation is governed not only by isolated barriers but by complex systematic interdependencies between enablers as well.This interdependencies are of enablers and barriers can be further classified into economical and financial, managerial and organizational, technological and infrastructure, policy and regularity and market and social.The study shows two systematic patterns, driving the transition technology-policy interdependence and conflicting relationship between large scale production and value extraction.The findings also presented a research agenda focusing on strategic value creation through material streams of automotive electronics, plastics and composites with high potential value and further insights are needed.Circular supply chain as a strategic approach for securing critical material supplies, while policymakers could leverage the use of digital tools as the foundational infrastructure for subsidies allocation and prevent the fraud.

items.title: Inter-Organisational Systems for Circular Value Chains: A Simulation of Digital Product Passport Adoption
items.abstract: Circular value chains rely on effective information sharing to recover materials from waste, reducing dependence on virgin resources and improving industrial sustainability. To support circular value chains, the EU has introduced the Digital Product Passport, an inter-organisational information system for disclosing product information. The effect of the DPP on the sustainability of circular value chains has not been explored, and extant literature focuses only on its technical design. Drawing on organisational information processing theory, we model the DPP characteristics as capabilities that address different information needs in each phase of a circular value chain for the recovery of photovoltaic waste, and simulate 500 random adoption scenarios. The findings indicate that the DPP increases the amount of material processed and improves environmental and social sustainability, while costs grow faster than revenues and the additional material is not matched by proportional downstream processing. These dynamics reveal tensions and trade-offs in both implementation and policy decisions regarding DPP adoption.

items.title: Material Flow Analysis of Domestic Water Consumption in Jos Metropolitan Area, Nigeria
items.venue: International journal of research and scientific innovation
items.abstract: Rapid urbanization and population growth are placing increasing pressure on domestic water systems in many African cities, particularly where the expansion of infrastructure has not kept pace with development. This study employed Material Flow Analysis (MFA) to quantify domestic water flows and to examine their implications for sustainable urban planning in the Jos Metropolitan Area, Nigeria. A cross-sectional survey of 400 households across 17 districts provided data on water sources, supply conditions, consumption, losses, and wastewater disposal. Field observations and secondary information served to complement the household survey. Metropolitan water flows were estimated by means of population-based scaling, employing a projected 2025 population of 1,357,142. At a gross domestic water input of 44.6 litres per capita per day, the estimated metropolitan input was 60.529 million litres per day (MLD). The application of the study's adopted 20% distribution-loss parameter yielded an estimated loss of 12.106 MLD, leaving 48.423 MLD, equivalent to 35.68 litres per capita per day, as net delivered water. Only 35% of surveyed households identified municipal or public supply as their principal water source, whereas 65% depended mainly on wells, boreholes, rivers, vendors, and rainwater. Cooking, drinking, and gardening constituted the predominant household uses. The findings reveal a fragmented and predominantly linear urban water metabolism, which is characterised by distribution losses, dependence on household self-provisioning, and limited opportunities for water recovery. The study recommends the rehabilitation of distribution networks, water auditing, the expansion of municipal coverage, improved metering, rainwater harvesting, water reuse, and stronger integration of water infrastructure with spatial planning.

items.title: The Circular Economy—A New Resilience Paradigm?
items.abstract: The circular economy (CE) has traditionally been positioned as a central instrument of the sustainability paradigm. Yet escalating geopolitical volatility and supply chain fragility have elevated resilience to a parallel strategic imperative, and the conceptual integration of CE and resilience remains underexplored. This article bridges this gap by reconceptualizing CE as a foundational instrument for (systemic) resilience. We advance eight theoretically grounded propositions specifying how core CE strategies (i.e., narrowing, slowing, and closing loops) can foster resilience across three nested levels: macro (socioeconomic systems), meso (territorial ecosystems and supply chains), and micro (organizations and products). A nested‐level proposition specifies the coupling between these levels and shows that cross‐level cascades may be reinforcing or countervailing. We argue that CE's future value lies in securing long‐term system continuity under exogenous shocks. By positioning CE as an instrument through which a resilience paradigm can be operationalized alongside sustainability, i.e., a paradigmatic evolution rather than a replacement, we offer a theoretical trajectory and research agenda for scholars, practitioners, and policymakers navigating an increasingly volatile global context.

items.abstract: The article substantiates the theoretical and applied principles of circular reconstruction of territorial communities of Ukraine in the conditions of large-scale war destruction, significant needs for infrastructure restoration and the need to transition from a linear resource model to the principles of a circular economy. The purpose of the study is to systematize verified practices of circular reconstruction in Ukraine, identify management lessons based on them and form practical tools suitable for direct use by local governments. The emphasis is on the need to transform destruction waste from a problematic component of post-war reconstruction into a resource for reuse, production of building materials and formation of local closed resource cycles. Five verified Ukrainian practices of circular reconstruction for 2022–2026 are systematized: recycling of destroyed building waste in Hostomel with the participation of Neo-Eco; GreenMix pilot project for recycling construction waste in the Kyiv region; resource-efficient restoration of the water supply system of Mykolaiv; implementation of a mechanical-biological complex for processing solid household waste in Lviv; formation of an intermunicipal platform for processing demolition waste in the Mykolaiv region. It has been established that the effectiveness of circular reconstruction depends not only on the amount of funding and availability of technologies, but also on the institutional capacity of territorial communities, the quality of project management, intermunicipal interaction, involvement of local business and the ability to ensure technology transfer. Based on the generalization of practical experience, a matrix for selecting circular instruments was developed based on the ratio of the expected effect and the complexity of implementation. items.title: A Planning and Decision-Making Tool for Circular Construction and Demolition Projects in Cities
items.abstract: Circular economy in the built environment is gaining attention due to its significant contribution to waste generation, resource depletion, and greenhouse gas emissions. Growing cities worldwide are the central reason for the increase of construction and demolition activities, presenting an important scope for sustainability transition when considering the transformation of urban areas. This article aims to address local government’s role in circular urban transformation projects with a comprehensive understanding of who, when, and how to implement circular practices in spatial planning, demolition, and construction activities. The study was conducted based on a collaborative process with two Danish municipalities involved in two urban transformation projects that designed, tested, and evaluated a planning and decision-making tool. First, a literature review was conducted to conceptualise planning and decision-making, followed by a series of workshops to identify phases, stakeholder involvement, and milestones in the case projects. Ad hoc meetings were held to monitor progress and reflect on decisions during the case projects, and afterwards document analysis and evaluation workshops were performed to assess implementation. The tool consists of (a) the key phases and circular economy practices in urban transformation projects, and (b) the main elements influencing planning and decision-making for those projects, encompassing a tangible framework to assist cities in implementing circular principles in complex and diverse urban transformation projects. The article concludes with the essential role of early identification of risks and potential and pinpoints the importance of transparent stakeholder collaboration and information management.

items.title: Planning for circular urban metabolism: Intertwining skills and spatial transformation for manufacturing transition in Padua and Venice, Italy
items.abstract: The shift from a linear to a circular economic structure needs a new urban metabolism that minimizes waste and the use of raw materials and energy. However, a city’s potential for circularity is contingent upon its manufacturing path-dependency, both from an economic and spatial perspective. The research looks at two Italian industrial areas—Padua and Venice—and proceeds to investigate the recent dynamics of their manufacturing spatial distribution at the “transect” level scale. Using a mixed-method approach that combines morphological-spatial analysis, urban planning assessment, and quantitative labor and waste data, the study investigates how manufacturing industries contribute to circular transitions and how planning policies can support or hinder this process. Findings show that technological manufacturing, supported by technical skills and green jobs, drives circular performance through waste prevention and recycling. Industrial diversification and firm relatedness further enable symbiotic material flows. However, both cities reveal a persistent misalignment between emerging circular dynamics and existing zoning frameworks. While Padua has begun adopting mixed-use zoning, planning strategies in both areas remain fragmented and reactive. The paper calls for more integrated, circularity-oriented spatial planning that mobilizes skills and proximity as key territorial resources.

items.title: Governing urban circular economy transitions: A mechanism-informed heuristic for local government
items.abstract: Despite the recognised role of the urban circular economy as a pathway to sustainable development within global planetary boundaries, governance of circular economy transitions by local government remains poorly operationalised. Existing sustainability transition frameworks provide theoretical perspectives but are insufficiently place-based, underspecify the role of actors and agency and have not been integrated into a coherent governance process for local government. Drawing on 65 semi-structured interviews with actors across government, business and knowledge providers, complemented by policy document analysis, we compare three local governments in each of metropolitan Amsterdam (The Netherlands) and metropolitan Melbourne (Australia) to contrast the respective stages of implementation maturity. Following a retrodictive analytical logic, we develop three candidate explanatory mechanisms for circular economy governance: (i) a ‘legitimation’ mechanism, whereby multilevel policy alignment reduces institutional risk within the circular ecosystem; (ii) a ‘boundary-spanning’ mechanism through which local government officers bridge between entrepreneurial and public-governance institutional logics and (iii) a ‘competitive-displacement mechanism’ whereby cooperative actor relationships shift toward competition as circular economy solutions mature toward mainstream adoption. Grounded in these mechanisms, we propose a three-step heuristic model, comprising (1) contextual ecosystem analysis, (2) intervention strategy development and (3) transition management. We introduce a circular ecosystem framework for place-specific actor mapping to operationalise the process. We present the mechanisms as a bounded middle-range explanation and the model as context-sensitive guidance, rather than as a deterministic or universally predictive account.
